He, Glorified, made colours and tongues differ, so that you scarcely hear two utterances agreeing in one timbre or one loudness, and scarcely see two forms alike in every respect in colours, features and lineaments, for the sake of mutual recognition; otherwise, were they of one skin, one colour, and one set of proportions and outlines, confusion and ambiguity would occur, and we would not lack means of distinguishing among them all; even twins, despite the agreement of their materials and causes and the things that meet them in their creation, differ in some respect inevitably, however close they are in aspects of resemblance.

dervis-irab:23-26.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمِنْ آياتِهِ مَنامُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ وَابْتِغاؤُكُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; من آياته is a fronted khabar (predicate) and منامكم a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); بالليل is attached to منامكم; ابتغاؤكم is conjoined to منامكم, and من فضله is attached to ابتغاؤكم.
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَسْمَعُونَ) إنّ is a particle resembling the verb, and في ذلك is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and آيات is its delayed ism; لقوم is an adjective of آيات and the clause يسمعون is an adjective of قوم. (وَمِنْ آياتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً) من آياته is a fronted khabar and يريكم is a delayed mubtadaʾ, in that it is an imperfect verb interpreted, together with the omitted maṣdariyya أن, as a maṣdar; the original is "أن يريكم", and more of this important topic will come in the chapter on benefits. يريكم is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent pronoun referring to Allah, the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and البرق is the second mafʿūl bihi; خوفا وطمعا are accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). This i'rab has been objected to on the ground that the mafʿūl lahu must be an act of the agent of the verb being explained, and fear and hope are not so. The answer to this objection comes from two directions: either the two objects are agents in meaning, because they are seers, as if it were said "He makes you see the lightning out of fear and hope"; or the second, that it is on the supposition of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "a showing of fear and a showing of hope", the muḍāf being omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. It is also permissible that they are two ḥāls (circumstantials), i.e. "fearing and hoping"; more of this discussion will come in the chapter on benefits.
(وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَيُحْيِي بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها) وينزل is conjoined to يريكم; من السماء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينزل; ماء is mafʿūl bihi; فيحيي is conjoined to ينزل; به is attached to يحيي, الأرض is mafʿūl bihi, and the adverb بعد موتها is attached to an omitted word, a ḥāl. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ) Its i'rab has already preceded. (وَمِنْ آياتِهِ أَنْ تَقُومَ السَّماءُ وَالْأَرْضُ بِأَمْرِهِ) Conjoined to what preceded. (ثُمَّ إِذا دَعاكُمْ دَعْوَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ إِذا أَنْتُمْ تَخْرُجُونَ) ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; إذا is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of condition, and the clause دعاكم is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; دعاكم is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; دعوة is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and من الأرض is attached to دعاكم (one says "I called him from the bottom of the valley and he came up to me"); إذا is the sudden إذا, which takes the place of the fāʾ in the apodosis; أنتم is mubtadaʾ and the clause تخرجون is the khabar. (وَلَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ كُلٌّ لَهُ قانِتُونَ) له is a fronted khabar and من a delayed mubtadaʾ; في السموات والأرض is the ṣila (relative clause); كل is mubtadaʾ, له is attached to قانتون, and قانتون is the khabar of كل, i.e. obedient with the obedience of submission.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying, Exalted, "ومن آياته منامكم بالليل والنهار وابتغاؤكم من فضله" there is the art of luff (al-laff), the discussion of which has often preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is of the chapter of al-laff, and its arrangement is: 'And among His signs is your sleep and your seeking of His bounty, by night and by day.' Except that He separated the first two counterparts from the other two, because the latter are two times, and time and what occurs in it are as one thing, with the aid of al-laff to unity. It is also possible that what is meant is: your sleep in both times and your seeking in both; but the apparent one is the first, because of its recurrence in the Qur'an; and the strongest meanings are those the Qur'an indicates, which they hear with retentive ears." I say: what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is problematic from the standpoint of the grammatical craft, because if the meaning is what he mentioned, النهار would be governed by ابتغاؤكم while it precedes it and it is a maṣdar, and that is not permissible; and further, it would require conjunction upon the objects of two different governors, so the construction is not admissible.
Ibn Hishām denounced al-Zamakhsharī's statement, saying: "Al-Zamakhsharī's statement 'ومن آياته منامكم بالليل والنهار وابتغاؤكم من فضله' that it is of al-laff wa-l-nashr and that the meaning is 'your sleep and your seeking of His bounty, by night and by day' requires النهار to be governed by الابتغاء despite its being fronted before it and conjoined to the object of منامكم, which is بالليل; this is not permissible in poetry, so how in the most eloquent speech?"
I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not intend the governing that Ibn Hishām said; rather his intention is that the night is connected in meaning with sleep and the day is connected in meaning with seeking, and بالليل is a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "and that is occurring by night and by day", and the sentence is parenthetical and ought to be delayed.

* Benefits:
1- The condition of identity of agent in the mafʿūl li-ajlihi:
We pointed in the i'rab to the objection directed at the i'rab of خوفا وطمعا as mafʿūl lahu, and the reply to the objection. The condition of identity of agent was stated by the later grammarians, and Ibn Kharūf differed from them, allowing the accusative with a different agent, arguing from this verse, saying that the agent of the showing is Allah, the Exalted, while the agent of fear and hope is those addressed. Ibn Mālik answered him in Sharḥ al-Tashīl, saying: "The meaning of يريكم is 'He makes you see', so the agent of the seeing, on this basis, is the agent of the fear and hope."
Among the examples of omitting أن and treating the verb as the equivalent of the maṣdar is the well-known proverb "تسمع بالمعيدي خير من أن تراه" (That you hear of al-Muʿaydī is better than that you see him). This proverb is applied to one whose report is better than his appearance. The first to say it was al-Mundhir ibn Māʾ al-Samāʾ, who used to hear of Mashaqqa ibn Khamra al-Muʿaydī and liked what reached him about him; when he saw him, he being ugly to look at, he said this proverb. So خير is the khabar of the maṣdar formed from the implied أن in تسمع, i.e. "your hearing". Of it is the saying of Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd:
ألا أيهذا الزاجري أحضر الوغى ... وأن أشهد اللّذات هل أنت مخلدي
(O you who rebuke me, that I attend the battle and that I take part in pleasures—are you going to make me immortal?)
It has been transmitted أحضر with accusative and with nominative; the accusative is justified by an implied أن, and "وأن أشهد" supports it. And the saying of another:
وقالوا: ما تشاء؟ فقلت ألهو ... إلى الإصباح آثر ذي أثير
(They said: "What do you wish?" I said: "To amuse myself until morning, first of all.")
This verse is by ʿUrwa ibn al-Ward al-ʿAbsī, from a set of verses, among them:
أرقت وصحبتي بمضيق عمق ... لبرق من تهامة مستطير
سقوني الخمر ثم تكنفوني ... عداة الله من كذب وزور وقالوا ما تشاء البيت..
(I lay sleepless, with my companions at the narrow pass of ʿAmq, because of lightning from Tihāma spreading far. They gave me wine to drink, then surrounded me—enemies of Allah, because of lies and falsehood—and said: "What do you wish?" ... the verse.)
وأرقت: I stayed awake, and the wāw is for accompaniment; المضيق is the narrow place; عمق, with kasra then sukūn, is a tree in the land of the Ḥijāz, and with ḍamma then fatḥa is a low place near Makka, and perhaps it has sukūn here for the metre. البرق is attached to أرقت, i.e. "I stayed awake in this place on account of lightning from Tihāma, the direction of my beloved"; it is possible that the wāw is circumstantial and حجتي is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is بمضيق عمق, and if his companions are in it, then he is in it, so it returns to the first. مستطير: spreading. تكنفوني: they surrounded me. عداة is the plural of عاد meaning "enemy", and it is said to be the plural of عدو, i.e. they are enemies of Allah because of their lies and falsehood, and it is a parenthetical clause; it is possible that عداة is a substitute (badal) for the fāʿil pronoun, i.e. "they surrounded me and said: What do you want? I said: ألهو", i.e. "it is that I amuse myself", so أن is implied in meaning, and the verb is not made accusative in form. Al-Jawharī said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "One says 'افعل هذا آثر ذي أثير', i.e. before everything," pointing out that آثر is accusative as a figurative adverb or as a ḥāl, i.e. "do it as the first of everything that is preferred", so it is an elative (afʿal tafḍīl) with the meaning of a passive participle. [Translator's note: the source's discussion of this verse is condensed and partly obscure; translated as written.]
2- The i'rab scholars went deep into the analysis of this verse, and Abū al-Baqāʾ summarised all their views in three, which we give below in the text of his words:
"'ومن آياته يريكم البرق': it has three aspects. The first, that من آياته is a ḥāl of البرق, i.e. 'He shows you the lightning being among His signs'; but the proper place of the wāw is to enter upon the verb here; since the verb was fronted and it belongs to the conjoined clause, the wāw was given priority, and it is made good by the preposition and its genitive noun being in the ruling of an adverb, like His saying: 'آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة'. The second aspect, that أن is omitted, i.e. 'and among His signs is that He shows you'; and when أن is omitted in a case like this, the verb may be in the nominative. The third, that the described is omitted, i.e. 'and among His signs is a sign in which He shows you the lightning', the described and the returning pronoun being omitted; it is also permissible that the implied form be: 'and among His signs is a thing' or 'a cloud', and the fāʿil be the pronoun of the omitted 'thing'." The second aspect is the one we have chosen; it is the apparent one, the farthest from affectation, and agrees with its sisters in which the maṣdar particle is mentioned.

dervis-irab:27-29.t:
* I'rab:
(وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; هو is mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي is khabar (predicate), and the clause يبدأ الخلق is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي. الخلق is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), but the pronoun in يعيده is returned to it in the sense of "the created thing", so it is an istikhdām (employment); the discussion of this lofty art will come in the chapter on rhetoric. [Translator's note: the source reads "ولكنه إعادة الضمير في يعيده عليه", which is evidently garbled; translated according to its evident sense.] وهو: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction, هو is mubtadaʾ and أهون is its khabar, and عليه is attached to أهون. The secret of the masculine form of the pronoun in His saying وهو, although what is meant by it is the re-creation (al-iʿāda), will come, as will the meaning of "easier for Him" and the secret of delaying the preposition and its genitive noun, namely عليه. (وَلَهُ الْمَثَلُ الْأَعْلى فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; له is a fronted khabar and المثل a delayed mubtadaʾ, and الأعلى is an adjective (naʿt); في السموات is a ḥāl (circumstantial) and الأرض is conjoined to السموات; هو is mubtadaʾ, العزيز the first khabar and الحكيم the second khabar.
(ضَرَبَ لَكُمْ مَثَلًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ) ضرب is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", and the meaning of ضرب here is جعل (made); لكم is in the position of accusative as the second object, and مثلا is the first object; من أنفسكم is an adjective of مثلا, i.e. "being from yourselves", so من has the meaning of beginning, as though He said: "He took a likeness and drew it from the nearest thing to you."
(هَلْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ مِنْ شُرَكاءَ فِي ما رَزَقْناكُمْ) هل is a particle of interrogation; لكم is a fronted khabar; مما is a ḥāl from شركاء, because originally it is an adjective of an indefinite noun and was fronted before it; the clause ملكت is the ṣila; أيمانكم is the fāʿil of ملكت; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and شركاء is a delayed mubtadaʾ; فيما رزقناكم is attached to شركاء. The ما in مما ملكت has the meaning of "kind", and the implied form is: "Are there partners in what We have provided you, being of the kind that your right hands possess, established for you?" So "being" (كائنون) is the description to which مما ملكت is attached, and when it was fronted it became a ḥāl, and "established" (مستقرون) is the khabar to which لكم is attached.
(فَأَنْتُمْ فِيهِ سَواءٌ تَخافُونَهُمْ كَخِيفَتِكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ كَذلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ) The fāʾ occurs in the answer to the question; أنتم is mubtadaʾ, فيه is attached to سواء, and سواء is the khabar; the clause تخافونهم is a second khabar of أنتم or is in the position of ḥāl from the fāʿil pronoun in سواء, i.e. "so you become equal, each of you fearing the other regarding his sharing with him in property" [Translator's note: the source reads "فتساووا خائنا بعضكم من بعض", which appears garbled; translated according to its evident sense]. وكخيفتكم is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a fear like your fear", the maṣdar being annexed to its fāʿil, and أنفسكم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar; وكذلك is also an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; نفصل الآيات is an imperfect verb with a latent fāʿil, its implied form being "نحن", and الآيات is mafʿūl bihi; لقوم is attached to نفصل, and the clause يعقلون is an adjective of قوم.
(بَلِ اتَّبَعَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ) بل is a particle of turning away and conjunction; اتبع is conjoined by way of iltifāt (shift of address); الذين is the fāʿil of اتبع and the clause ظلموا is the ṣila of الذين; أهواءهم is mafʿūl bihi and بغير علم is a ḥāl. (فَمَنْ يَهْدِي مَنْ أَضَلَّ اللَّهُ وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (eloquent fāʾ); من is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the clause يهدي is the khabar; من is the mafʿūl of يهدي, and the clause أضل الله is the ṣila, the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "أضله الله"; the wāw is a conjunction, ما is negative, لهم is a fronted khabar, من is a redundant preposition, and ناصرين is genitive in form and a delayed mubtadaʾ in position; it is permissible to take ما as Ḥijāzī (like laysa) according to those who allow fronting its khabar before its ism.

* Rhetoric:
1- The art of istikhdām (employment):
In His saying "وهو الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده" there is the art of istikhdām as we established in the i'rab. It is a subtle art with an obscure path, and there are two views on it. The first is that the speaker brings a word shared between two meanings by original sharing, placed between two contextual indications, or preceding both or following both, employing each indication for one of the two meanings of that shared word. This is the view of Ibn Mālik, whether the employment is by a pronoun or without a pronoun. Allah the Exalted said: "لكل أجل كتاب يمحو الله ما يشاء ويثبت", for the word كتاب admits the decreed term and the written book, and it is placed between the words أجل and يمحو; it employs one of its two senses, namely the term, by the indication of mentioning الأجل, and employs the other sense, namely the written thing, by the indication of يمحو.
The second view is that it is the use of a word shared between two meanings unrestrictedly, so that he intends by that word one of the two meanings, then returns to it a pronoun by which he intends the other meaning, or returns two pronouns to it, intending by one of them one meaning and by the other the other meaning, after having used it in its (first) meaning [Translator's note: the source writes "بعد استعماله في معناه الثالث" (in its third meaning), which seems an error]. This is the well-known position in istikhdām and is the way of the author of al-Īḍāḥ and those who followed him. Of it is the verse we are discussing: He returned the pronoun, His saying "وهو أهون عليه", to الخلق in its other sense, namely "the created thing", not its first sense, namely the maṣdar. Of it is the saying of al-Buḥturī:
فسقى الغضا والساكنيه وان هم ... شبوه بين جوانحي وضلوعي
(So may He water the ghaḍā and its dwellers, even though they kindled it between my ribs and my flanks.)
He returned the pronoun of شبوه to الغضا in its other sense, namely the tree whose fire is strong and by which a proverb is struck, as one says "embers of the ghaḍā", although he intends a specific place where his beloved resides.
2- In this verse there is also the art of al-madhhab al-kalāmī (the scholastic-theological method). It is said that the first to invent it was al-Jāḥiẓ, who claimed that nothing of it is found in the noble Qur'an, whereas it is full of it. Its definition is that the speaker argues for what he wishes to establish with a proof that silences the one who opposes him, in the way of the masters of kalām; of it is a logical kind in which sound conclusions are drawn from true premises. Al-Rummānī presented, in his work on the inimitability entitled al-Nukat and in his commentary al-Jāmiʿ al-kabīr, in the fifth category of the chapter on hyperbole in the iʿjāz: bringing speech out in the form of doubt, for the sake of hyperbole in fairness, for argument.
3- The secret of the masculine form of the pronoun:
The masculine form of the pronoun in His saying "وهو أهون", although it refers to the re-creation (al-iʿāda), is in consideration of its being a returning and restoring, or in consideration of the khabar, أهون. Al-Karkhī said:
"The pronoun is made masculine in it although it refers to al-iʿāda, taken from the word يعيده, with regard to the meaning not the form, namely 'its returning' or 'its restoring', as it was regarded in His saying: 'لنحيي به بلدة ميتا', i.e. a dead place; or its being masculine is in consideration of the khabar."
4- The delaying of the preposition and its genitive noun, namely "عليه", although it is fronted in His saying:
"هو عليّ هين" (it is easy for Me), because what is intended here is the opposite of what is intended there, for there it is Allah's being singled out in power for bringing forth the aged and the barren [Translator's note: the source writes "الهم" (grief); the intended word is evidently "الهرم" (the aged)]. As for the intention here, there is no meaning of singling out in it; how could there be, when the matter is built on what they believe from observation, that repetition is easier than initiation? Had the preposition been fronted, the meaning would have changed. This is a well-known question, familiar among them: how could He, Exalted, say "وهو أهون عليه" when all acts, in relation to His power, Exalted, are equal in ease? Its clarification is that the matter is built on what is inferred by analogy from your own principles and required by your reasoning, that repeating a thing is easier than originating it, because whoever among you repeats the making of something finds it easier and lighter than producing it; so re-creation is judged to be greater in ease. There is another answer, which is that أهون is not for comparison but is an adjective with the meaning of هين (easy), as in their saying "الله أكبر", i.e. "great".

farraa:2-3.t:
His saying: ﴿غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ﴾: The readers agree on ﴿غُلِبَت﴾, except Ibn ʿUmar, who read it (غَلَبَتِ الرُّومُ) ("the Romans have conquered"). It was said to him: over what [143] did they prevail? He said: over the nearest countryside of Syria. The exegesis rejects the view of Ibn ʿUmar. That is because Persia triumphed over the Romans, and the Muslims were saddened by that, while the idolaters of Mecca rejoiced, because the Persians worshipped idols and had no scripture, so the idolaters loved them for that; and the Muslims inclined towards the Romans because they were people of scripture and prophethood. The evidence for that is the saying of Allah: ﴿وَهُم مِّن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ﴾, and then He said after that: and on the day they prevail the believers will rejoice, when they prevail. And all of that came to pass.
His saying: ﴿مِّن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ﴾: the speech of the Arabs is ghalabtuhu ghalabatan; when they annex it they drop the hāʾ [i.e. the tāʾ marbūṭa], as they dropped it in His saying ﴿وإقام الصَّلاةِ﴾, while the [usual] speech is iqāmat al-ṣalāt.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿لِلَّهِ ٱلأَمْرُ مِن قَبْلُ وَمِن بَعْدُ﴾: The reading is with the nominative [ḍamma] without tanwīn, because in meaning both are intended to be annexed to something, inevitably. When they conveyed the meaning of what they are annexed to, they marked them with the nominative while they are [in position] genitive, so that the nominative would be an indication of what has been dropped of that to which you annexed them. The same applies to what resembles them, as in the poet's saying:
* إن تأتِ من تحتُ أجِئْها من عَلُ *
(If you come at it from below, I will come at it from above.)
And similar is the poet's saying:
إذا أنا لم أُومَن عَليكِ ولم يَكُن * لقاؤكِ إلاَّ من ورَاءُ ورَاءُ
(If I am not trusted with you, and meeting you is only from behind, behind…)
You put it in the nominative when you make it a ghāya (an "end-word", whose annexed complement is cut off) and do not mention after it what you annexed it to. If you intend to make it overt, or you do make it overt, you say: "lillāhi al-amru min qabli wa-min baʿdi", as though you had made overt the genitive to which you attached (قَبْل) and (بعد). Al-Kisāʾī heard one of Banū Asad read it (لِلَّهِ ٱلأَمْرُ مِن قَبْلِ وَمِن بَعْدُ), putting (قبل) in the genitive and (بَعد) in the nominative, according to what he intended. And he — meaning al-Kisāʾī — recited to me:
أكابِدهَا حَتى أُعَرِّسَ بَعْد مَا * يكون سُحُيْراً أو بُعَيدَ فأهْجَعَا
(I struggle with it until I halt to rest after it is just before dawn, or a little after, and then I sleep.)
He meant "a little after dawn" (buʿayda al-saḥar) and left it implied. Had he not intended the implied annexation, he would have used the nominative and said buʿaydu. Similar is the poet's saying:
لَعَمْركَ ما أدرى وإنى لأَوجَلُ * على أيِّنا تَعْدو المنيَّةُ أوّلُ
(By your life, I do not know — and I am afraid — on which of us death will fall first.)
You put (أوّل) in the nominative because it is a ghāya; do you not see that it is attached to something of which it is the first? Just as you know that (قبل) can only be before something, and that (بعد) is likewise. And had you set them free in Arabic and given them tanwīn while they carry the meaning of annexation — putting them in the genitive [with tanwīn] in the genitive, and with tanwīn in the accusative and nominative — it would be correct; that has been heard from the Arabs and has come in their poetry. One of them said:
وساغَ لى الشرابُ وكنت قبلاً * أكاد أغَصُّ بالمَاء الحمِيم
(Drink became pleasant to me, while before I nearly choked on warm water.)
He used tanwīn. Likewise you say: "I came to you before (min qablin) and saw you." Likewise his saying:
مِكَرٍّ مِفَرٍّ مقبل مُدبرٍ معاً * كجُلمودِ صخرٍ حطّه السيلُ من عَلِ
(Wheeling, fleeing, advancing, retreating all at once, like a boulder the torrent has sent down from on high.)
This is genitive; if you wish you may use tanwīn, and if you wish you may not use tanwīn, according to your intention. Another said, in the nominative:
كَأنّ مِحَطّا فى يدَى حارثيَّةٍ * صَنَاعٍ علت منّى به الجِلدَ من عَلُ
(As though a tattooing needle in the hands of a skilful woman of Banū al-Ḥārith had gone over my skin with it from above.)
Al-miḥaṭṭ is a needle with which she tattoos her hand.
As for the saying of the other:
هتكت به بيوتَ بنى طَرِيفٍ * على ما كان قبلٌ من عِتاب
(With it I tore open the tents of Banū Ṭarīf, for the reproach there had been before.)
where he used tanwīn and the nominative, that is due to poetic necessity, just as the poet is forced to use tanwīn in the single vocative and says "yā Zaydun, come forward!" He said:
قدَّمُوا إذْ قيل قيسٌ قدِّمُوا * وارفعُوا المجدَ بأطرافِ الأَسَل
(They advanced when it was said: "Qays, advance! and raise glory on the tips of the spears.")
And one of Banū ʿUqayl recited to me:
ونحن قتلنا الأَسْدَ أَسْدَ شَنُوءَة * فما شرِبُوا بعدٌ عَلَى لذَّة خمرَا
(We killed al-Asd, the Asd of Shanūʾa, and after that they never drank wine with pleasure.)
Had he turned it back to the accusative when he used tanwīn, that would be a valid way, as he said:
وسَاغ لى الشراب وكنت قبلاً * أكاد أغَصَّ بالمََـَاء الحَمِيم
(Drink became pleasant to me, while before I nearly choked on warm water.)
Likewise in the vocative: had the accusative been restored when tanwīn is used in it, that would be a valid way, as he said:
فطِر خالداً إن كنتَ تَسْطيع طَيْرةً * وَلا تَقَعْن إلاَّ وقلبُـكَ حَاذِِر
(Fly, Khālid, if you can manage a flight, and do not land except with your heart on its guard.)
And do not reject annexing qabl, baʿd and the like even when [the second element] is not overt, for he said:
إِلاَّ بُدَاهةَ أو عُلاَلَة * سَابحٍ نَهْدِ الجُزَاره
(Except the first burst or the second run of a swift-galloping horse with stout limbs.)
And another said:
يامن يرى عَرِضاً أكفكفُهُ * بين ذِرَاعىْ وجَبْهةِ الأَسَدِ
(O who sees a cloud I keep watching, between the Forearms and the Forehead of the Lion [constellation]?)
I heard Abū Tharwān al-ʿUklī say: "May Allah this morning cut off the hand and foot of whoever said it" (yada wa-rijla man qālahu). This is permissible only with two things that accompany each other, like the hand and the foot, and like saying "I have half or a quarter of a dirham" and "I came to you before or after the afternoon prayer". It is not permissible with two things that are far apart, like the house and the slave-boy: do not allow "I bought the house or the slave-boy of Zayd"; but [you may say] "the slave or the slave-woman of Zayd", "an eye or an ear", "a hand or a foot", and the like.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ ظَاهِراً مِّنَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾ means the people of Mecca. He says: they know trade and livelihood, and He made that their knowledge; but as for the affair of the Hereafter, they are blind.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾: he says: We did not create them ﴿إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ — for reward, punishment and deeds — ﴿وَأَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾: the Resurrection.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَثَارُواْ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾: they ploughed it, ﴿وَعَمَرُوهَآ أَكْثَرَ﴾ than they [the Meccans] cultivate it. He says: they used to cultivate more than the people of Mecca cultivate, and they were destroyed.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ عَاقِبَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَاءُواْ ٱلسُّوۤءَىٰ﴾.
You put "the outcome" in the accusative by kāna, and make the nominative of (كان) be in ﴿ٱلسُّوۤءَىٰ﴾. Had you put "the outcome" in the nominative and ﴿ٱلسُّوۤءَىٰ﴾ in the accusative, it would be correct. ﴿ٱلسُّوۤءَىٰ﴾ in this place is the punishment; it is also said: the Fire.
His saying ﴿أَن كَذَّبُواْ﴾: for their denial, and because (li-an) they denied; when you drop the lām it is accusative.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يُبْلِسُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾: they despair of all good, and their speech and their arguments are cut off. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (يُبْلَسُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ) with fatḥa on the lām. The first is better. The poet said:
يا صَاحِ هل تعرف رَسماً مكرَساً * قال نعم أعرفُه وَأبلسَا
(O friend, do you recognise a trace caked with dung? He said: yes, I know it — and fell silent in despair.)

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ ٱللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ﴾: he says: pray to Allah ﴿حِينَ تُمْسُونَ﴾, which is the sunset and night prayers; ﴿وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ﴾: the dawn prayer; ﴿وَعَشِيّاً﴾: the afternoon prayer; ﴿وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ﴾: the noon prayer.

farraa:22-22.t: His saying: ﴿لآيَاتٍ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾: He means the worlds of jinn and humans. Whoever reads it ﴿للعَالِمينَ﴾ ("for those who know"), that is a good reading, because He has said ﴿لآياتٍ لقومٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ and ﴿لآياتٍ لأُولِى الأَلْبَابِ﴾.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ ٱلْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً﴾: before it and after it there is (أنْ … أنْ), and each is correct. Whoever makes (أنْ) overt, it is in the position of a nominative noun, as He said ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ مَنَامُكُمْ بِاللَّيِْلِ والنَّهَارِ﴾. When you omit (أنْ), you make (مِن) stand for an omitted noun of which the verb is the ṣila, as in the poet's saying:
وما الدهر إِلاَّ تارتان فمنهُمَا * أمُوتُ وَأُخرى أبتغى العَيْش أكدح
(Time is but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek a living, toiling.)
[144/b] / As though he meant: of them is a time in which I die, and a time in which I live. Likewise: of His signs is a sign for the lightning and a sign for such-and-such. And if you wish: He shows you, of His signs, the lightning — without implying (أن) or anything else.

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿أَن تَقُومَ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلأَرْضُ بِأَمْرِهِ﴾: he says: that they continue standing by His command without pillars.

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUmāra related from al-Ḥakam from Mujāhid that he said: re-creating is easier for Him than originating. Abū Zakariyyāʾ [al-Farrāʾ] said: I do not care for that. What is to be said about it is that it is a parable Allah struck, saying: do you disbelieve in the resurrection? The original creation of you from nothing is harder; so re-creating from something ought, in your view, O people of disbelief, to be easier for Him. Then He said ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ﴾, and this is a witness that it is a parable Allah struck. Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us, saying: Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Ḥibbān related to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ﴾: [easier] for the created being, because He will say to him on the Day of Resurrection "Be!" and he will be, whereas the beginning of his creation was a drop of semen, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh.

farraa:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿كَخِيفَتِكُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ﴾: You put "selves" in the accusative because the interpretation of the kāf and mīm in ﴿خِيفَتِكُمْ﴾ is nominative [i.e. they are the agent of the maṣdar]. If you intended it — the kāf and mīm — to be in the interpretation of an accusative, you would put what follows in the nominative. You say in ordinary speech: "I wondered at abundant water-drinking's agreeing with you (min muwāfaqatika kathratu shurbi al-māʾ)" [with the following noun nominative], and "I wondered at your buying a slave you do not need" [with it accusative]. When the like of this occurs in speech, treat it according to the meaning, not according to the wording. The Arabs say: "I wondered at your standing, all of you (ajmaʿūna and ajmaʿīna)", and "your standing, all of you (kullukum and kullikum)": whoever uses the genitive makes it follow the wording, because it is genitive on the surface, and whoever uses the nominative goes by the interpretation. Similar is ﴿لإيلاَفِ قرَيْشٍ إيلاَفِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتَاء والصَّيْفِ﴾: you made the action of Quraysh fall upon ﴿رِحْلَة﴾. And the Arabs say: "I wondered at their falling one upon another (baʿḍuhā fawqa baʿḍin)" and "baʿḍihā", in the same way; this is when they use a pronoun. But when they say "I heard the grinding of his canines, one against another (baʿḍihā baʿḍan)", they put (بعض) in the genitive, and that is the proper way in speech, because what precedes it is an overt noun, so they made it follow it. Had you put (بعضهَا) in the nominative, it would be according to the interpretation.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿فِطْرَتَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He means the religion of Allah; it is accusative by a verb, like His saying ﴿صِبْغَةَ اللهِِ﴾. His saying ﴿ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا﴾: he says: the newborn is upon the natural disposition (al-fiṭra) until his two parents are the ones who make him a Christian or make him a Jew. It is also said: the fiṭra of Allah is that Allah created the servants on this: on their knowing that they have a Lord and a Disposer.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿مُنِيبِينَ﴾ is accusative by a verb, or, if you wish, by severance (qaṭʿ, as a ḥāl):
"So set your face, you and those with you, turning in repentance (مُنِيبِينَ)", turning towards Him.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَكُونُواْ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ ﴿مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ فَارَقُواْ دِينَهُمْ﴾: this is one way. And if you wish you may begin anew and say: ﴿مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ فَارَقُواْ دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعاً كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾, as though you said: of those who split up and formed factions, each party is rejoicing in what is in its hand.

farraa:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَاناً﴾: a book, which commands them to worship idols and to associate partners [with Allah].

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿لِّيَرْبُوَ﴾: ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it with the yāʾ and the wāw in the accusative. The people of the Ḥijāz read it ﴿لِتُرْبُوَ﴾ [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the form intended is li-turbū], "you". All are correct. Whoever reads ﴿ليَرْبوَ﴾, the verb belongs to the usury; whoever says ﴿لتُرْبُوا﴾, the verb belongs to the people addressed, and the dropping of the nūn indicates its accusative. Its meaning is: whatever you give of anything in order to take more than it, that is not growing with Allah; ﴿وَمَآ آتَيْتُمْ مِّن زَكَاةٍ تُرِيدُونَ﴾ by it ﴿وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ — that grows by being multiplied.
His saying: ﴿هُمُ ٱلْمُضْعِفُونَ﴾: people entitled to multiplication, just as the Arabs say "aṣbaḥtum musminīna, muʿṭishīna" when [your animals] have become thirsty or fat. Al-Kisāʾī heard the Arabs say: "aṣbaḥta muqwiyan", i.e. your camels are strong, and "aṣbaḥta muḍʿifan", i.e. your camels are ḍiʿāf — meaning weak, from al-ḍuʿf (weakness).

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿ظَهَرَ ٱلْفَسَادُ فِي ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي ٱلنَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُمْ﴾: he says: the land became barren and the supply of the sea was cut off because of their sins; and that was so that they might be made to taste hardship for their sins in this present life.

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿يَصَّدَّعُونَ﴾: they will be split apart. He said: I heard the Arabs say: "I split my sheep into two groups (ṣadaʿtu ghanamī ṣidʿatayn)", like your saying: I divided them into two divisions.

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿إِلَىٰ آثَارِ رَحْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it (آثَارِ), and the people of the Ḥijāz (أَثَر); all are correct.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرّاً﴾: they fear its perishing after its greenness — he means the crops.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿بِهَادِ ٱلْعُمْيِ عَن ضَلاَلَتِهِمْ﴾ and ﴿من ضَلاَلَتِهِمْ﴾: each is correct. Whoever says ﴿عَن ضَلاَلَتِهِمْ﴾, it is as though he said: you cannot turn the blind away from error; and whoever says (مِنْ) says: you cannot hold them back from error.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿يُقْسِمُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ مَا لَبِثُواْ غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ﴾: they swear, when they come forth, that they remained in their graves only an hour. Allah said: they lied in this, as they lied in the world and denied. Had it been "we did not remain (mā labithnā) but an hour", it would be a valid way, because it is their own speech, as in your saying in ordinary speech: "they swore they did not stand (mā qāmū)" and "they swore: we did not stand (mā qumnā)".

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The preposition «في أدنى» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {غُلِبَتِ}. The clause «وهم سيغلبون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the initial clause {غُلِبَتِ}, and the preposition «من بعد» is attached to «سيغلبون».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The preposition «في بضع» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {سَيَغْلِبُونَ}. The clause «لله الأمر» is parenthetical. The clause «يفرح المؤمنون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «وهم سيغلبون». The preposition «من قبل» is attached to the "being" (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached. The adverb «يوم» is attached to «يفرح», and «إذٍ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The preposition «بنصر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يَفْرَحُ}. The clause «ينصر» is resumptive, and the clause «وهو العزيز» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ينصر»; «الرحيم» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «وَعْدَ»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is implied, and the clause is resumptive. Likewise the clause «لا يخلف الله وعده» is resumptive, confirming the meaning of the preceding maṣdar. The clause «ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا يخلف الله».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «يعلمون» is resumptive. The preposition «من الحياة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ظاهرا». The clause «وهم غافلون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «يعلمون», and the preposition «عن الآخرة» is attached to «غافلون». The second «هم» is tawkīd (emphasis).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «أولم يتفكروا» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «ما خلق». The preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «خلق», and «أجل» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الحق». The clause «وإن كثيرا ...» is resumptive. The preposition «من الناس» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا», and the preposition «بلقاء» is attached to «كافرون».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «أولم يسيروا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا}. «كيف»: an interrogative noun, khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the clause «كان عاقبة» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative and carries the meaning of knowing. The clause «كانوا» is resumptive. The preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أشد». «قوة»: tamyīz (specification). «أكثر»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its adjective standing in for it, i.e. "a cultivation greater than their cultivation". His words «مما»: composed of the preposition «مِنْ» and maṣdariyya «ما», and the genitive maṣdar is attached to أكثر. The clause «وجاءتهم رسلهم» is conjoined to the first clause «عمروها». The clause «فما كان الله ليظلمهم» is resumptive; the lām is that of denial (lām al-juḥūd), and the interpreted maṣdar «ليظلمهم» is genitive, attached to the khabar of kāna, implied as "intending".

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «ثم كان عاقبة ...» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ما كان الله ليظلمهم». «السوءى»: ism (subject) of kāna. «أن» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is by removal of the preposition (the lām). The preposition «بها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يستهزئون».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «ترجعون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause on «يعيد». [Translator's note: the source reads «جملة على «يعيد»», with a superfluous «على».]

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: His words «ويوم»: the wāw is a conjunction, and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يبلس». The clause «يبلس المجرمون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {اللَّهُ يَبْدَأُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «ولم يكن لهم شفعاء» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {يُبْلِسُ}. The preposition «من شركائهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شفعاء», and the preposition «بشركائهم» is attached to «كافرين».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «يتفرقون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {يُبْلِسُ}. The adverb «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يتفرَّقون», and the second «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from the first. «إذ»: an adverbial noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and the preposition «في روضة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) clause «يحبرون».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «فأولئك محضرون» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين», and the preposition «في العذاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The fāʾ in «فسبحان» is resumptive. «حين»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the governor of سبحان, implied as "نسبِّح" (we glorify). «تمسون» is a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb, and the clause «تمسون» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The wāw in «وله الحمد» is parenthetical, and the clause «وله الحمد» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items. His words «وعشيا»: an adverb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to {حِينَ}. The preposition «في السموات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الحمد». «حِينَ» is a noun conjoined to the preceding {حِينَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «يخرج» is resumptive. The kāf is a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "you will be brought out with a bringing-out like that bringing-out". The clause «تخرجون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يحيي».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «ومن آياته أن خلقكم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يحيي». «أن» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «من آياته» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya), and the clause «ثم إذا أنتم بشر» is conjoined to the clause «خلقكم». The clause «تنتشرون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «بَشَر».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The maṣdar «أن خلق» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the interpreted maṣdar «لتسكنوا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلق». The adverb «بينكم» is attached to the implied second object. His words «لآيات»: the lām is for emphasis, and the ism of «إنَّ» is accusative with kasra. The clause «يتفكرون» is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause «إن في ذلك ...» is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «ومن آياته خلق» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «من آياته أن خلقكم», and the preposition «للعالمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of آيات.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The preposition «بالليل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «منامكم», and the preposition «من فضله» is attached to a ḥāl from «ابتغاؤكم». The clause «إن في ذلك لآيات» is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The preposition «من آياته» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يريكم», i.e. "He shows you the lightning as one of His signs"; so He will have conjoined a verbal clause to a nominal clause, i.e. «يريكم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding nominal clause. This construal is more commonly used than construing «أن» as omitted from «يريكم» so that it would be like the preceding parallel cases. «خوفا»: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The preposition «بأمره» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the heaven and the earth. The clause «ومن آياته قيام» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding verbal clause {يُرِيكُمُ}. The conditional clause is conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar «أن تقوم», so that He will have conjoined a clause to a single word. The clause «إذا أنتم تخرجون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and this «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya). His words «دعوة»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The preposition «من الأرض» is attached to «دعاكم».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «وله من في السموات» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ تَقُومَ}. The preposition «في السموات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause), and the preposition «له» is attached to «قانتون». The clause «كل له قانتون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the preceding «مَنْ».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «وهو الذي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَلَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ}, and the clause «وهو أهون» is parenthetical. «أهون» here is not for comparison (tafḍīl); rather it is an adjective meaning "easy" (هيّن). The preposition «عليه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أهون». The clause «وله المثل» is conjoined to the clause «وهو الذي», and the clause {وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ} is conjoined to the clause «وله المثل». The preposition «في السموات» is attached to «الأعلى».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The preposition «من أنفسكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «مثلا». The preposition «لكم» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «شركاء», and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The preposition «مما» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شركاء», and the preposition «في ما» is attached to «شركاء». The clause «هل لكم شركاء» is explicative of the parable, and the clause «فأنتم فيه سواء» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the explicative one. The clause «تخافونهم» is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ «أنتم», and the preposition «فيه» is attached to the maṣdar (سواء). The kāf in «كخيفتكم» is a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a fearing like your fear", and «أنفسكم» is the object of the maṣdar. The clause «نفصِّل» is resumptive, and the kāf in «كذلك» is a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "We detail with a detailing like that".

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «بل اتبع» is resumptive, and «بل» is for digression (iḍrāb). The preposition «بغير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الذين». The clause «فمن يهدي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause. The clause «وما لهم من ناصرين» is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) «أضلَّ الله»; «ناصرين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «فأقم» is resumptive. «حنيفا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in «وجهك». His words «فطرة»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "adhere to" (الزموا). The preposition «عليها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فطر». The clause «لا تبديل لخلق الله» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «ذلك الدين القيم». The clause «ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ذلك الدين القيم».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: «منيبين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of الزموا. The preposition «إليه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «منيبين». The clause «واتقوه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the implied clause الزموا.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The preposition «من الذين» is a badal (substitute) from {الْمُشْرِكِينَ}, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what that is attached to. The preposition «بما» is attached to «فرحون». «لديهم»: an adverb attached to the ṣila (relative clause). The clause «كل حزب فرحون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and the clause «مسّ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). «منيبين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «دعوا», and the preposition «إليه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ḥāl. The second conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first, and the clause «إذا فريق ...» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya), and «فريق» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). The preposition «منهم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «فريق». The clause «يشركون» is the khabar (predicate), and the preposition «بربهم» is attached to «يشركون».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The interpreted maṣdar «ليكفروا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يُشْرِكُونَ}, and the lām is that of outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba). The clause «فتمتعوا» is resumptive, and the clause «فسوف تعلمون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «تمتعوا».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «أنزلنا» is resumptive, and the clause «فهو يتكلم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أنزلنا». The preposition «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يشركون».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the conditional clause {وَإِذَا مَسَّ} in verse (33). «رحمة»: second object. The clause «وإن تصبهم» is conjoined to the conditional clause «وإذا أذقنا». The preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تصبهم». The clause «إذا هم يقنطون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya).

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The clause «أولم يروا» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from «أنَّ» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «يروا». The clause «إن في ذلك لآيات» is resumptive, and the clause «يؤمنون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The clause «فآت» is resumptive. «حقه»: second object. The preposition «للذين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خير». «هم»: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). The clause «وأولئك هم المفلحون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ذلك خير».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The clause «وما آتيتم» is resumptive. «ما» is conditional, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ما». The genitive interpreted maṣdar is attached to «آتيتم». The clause «فلا يربو» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then it does not increase", and the nominal clause «فهو لا يربو» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The clause «تريدون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «آتيتم». The clause «وما آتيتم من زكاة» is like its counterpart.

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The preposition «من شركائكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «مَنْ». The preposition «من ذلكم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شيء»; «شيء» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida). The preposition «عمَّا» is attached to «تعالى».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: «ما» in His words «بما» is maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar (بكسب) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ظهر». The genitive interpreted maṣdar «ليذيقهم» is attached to «ظهر». The clause «لعلهم يرجعون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: The clause «كيف كان» is the object of the looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative and carries the meaning of knowing; «كيف» is an interrogative noun, khabar (predicate) of «كان» placed first. The clause «كان أكثرهم مشركين» is resumptive. The preposition «من قبل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause).

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The clause «فأقم» is resumptive. The maṣdar «أن يأتي» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The preposition «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يأتي», and it is not attached to «مردّ», because then it would have had to take tanwīn and become resembling the muḍāf. The clause «لا مردَّ له» is a naʿt (adjective) of «يوم», and the clause «يصَّدَّعون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: «مَنْ»: conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «كفر» is its khabar (predicate). His words «فلأنفسهم»: the fāʾ is the linking one (rābiṭa), and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the imperfect «يمهدون». The clause «يمهدون» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" (they), and the clause «فلأنفسهم يمهدون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), in the position of the jussive.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The genitive maṣdar «ليجزي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يَمْهَدُونَ}, and the clause «إنه لا يحب» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The maṣdar «أن يرسل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «ومن آياته ...» is resumptive. «مبشرات»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الرياح». The genitive interpreted maṣdar «وليذيقكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied verb, i.e. "and He sent them to let you taste". The clause «ولعلكم تشكرون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the single word, the genitive interpreted maṣdar, i.e. "for your seeking, and that you may be grateful".

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The clause «ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك» is resumptive, and the clause «وكان حقا» is resumptive. «حقًا»: khabar (predicate) of kāna.

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: His words «كيف يشاء»: a non-jussive conditional noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is resumptive and its apodosis is omitted, i.e. "however He wills, He spreads it". The preposition «من عباده» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl from «مَنْ». The clause «يخرج» is a ḥāl from «الودق». The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ترى». The clause «إذا هم يستبشرون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya).

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in {يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ}. «إن» is lightened and inoperative (muhmala), and the lām in the khabar (predicate) is the one distinguishing (al-fāriqa) between the lightened one and the negating one. The preposition «من قبل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: «كيف»: an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «كيف يحيي» is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «آثار». The clause «إن ذلك لمحيي الموتى» is resumptive, and the clause «وهو على كل شيء قدير» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive one.

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The wāw is resumptive, and the lām is the one preparing for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam). «مصفرا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ referring to the vegetation, since the context indicates it. The clause «لظلوا» is the answer to the oath. The preposition «من بعده» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the imperfect verb «يكفرون».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The clause «فإنك لا تسمع» is resumptive. «الدعاء» is the second object of the second verb, and the object of the first is a pronoun; the question is one of contention (tanāzuʿ). «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied apodosis (jawāb), i.e. "when they turn away, you do not make them hear". «مدبرين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw. The conditional clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The negative clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إنك لا تسمع». «ما» operates like laysa, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate). The preposition «عن ضلالتهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «هادي», which includes the meaning of "turning away". The clause «إن تسمع» is resumptive, and the clause «فهم مسلمون» is conjoined to the clause «يؤمن».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The preposition «من بعد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل». The clause «يخلق» is a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «الله», and the clause «وهو العليم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يخلق».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The wāw is resumptive. «يوم»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يقسم», and the clause «يقسم المجرمون» is resumptive. The clause «ما لبثوا» is the response to an implied oath. The clause «كانوا» is resumptive. «غير»: an adverb of time attached to «لبث». The kāf is a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e. "they were deluded with a delusion like that delusion".

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: «العلم»: second object. The clause «لقد لبثتم» is the response to the implied oath, and the oath with its response is the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl). The clause «فهذا يوم البعث» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the content of speech, and likewise the clause «ولكنكم كنتم لا تعلمون».

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The fāʾ is a conjunction. «يوم»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينفع». «إذٍ»: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and the tanwīn is compensation for a clause, i.e. "on the day when that occurs". «معذرتهم»: fāʿil (agent) of «ينفع». The clause «لا ينفع» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يقسم المجرمون», and the clause «ولا هم يُستعتبون» is conjoined to the clause «لا ينفع».

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: The clause «ولقد ضربنا» is resumptive, and the three prepositions are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ضربنا». The clause «ولئن جئتهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive one, the oath clause. The clause «ليقولَنَّ» is the response to the second implied oath. «إن» is negating, «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr), and the clause is the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl).

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: (كذلك يطبع الله) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf is a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e. "He seals with a sealing like that sealing". The clause «يطبع» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The clause «فاصبر» is resumptive, and the clause «إن وعد الله حق» is parenthetical, with no grammatical position. The clause «ولا يستخفنَّك» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «اصبر».

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying, exalted is He, {فِي بضع سِنِين}: the rule for سنة is that it is not pluralised with yāʾ and nūn or wāw and nūn, because wāw and nūn are for rational beings. But that was allowed in سنة, even though it is among non-rational things, because of the elision that affected it, since its origin is سنوة on the pattern فعلة — and it is also said سنهة — the evidence for this being their saying سنوات and their saying سانهت, from السنين. The sīn in سنين was given kasra to indicate that it is pluralised in a way contrary to the rule, because in everything pluralised with the sound plural the structure of the singular does not change; so when the structure of the singular changed in this plural, by the kasra on its first letter while it had fatḥa in the singular, it was known that it is pluralised contrary to its rule.
His saying {من قبل وَمن بعد}: قبل and بعد are indeclinable (mabnī), and they are two adverbs of time whose original state is declension. They were made indeclinable only because they became definite by something other than that by which nouns become definite. Nouns become definite by the alif and lām, by annexation to a definite noun, by being pronouns, by being demonstratives, and by prior mention (ʿahd), and there is none of that in قبل and بعد. So when they became definite in a way different from that by which nouns become definite — namely the omission of what they are annexed to — they differed from nouns and resembled particles, and so they were made indeclinable as particles are made indeclinable. Their rule would have been to be indeclinable on sukūn, since that is the basic state of indeclinability; but the letter before the last is vowelless in both. Moreover, they originally had full declinability (tamakkun), since they are declined when annexed or made indefinite, so they were made indeclinable on a vowel. Moreover, there had to be either a vowel or an elision, and elision is not possible in sound letters, so the second (i.e. the last) letter was vowelled, since the indeclinability is in it. The vowel had to be ḍamma rather than kasra or fatḥa because they resemble the singular vocative noun, since the vocative noun is declined when it is annexed or made indefinite, as happens with these two; so they were made indeclinable on ḍamma, just as the singular vocative is. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān (al-Akhfash the Younger) said: they were made indeclinable only because they are dependent on what comes after them, so they resembled particles, since particles are dependent on other words and convey nothing except by what comes after them. It is also said that they were made indeclinable on ḍamma only because they are two "limits" (ghāyatān): they were used alone and what comes after them was omitted, so they were made indeclinable because they differ from nouns, and they were given ḍamma because it is the limit of the vowels. It is also said that when they included the omitted word after them, they became like part of a noun, and part of a noun is indeclinable. Al-Farrāʾ said: when they included two meanings — that is, their own meaning and the meaning of the omitted word after them — they were made indeclinable and given ḍamma because it is the strongest of the vowels. Hishām said: since they could not take fatḥa, lest they resemble their state in annexation, and could not take kasra, lest they resemble a word annexed to the (first-person) speaker, and were not made vowelless because the letter before the last is vowelless, nothing remained but ḍamma, so they were given it. Al-Farrāʾ allowed رأيتك بعدٌ with tanwīn, in the nominative, and بعدًا in the accusative with tanwīn, both being definite. Hishām allowed رأيتك بعدَ يا هذا with fatḥa and without tanwīn, by implying the muḍāf ilayhi. The meaning of the verse is "to Allah belongs the command before everything and after everything"; so when what follows قبل and بعد was omitted and they included its meaning, they differed from nouns and were made indeclinable.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying وعد الله: an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {ثمَّ كَانَ عَاقِبَة الَّذين أساؤوا السوأى أَن كذبُوا}: عاقبة is the ism (noun) of كان, السوأى is its khabar (predicate), and أن كذبوا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It is also permissible for السوأى to be the object of أساءوا, with {أَن كذبُوا} as the khabar of كان. Whoever puts عاقبة in the accusative makes it the khabar of كان and السوأى its ism; it is also permissible for أن كذبوا to be its ism and السوأى the object of أساءوا.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying {أَن خَلقكُم}: أن is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the genitive phrase before it is its khabar (predicate); likewise everything after it of this description.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying {كخيفتكم}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "you fear them with a fear like your fear of yourselves", i.e. like your fear of yourselves, meaning like your fear of your partners. Similar to it is {كَذَلِك نفصل}, its implied form being "We set out the signs in detail with a setting-out like that", i.e. similar to that.
His saying {فطْرَة الله}: accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "follow the nature (fiṭra) of Allah", indicated by His saying {فأقم وَجهك للدّين}, because its meaning is "follow the religion". It is also said that {فطْرَة الله} is accusative as a maṣdar, because the sentence indicates "Allah created (faṭara) creation with a creating".

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying {منيبين إِلَيْهِ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in فأقم. It is plural only because it refers back to the meaning, since the address is to the Prophet ﷺ and it is an address to his community; so its implied form is "so set your faces, turning to Him". Al-Farrāʾ said: (it means) "set your face, and those with you", and that is why He said منيبين.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying {أم أنزلنَا عَلَيْهِم سُلْطَانا}: (سلطان) is treated as feminine and masculine. It is the plural of سليط, like رغيف and رغفان. Whoever treats it as masculine does so in the sense of "plural" (al-jamʿ), and whoever treats it as feminine does so in the sense of "group" (al-jamāʿa).

mekki-muskil:36-36.t:
His saying {وَإِن تصبهم سَيِّئَة بِمَا قدمت}: a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb) is {إِذا هم يقنطون}. So إذا is an apodosis standing in the place of the fāʾ, because one does not begin with it, just as one does not begin (with the fāʾ); (it is the إذا) of surprise (mufājaʾa). The (إذا) that is for condition is begun with and is not an apodosis of a condition, whereas the إذا of surprise is (equivalent) to the fāʾ. One does not begin with it only because it is the one for surprise. So the إذا that contains the meaning of condition is other than the one with which one does not begin; thus (the latter) resembles the fāʾ, took its place, and became an apodosis for the condition. The fāʾ may enter upon the إذا of surprise in the apodosis of a condition, and that is for emphasis; so know it.
[Translator's note: the Arabic of this passage is elliptical and partly garbled («كما لا يبتدأ للمفاجأة», «غير التي لا يبتدأ لها»); it has been translated as closely as possible, with obvious connective sense in parentheses.]

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {وَكَانَ حَقًا علينا نصر الْمُؤمنِينَ}: حقا is the khabar (predicate) of كان and نصر is its ism (noun). It is also permissible to imply the ism latent in كان and put نصر in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with علينا as the khabar, and the clause as the khabar of كان. In ordinary speech it is permissible to put حق in the nominative as the ism of كان, since it has been described by علينا, and put نصر in the accusative as the khabar of كان. It is also permissible to put both in the nominative as mubtadaʾ and khabar, implying in كان (a pronoun of) the story or the matter, with the clause as the khabar of كان.

mekki-muskil:48-48.t:
His saying {كسفا}: whoever reads the sīn with fatḥa makes it the plural of كسفة, as you say كسرة and كسر; whoever makes it vowelless does so for lightening.
The hāʾ in His saying {من خلاله} refers to السحاب. It may also refer to الكسف, but (the pronoun) is masculine, just as He said {من الشّجر الْأَخْضَر}.

mekki-muskil:51-51.t:
His saying {فرأوه مصفرا}: the hāʾ refers to the crops. It is also said: to the clouds; and it is also said: to the wind. الريح is treated as masculine (here) because the hāʾ is for what is sent of it. It is also said that it is treated as masculine since it has no male counterpart, so its femininity is not real.
His saying {لظلوا من بعده}: its meaning is ليظلوا ("they would remain"), so the past stands in the position of the future. This is good because the sentence has the meaning of a conditional requital (mujāzāt), and requital is only with the future. This is the doctrine of Sībawayh.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿الم﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿غلبت الروم﴾: غلبت: a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); and الروم: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿في أدنى الأرض وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون﴾: في أدنى: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) غلبت; the wāw: a conjunction; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); من بعد: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to His saying سيغلبون; غلبهم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and it [the maṣdar] has been annexed to its object; and the clause سيغلبون: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿في بضع سنين لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد﴾: في بضع سنين: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying ﴿سيغلبون﴾; لله: fronted khabar (predicate); الأمر: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); من قبل: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); من: a preposition; قبل and بعد: two adverbs made indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because they are cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning; they were then put in the genitive by من and remained on their ḍamma.
﴿ويومئذ يفرح المؤمنون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يفرح﴾; إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for a clause, the implied form being: "and on the day when the Romans overcome Persia the believers will rejoice." ﴿يفرح﴾ is an imperfect verb, and ﴿المؤمنون﴾ is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿بنصر الله ينصر من يشاء وهو العزيز الرحيم﴾: بنصر: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يفرح, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ينصر: an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; من: a relative noun, the object of ينصر; the clause يشاء: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; the wāw is a conjunction; هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); العزيز: first khabar (predicate); and الرحيم: second khabar.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وعد الله لا يخلف الله وعده ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون﴾: وعد: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governing verb is implied, the implied form being "Allah promised them that as a promise"; لا: negating; ﴿يخلف الله وعده﴾: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the wāw: circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿لكنَّ أكثر﴾: لكن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and أكثر is its noun; الناس: muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause ﴿لا يعلمون﴾: the khabar (predicate) of لكِنَّ.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t: ﴿يعلمون ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون﴾: يعلمون ظاهرا: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من الحياة الدنيا: a preposition, its genitive noun and a naʿt (adjective); the clause ﴿يعلمون﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); عن الآخرة: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) غافلون; the second ﴿هم﴾: a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first ﴿هم﴾; and غافلون: the khabar (predicate) of the first ﴿هم﴾. Or the second ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and ﴿غافلون﴾ a khabar of the second ﴿هم﴾, the clause ﴿هم غافلون﴾ being a khabar of the first ﴿هم﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿أولم يتفكروا في أنفسهم ما خلق الله السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إلا بالحق وأجل مسمى﴾: the hamza: for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); the wāw: conjoining to something implied which the context requires; لم: a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; يتفكروا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, and the wāw of the plural: fāʿil (agent); في أنفسهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتفكروا﴾. ما: negating; خلق الله السماوات: a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is a conjunction; ما: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi; بينهما: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; the pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); إلا: a particle of restriction; بالحق: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of خلق; أجل: conjoined to الحق; and مسمى: a naʿt (adjective) of أجل.
﴿وإن كثيرا من الناس بلقاء ربهم لكافرون﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); إن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and كثيرا is its noun; من الناس: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of كثيرًا; بلقاء: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كافرون; ربهم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the lām: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and كافرون: the khabar (predicate) of إن.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); the wāw: conjoining to something implied which the context requires, i.e. "did they stay sitting in their places and not travel?"; لم: a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; يسيروا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the wāw: fāʿil (agent); في الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يسيروا; فينظروا: the fāʾ conjoins to يسيروا, or the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya), and ينظروا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن concealed after the fāʾ, the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the concealed ﴿أن﴾ and the verb being conjoined to a maṣdar taken from the preceding speech, its implied form being: "was there not a travelling and then a looking?"; كيف: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; عاقبة: its noun; الذين: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); من قبلهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿كانوا أشد منهم قوة وأثاروا الأرض وعمروها أكثر مما عمروها﴾: كان is a defective past verb, the wāw of the plural its noun, and أشد its khabar (predicate); منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أشد; قوة: tamyīz (specification); أثاروا الأرض: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause ﴿أثاروا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿كانوا...﴾; عمروها: a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, the wāw conjoining the clause to what precedes it; أكثر: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a greater cultivation"; مما: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أكثر; and ما: maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar made genitive by من.
﴿وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); جاءتهم رسلهم: a verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a fāʿil (agent); بالبينات: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) جاءتهم; the fāʾ: a conjunction; ما: negating; كان الله: كان is a defective past verb and the Name of Majesty its noun; the lām: the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); يظلمهم: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن concealed after the lām of denial, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the implied khabar (predicate) of كان; ولكن: the wāw is circumstantial, and لكن: an inoperative particle of rectification (istidrāk); كانوا: a defective past verb, and the wāw: its noun; أنفسهم: a fronted object of يظلمون; and يظلمون: a verb and its fāʿil, the clause being the khabar of كانوا.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿ثم كان عاقبة الذين أساءوا السوءى﴾: ثم is a conjunction; كان: a defective past verb; عاقبة: the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; الذين: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause أساءوا: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and السوأى: the noun of كان.
﴿أن كذبوا بآيات الله وكانوا بها يستهزئون﴾: أن is a maṣdar-forming, accusative-governing particle; كذبوا: a past verb, accusative by أن [Translator's note: so in the source; a past verb is indeclinable, so it is "in the position of" accusative], and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن كذبوا﴾ is accusative by removal of the preposition; بآيات الله: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) كذبوا, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); كانوا: a defective past verb, the wāw of the plural being its noun; بها: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يستهزئون﴾; and the clause يستهزئون: the khabar (predicate) of كان.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ثم إليه ترجعون﴾: the Name of Majesty: mubtadaʾ (subject); يبدأ الخلق: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "He", and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the clause being the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; ثم is a conjunction; and the clause ﴿يعيده﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿يبدأ...﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t: ﴿ويوم تقوم الساعة يبلس المجرمون﴾: يوم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) يبلس; تقوم الساعة: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿تقوم...﴾ is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; and يبلس المجرمون: a verb and its fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿ولم يكن لهم من شركائهم شفعاء وكانوا بشركائهم كافرين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لم: a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; يكن: a defective imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم; لهم: the fronted khabar (predicate) of يكن; من شركائهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of شفعاء; شفعاء: the noun of يكن; كانوا: كان is a defective past verb and the wāw of the plural its noun; بشركائهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كافرين; and كافرين: the khabar of كانوا.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يتفرقون﴾: ﴿يوم﴾ is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتفرقون﴾; ﴿تقوم الساعة﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿تقوم الساعة﴾ is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; يومئذ: يوم: an adverb of time attached to ﴿يتفرقون﴾, and it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the preceding adverb or a badal (substitute) of it; إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for a clause, the implied form being "on the day when the Hour is established." يتفرقون: a verb and its fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فهم في روضة يحبرون﴾: the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿiyya); أما: a particle of condition and detailing; الذين: mubtadaʾ (subject); آمنوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; the wāw is a conjunction; عملوا الصالحات: a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is conjoined to the preceding ṣila clause, with no grammatical position; the fāʾ: in the apodosis of the condition; هم: mubtadaʾ; في روضة: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحبرون; the clause يحبرون: the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾; and the clause is the khabar of الذين.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿وأما الذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا ولقاء الآخرة فأولئك في العذاب محضرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أما: a particle of condition and detailing; الذين: mubtadaʾ (subject); كفروا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; the wāw is a conjunction; كذبوا: a verb and its fāʿil; بآياتنا: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) كذبوا; the wāw is a conjunction; لقاء: conjoined to آيات; الآخرة: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause ﴿كذبوا﴾ is conjoined to the ṣila clause, with no grammatical position. The fāʾ: in the apodosis of the condition; أولئك: mubtadaʾ; في العذاب: a preposition and its genitive noun; محضرون: the khabar (predicate) of أولئك; and the clause is the khabar of الذين.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين تصبحون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted clause); سبحان: a substitute for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative by an omitted verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); حين: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبحان; تمسون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw: fāʿil (agent), because it is complete (tāmma); the clause تمسون is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; and حين تصبحون: conjoined to حين تمسون.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿وله الحمد في السماوات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون﴾: the wāw: parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya); له: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); الحمد: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); في السماوات: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الحمد; الأرض: conjoined to السماوات; عشيا: conjoined to ﴿حين تمسون﴾, and likewise His saying ﴿وحين تظهرون﴾; and the clause ﴿وله الحمد في السماوات والأرض﴾: parenthetical between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or a ḥāl (circumstantial); يخرج: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "He"; الحي: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من الميت: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يخرج﴾; and يخرج الميت من الحي: conjoined to what preceded.
