﴿ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يحيي الأرض: an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بعد موتها: the adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحيي, and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); كذلك: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and like that bringing forth you will be brought forth"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; and تخرجون: an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), the wāw of the plural being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من آياته: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن خلقكم﴾ is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); من تراب: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلقكم; ثم: a conjunction denoting delay (tarākhī); إذا: of surprise (fujāʾiyya); أنتم: mubtadaʾ; بشر: khabar; and the clause تنتشرون: a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿ومن آياته أن خلق لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا لتسكنوا إليها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من آياته: fronted khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن خلق﴾ is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); لكم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلق; من أنفسكم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلق, or the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿أزواجا﴾; أزواجًا: the object of خلق; the lām: for causation (taʿlīl); تسكنوا: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن concealed after the lām, the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb being genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلق; and إليها: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تسكنوا.
﴿وجعل بينكم مودة ورحمة﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جعل is conjoined to خلق; بينكم: an adverb (ẓarf) in the place of the second object of جعل; مودة: it is the first object; and رحمة: conjoined to مودة.
﴿إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون﴾: إن: a particle of emphasis and accusative; في ذلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, the fronted khabar (predicate) of إن; the lām: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات: its postponed noun; لقوم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of آيات; and the clause يتفكرون: a naʿt of قوم.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف ألسنتكم وألوانكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من آياته: fronted khabar (predicate); خلق: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); السماوات: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the wāw is a conjunction; الأرض: conjoined to السماوات; اختلاف: conjoined to خلْق; ألسنتكم: muḍāf ilayhi; the wāw is a conjunction; and ألوانكم: conjoined to ألسنتكم.
﴿إن في ذلك لآيات للعالمين﴾: إن is a particle of emphasis and accusative; في ذلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, the fronted khabar (predicate) of إن; the lām: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات: its postponed noun; and للعالمين: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of آيات.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿ومن آياته منامكم بالليل والنهار وابتغاؤكم من فضله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من آياته: fronted khabar (predicate); منامكم: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); بالليل: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) منامكم; النهار: conjoined to الليل; ابتغاؤكم: conjoined to منامكم; and من فضله: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ابتغاؤكم.
﴿إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون﴾: إن is a particle of emphasis and accusative; في ذلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, the fronted khabar (predicate) of إن; the lām: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات: its postponed noun; لقوم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of آيات; and the clause يسمعون: a naʿt of قوم.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿ومن آياته يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من آياته: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); يريكم: an imperfect verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) referring to Allah; the kāf: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); البرق: second mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the omitted maṣdariyya أن and ﴿يريكم﴾ is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿خوفًا وطمعًا﴾ are accusative as maṣdars (absolute objects), i.e. "that you may fear with fear and hope with hope"; or two ḥāls (circumstantials) of the kāf in ﴿يريكم﴾, i.e. "while you are fearing and hoping"; or of البرق, the implied form being "He shows you the lightning as a thing of fear and a thing of hope", or the lightning is made in itself fear and hope by way of hyperbole; or they are two mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose).
﴿وينزل من السماء ماء فيحيي به الأرض بعد موتها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ينزل is conjoined to يريكم; من السماء: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينزل; ماء: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فيحيي: conjoined to ينزل; به: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يحيي; الأرض: mafʿūl bihi; and بعد موتها: the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون﴾: إن is a particle of emphasis and accusative; في ذلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, the fronted khabar (predicate) of إن; the lām: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات: its postponed noun; لقوم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of آيات; and the clause يعقلون: a naʿt of قوم.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿ومن آياته أن تقوم السماء والأرض بأمره﴾: the wāw conjoins to what preceded; من آياته: fronted khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن تقوم﴾ is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); السماء: the fāʿil (agent) of تقوم; الأرض: conjoined to السماء; and بأمره: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تقوم.
﴿ثم إذا دعاكم دعوة من الأرض إذا أنتم تخرجون﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay (tarākhī); إذا: an adverb (ẓarf) of the future containing the sense of condition; دعاكم: a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause ﴿دعاكم﴾ is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. دعوة: a substitute for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), accusative, its sign of the accusative being the fatḥa. من الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) دعاكم; the إذا of surprise stands in place of the fāʾ in the apodosis of the condition; أنتم: mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause تخرجون: khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿وله من في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; له: a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of nominative as fronted khabar (predicate); من: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); في السماوات: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; الأرض: conjoined to السماوات. كل: mubtadaʾ; له: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قانتون; and قانتون: the khabar of كل.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿وهو الذي يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده وهو أهون عليه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: khabar (predicate); ﴿يبدأ الخلق﴾: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object, and the clause ﴿يبدأ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ثم: a conjunction. يعيده: an imperfect verb, the fāʿil latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وهو﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction, and هو: mubtadaʾ. أهون: its khabar. And عليه: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أهون.
﴿وله المثل الأعلى في السماوات والأرض وهو العزيز الحكيم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; له: fronted khabar (predicate); المثل: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); الأعلى: naʿt (adjective); في السماوات: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial); الأرض: conjoined to السماوات; هو: mubtadaʾ; العزيز: first khabar; and الحكيم: second khabar.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿ضرب لكم مثلا من أنفسكم﴾: ضرب: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He"; لكم: in the position of accusative as the second object; مثلا: it is the first object; and من أنفسكم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of مثلا.
﴿هل لكم من ما ملكت أيمانكم من شركاء في ما رزقناكم﴾: هل: an interrogative particle; لكم: fronted khabar (predicate); مما: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of شركاء; the clause ملكت: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; أيمانكم: the fāʿil (agent) of ملكت; من: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; شركاء: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and فيما رزقناكم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شركاء.
﴿فأنتم فيه سواء تخافونهم كخيفتكم أنفسكم كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يعقلون﴾: the fāʾ: occurring in the response to the interrogation; أنتم: mubtadaʾ (subject); فيه: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) سواء; سواء: khabar (predicate); the clause تخافونهم: a second khabar of ﴿أنتم﴾, or in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent pronoun in سواء; كخيفتكم: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a fear like your fear", and ﴿خيفتكم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); أنفسكم: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar ﴿خيفتكم﴾. كذلك: the kāf is a noun meaning "like", indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; نفصل: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "We"; الآيات: mafʿūl bihi; لقوم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نفصِّل﴾; and the clause ﴿يعقلون﴾ is a naʿt of قوم.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿بل اتبع الذين ظلموا أهواءهم بغير علم﴾: بل: a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; اتبع: conjoined by way of a shift of address (iltifāt); الذين: the fāʿil (agent) of اتبع; ظلموا: a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause ﴿ظلموا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; أهواءهم: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and بغير: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿فمن يهدي من أضل الله﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted clause); من: an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يهدي: khabar (predicate); من: the object of يهدي; the clause ﴿أضل الله﴾: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "whom Allah has led astray (aḍallahu)".
﴿وما لهم من ناصرين﴾: the wāw: a conjunction; ما: negating; لهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate); من: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; and ناصرين: genitive in form, nominative in position, the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿فأقم وجهك للدين حنيفا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted clause); أقم: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; وجهك: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); للدين: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقم﴾; and حنيفًا: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of ﴿أقم﴾, or of its object, or of الدين.
﴿فطرت الله التي فطر الناس عليها﴾: فطرة: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "adhere to Allah's natural disposition (fiṭra)"; التي: a naʿt (adjective) of الفطرة; فطر الناس: a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause ﴿فطر الناس﴾: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and عليها: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) فطر.
﴿لا تبديل لخلق الله﴾: لا: the lā of generic negation; تبديل: its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; and لخلق الله: khabar (predicate).
﴿ذلك الدين القيم﴾: ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); الدين: its khabar (predicate); and القيم: naʿt (adjective).
﴿ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون﴾: the wāw: circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive; لكن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and أكثر its noun; لا: negating; يعلمون: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿لا يعلمون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of لكن; and the clause ﴿ولكن أكثر...﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t: ﴿منيبين إليه واتقوه وأقيموا الصلاة ولا تكونوا من المشركين﴾: منيبين: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of the implied الزموا ("adhere"); اتقوه: conjoined to the implied الزموا, and likewise His saying وأقيموا الصلاة; لا: prohibitive; تكونوا: a defective imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, the wāw of the plural being its noun; and من المشركين: its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿من الذين فرقوا دينهم وكانوا شيعا﴾: من الذين: a preposition and its genitive noun, a badal (substitute) of His saying ﴿من المشركين﴾ with repetition of the governing word; فرقوا: a past verb, the wāw of the plural being the fāʿil (agent); دينهم: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the hāʾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the mīm the plural marker; the clause ﴿فرقوا دينهم﴾: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; كانوا شيعا: كان is a defective past verb, the wāw of the plural its noun, and شيعا its khabar (predicate).
﴿كل حزب بما لديهم فرحون﴾: كل حزب: mubtadaʾ (subject); بما: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) فرحون; لديهم: the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; and فرحون: the khabar (predicate) of كل.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿وإذا مس الناس ضر دعوا ربهم منيبين إليه﴾: the wāw is resumptive; إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) of the future containing the sense of condition; the clause ﴿مس﴾: in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; الناس: a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ضر: postponed fāʿil (agent); دعوا ربهم: a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause ﴿دعوا ربهم﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; منيبين: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of دعوا; إليه: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) منيبين; and the clause ﴿وإذا مس الناس...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿ثم إذا أذاقهم منه رحمة إذا فريق منهم بربهم يشركون﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence and delay (tarākhī); إذا: conditional; أذاقهم: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause ﴿أذاقهم﴾ is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; منه: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of رحمة; رحمة: second mafʿūl bihi; إذا: the إذا of surprise, standing in place of the fāʾ in the apodosis of the condition; فريق: mubtadaʾ (subject); منهم: naʿt (adjective); بربهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يشركون; يشركون: a verb and its fāʿil; and the clause يشركون: in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿ليكفروا بما آتيناهم﴾: the lām is for causation (taʿlīl) or for consequence and outcome (ʿāqiba, ṣayrūra); يكفروا: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن concealed after the lām, the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the concealed أن and the verb being genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يشركون﴾; بما: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يكفروا﴾; and the clause ﴿آتيناهم﴾: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; تمتعوا: an imperative verb; the fāʾ: occurring in the response to the command; سوف: a particle of futurity; and تعلمون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:35-35.t: ﴿أم أنزلنا عليهم سلطانا فهو يتكلم بما كانوا به يشركون﴾: أم: disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of "rather" (بل) and the interrogative hamza, the interrogation being for disapproval and rebuke; أنزلنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); عليهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزلنا; سلطانا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ: a conjunction; هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يتكلم: a verb and its fāʿil, in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate); بما: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يتكلم﴾; the clause كانوا: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position — or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya; كانوا: كان is a defective past verb and the wāw of the plural its noun; به: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يشركون; and the clause يشركون: the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة فرحوا بها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إذا: an adverb (ẓarf) containing the sense of condition; أذقنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); الناس: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); رحمة: second mafʿūl bihi; the clause أذقنا: in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; and the clause ﴿فرحوا بها﴾: has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
﴿وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم إذا هم يقنطون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; تصبهم: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); سيئة: fāʿil (agent); the bāʾ: causal; ما: a relative noun in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تصبهم; the clause ﴿قدمت أيديهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; إذا: the إذا of surprise, which has taken the place of the fāʾ in linking the apodosis to the condition; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يقنطون: khabar (predicate); and the clause إذا هم يقنطون: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿أولم يروا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī) conveying affirmation; the wāw: conjoining to something omitted which the context requires; لم: a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; يروا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم; أن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), the Name of Majesty its noun, and the clause ﴿يبسط الرزق﴾: its khabar (predicate); لمن: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يبسط; the clause ﴿يشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; يقدر: conjoined to يبسط; and أنّ with what falls within its scope fills the place of the two objects of يروا.
﴿إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون﴾: إن is a particle of emphasis and accusative; في ذلك: a preposition and its genitive noun, the fronted khabar (predicate) of إن; the lām: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات: its postponed noun; لقوم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of آيات; and the clause ﴿يؤمنون﴾: a naʿt of قوم.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿فآت ذا القربى حقه والمسكين وابن السبيل﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it discloses (afṣaḥat) something implied, i.e. "if you have known that the evil befell them because of what their hands sent forth, then give." آت: an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; ذا القربى: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and حقه: second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ذلك خير للذين يريدون وجه الله وأولئك هم المفلحون﴾: ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); خير: khabar (predicate); للذين: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) خير; يريدون: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿يريدون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; وجه الله: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is a conjunction; أولئك: mubtadaʾ; هم: second mubtadaʾ; المفلحون: the khabar of «هم»; and the clause ﴿هم المفلحون﴾: the khabar of أولئك.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿وما آتيتم من ربا ليربو في أموال الناس فلا يربو عند الله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما: conditional, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of آتيتم; آتيتم: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); من ربا: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial); ليربوا: the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and يربو: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن concealed after the lām, the concealed أن and the imperfect verb being interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by the lām of causation, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿آتيتم﴾; في أموال الناس: a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ﴿يربو﴾; the fāʾ: linking the apodosis of the condition; لا: negating; يربو: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the clause ﴿فلا يربو﴾: in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and عند الله: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to ﴿يربو﴾.
﴿وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما: conditional, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of آتيتم; آتيتم: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); من زكاة: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial); تريدون: a verb and its fāʿil; وجه الله: mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿تريدون﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of آتيتم; the fāʾ: linking the apodosis of the condition; أولئك: mubtadaʾ (subject); هم المضعفون: a mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate); and the clause ﴿هم المضعفون﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أولئك.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿الله الذي خلقكم ثم رزقكم ثم يميتكم ثم يحييكم﴾: الله: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي خلقكم: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿خلقكم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and what follows it is conjoined to it.
﴿هل من شركائكم من يفعل من ذلكم من شيء﴾: هل is an interrogative particle; من شركائكم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate); من يفعل: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); من ذلكم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of شيء; مِن: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; and شيء: genitive by من in form, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿يفعل﴾, accusative in position.
﴿سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون﴾: سبحانه: a substitute for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative by an omitted verb, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); تعالى: a past verb; عما: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تعالى; and ما: maṣdariyya, or relative.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿ظهر الفساد في البر والبحر بما كسبت أيدي الناس﴾: ظهر الفساد: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); في البر: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ظهر, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الفساد, and this is perhaps preferable; the clause ﴿ظهر الفساد...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position. بما: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾ is relative, i.e. "because of that which they earned"; or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿ما كسبوا﴾ being genitive by the bāʾ, i.e. "because of their earning"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ظهر; and أيدي الناس: the fāʿil of كسبت.
﴿ليذيقهم بعض الذي عملوا لعلهم يرجعون﴾: the lām: the lām of causation (taʿlīl); يذيقهم: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by a concealed أن, the concealed أن and the imperfect verb being interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by the lām of causation, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ظهر﴾ or to something omitted, the implied form being "He punished them with that so that He might make them taste." And it was said: the lām in ﴿ليذيقهم﴾ is not for causation but for outcome (ṣayrūra). هم: the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿يذيق﴾; بعض الذي عملوا: its second object; لعلهم: لعل is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters) of hope (tarajjī), ﴿هم﴾ its noun, and the clause يرجعون its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبل﴾: قل: an imperative verb; the clause ﴿سيروا في الأرض﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of accusative; فانظروا: conjoined to سيروا; كيف: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; كان is a defective past verb and عاقبة its noun; the clause ﴿كيف كان ...﴾ is in the position of accusative as the object of ﴿انظروا﴾; and من قبل: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿كان أكثرهم مشركين﴾: كان is a defective past verb; أكثرهم its noun, and the pronoun muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and مشركين: the khabar (predicate) of كان.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿فأقم وجهك للدين القيم﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted clause); أقم: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; وجهك: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); للدين: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أقم; and القيم: a naʿt (adjective) of الدين.
﴿من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله يومئذ يصدعون﴾: من قبل: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقم﴾; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن﴾ and what follows it is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); يوم: the fāʿil (agent) of يأتي; لا: the lā of generic negation; مرد: its noun; له: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿لا مرد له...﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of يوم; من الله: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يأتي﴾; ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to ﴿يصدعون﴾, and إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for a clause, the implied form being "on the day when that Day comes"; and يصدعون: an imperfect verb, the wāw of the plural being the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿من كفر فعليه كفره﴾: من: a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); كفر: a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ: linking the apodosis; عليه: fronted khabar (predicate); كفره: postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of مَن.
﴿ومن عمل صالحا فلأنفسهم يمهدون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من: a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); عمل: a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); صالحا: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿عمل﴾, or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar, i.e. "did a righteous deed". The fāʾ: linking the apodosis of the condition; لأنفسهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يمهدون﴾; يمهدون: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿يمهدون﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "they"; and the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

muyesser-irab:45-45.t:
﴿ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات من فضله﴾: the lām: for causation (taʿlīl); يجزي: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن concealed after the lām, the concealed أن and the imperfect verb being interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by the lām of causation, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يمهدون﴾ or to ﴿يصدعون﴾, or to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "that is so in order that He may reward." الذين: the object of يجزي; the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿عملوا الصالحات﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾; and من فضله: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يجزي.
﴿إنه لا يحب الكافرين﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), the hāʾ its noun, and the clause لا يحب its khabar (predicate); الكافرين: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is a statement of cause (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:46-46.t:
﴿ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات﴾: the wāw is resumptive; من آياته: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن يرسل﴾ is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); الرياح: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and مبشرات: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الرياح.
﴿وليذيقكم من رحمته ولتجري الفلك بأمره ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the clause ﴿ليذيقكم﴾ is conjoined to His saying ﴿مبشرات﴾, the implied form being "to give you glad tidings and to make you taste"; من رحمته: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يذيقكم; ولتجري الفلك: the lām is for consequence (ʿāqiba) or outcome (ṣayrūra), and تجري الفلك: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بأمره: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجري, or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الفلك. ولتبتغوا من فضله: likewise conjoined; ولعلكم تشكرون: لعل is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), ﴿كم﴾ its noun, and the clause تشكرون its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:47-47.t:
﴿ولقد أرسلنا من قبلك رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the lām occurs in the response to an implied oath; قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); أرسلنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); من قبلك: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of رسلا; رسلا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلى قومهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسلنا; the fāʾ is a conjunction; جاءوهم: a verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause ﴿ولقد أرسلنا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿جاءوهم﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أرسلنا﴾; and بالبينات: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاءوهم or to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of جاءوهم.
﴿فانتقمنا من الذين أجرموا﴾: the fāʾ: conjoining to something omitted, its implied form being "so they denied them, and We took vengeance"; من الذين: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿انتقمنا﴾; and the clause أجرموا: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين﴾: the wāw is resumptive; كان: a defective past verb; حقا: its fronted khabar (predicate); علينا: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حقا﴾ or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of it; نصر المؤمنين: the postponed noun of كان; and the clause ﴿وكان حقا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿الله الذي يرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فيبسطه في السماء كيف يشاء﴾: الله: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: its khabar (predicate); يرسل الرياح: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object, the clause being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; فتثير: conjoined to يرسل; سحابًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ: a conjunction; the clause ﴿يبسطه﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿تثير﴾; في السماء: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يبسطه; and كيف: a particle of condition and suspension (taʿlīq) in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its apodosis omitted, i.e. "however He wills, He spreads it."
﴿ويجعله كسفا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يجعله: conjoined to يبسطه; the hāʾ: the first object of ﴿يجعل﴾; and كسفا: the second object of ﴿يجعل﴾.
﴿فترى الودق يخرج من خلاله﴾: فترى: conjoined to the preceding clause, and the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿ترى﴾ is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; الودق: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يخرج﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and من خلاله: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يخرج.
﴿فإذا أصاب به من يشاء من عباده إذا هم يستبشرون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا: an adverb (ẓarf) of the future containing the sense of condition; the clause أصاب: in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; به: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أصاب; من: the object of أصاب; يشاء: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿يشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) being omitted, the implied form being "He wills it (yashāʾuhu)". من عباده: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative noun or of the returning pronoun «the omitted hāʾ» (الهاء المحذوفة); إذا: of surprise (fujāʾiyya), occurring in the apodosis of the first إذا; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause يستبشرون: khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:49-49.t: ﴿وإن كانوا من قبل أن ينزل عليهم من قبله لمبلسين﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction; إن: lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), inoperative; كان is a defective past verb, the wāw of the plural its noun; من قبل: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) مبلسين or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdariyya; ﴿ينزل﴾: an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن ينزل﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); عليهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يُنَزَّل; the second ﴿من قبله﴾ is a repetition and tawkīd (emphasis) of the first ﴿من قبل﴾; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); and مبلسين: the khabar (predicate) of كان.

muyesser-irab:50-50.t:
﴿فانظر إلى آثار رحمت الله كيف يحي الأرض بعد موتها﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted clause), i.e. "if you wish to know what results from the sending down of rain, then look." انظر: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; إلى آثار: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) انظر; رحمة: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the Name of Majesty: muḍāf ilayhi; كيف: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it suspends ﴿انظر﴾ from governing (muʿalliqa); يحيي: a verb and its fāʿil; الأرض: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بعد موتها: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to يحيي; and the clause ﴿كيف يحيي...﴾ is a badal (substitute) of آثار, so it is in the domain of the accusative by removal of the preposition.
﴿إن ذلك لمحي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), and ذلك its noun; the lām: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); محيي الموتى: its khabar (predicate); هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); على كل شيء: a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) قدير; and قدير: the khabar of هو.

muyesser-irab:51-51.t: ﴿ولئن أرسلنا ريحا فرأوه مصفرا لظلوا من بعده يكفرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām: preparing for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), having entered upon the conditional particle; أرسلنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ريحا: the object of أرسلنا; فرأوه: a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause ﴿رأوه﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أرسلنا﴾; مصفرا: a ḥāl (circumstantial); لظلوا: the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and ظلوا: a defective past verb, the wāw its noun, the clause having no grammatical position because it is the response to the oath and has made the apodosis of the condition unnecessary; من بعده: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يكفرون or attached to a ḥāl; and the clause يكفرون: the khabar (predicate) of ظلوا.

muyesser-irab:52-52.t: ﴿فإنك لا تسمع الموتى ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ولوا مدبرين﴾: the fāʾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), the clause being a statement of cause for something omitted, i.e. "do not grieve over their not believing, for you cannot make the dead hear… etc." إن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), the kāf its noun, and the clause ﴿لا تسمع الموتى﴾: its khabar (predicate); لا تسمع الصم الدعاء: conjoined to the preceding clause; الصم: the first object of تُسمِع; الدعاء: the second object of تُسمِع; إذا: an adverb (ẓarf) of the future attached to (mutaʿalliq) تُسمِع; the clause ﴿ولوا﴾ is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; ولوا: a past verb, the wāw of the plural being the fāʿil (agent); and مدبرين: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw of the plural.

muyesser-irab:53-53.t:
﴿وما أنت بهاد العمي عن ضلالتهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما: negating, operating like ليس; أنت: the noun of ما; the bāʾ: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; هادي: genitive in form, accusative in position, because it is the khabar (predicate) of ما; العمي: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and عن ضلالتهم: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) هادي, هادي being made to imply the sense of "turning away" (ṣārif), or attached to العمي.
﴿إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا فهم مسلمون﴾: إن is negating; تسمع: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; إلا: a particle of restriction; مَن: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause يؤمن: the ṣila (relative clause) of مَن, with no grammatical position; بآياتنا: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤمن﴾. فهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); and مسلمون: khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:54-54.t:
﴿الله الذي خلقكم من ضعف﴾: the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: khabar (predicate); the clause خلقكم: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and من ضعف: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلقكم.
﴿ثم جعل من بعد ضعف قوة ثم جعل من بعد قوة ضعفا وشيبة﴾: ثم: a conjunction denoting delay (tarākhī); جعل: a past verb; من بعد ضعف: a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) جعل; قوة: the object of جعل; and ثم with what follows it: conjoined to what preceded.
﴿يخلق ما يشاء وهو العليم القدير﴾: يخلق ما: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and an object, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); العليم: first khabar (predicate); and القدير: second khabar.

muyesser-irab:55-55.t:
﴿ويوم تقوم الساعة يقسم المجرمون ما لبثوا غير ساعة﴾: the wāw is resumptive; يوم: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) يقسم; the clause ﴿تقوم الساعة﴾ is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; يقسم المجرمون: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ما: negating; لبثوا: a verb and its fāʿil; the clause ﴿ما لبثوا...﴾ has no grammatical position because it occurs as the response to the oath; غير: an adverb attached to لبثوا; ساعة: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause ﴿ويوم تقوم...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿كذلك كانوا يؤفكون﴾: كذلك: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they were turned away with a turning-away like that"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; كان is a defective past verb, the wāw of the plural its noun; يؤفكون: an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), the wāw of the plural being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause ﴿يؤفكون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of كانوا.

muyesser-irab:56-56.t:
﴿وقال الذين أوتوا العلم والإيمان لقد لبثتم في كتاب الله إلى يوم البعث﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; قال الذين: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿أوتوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; العلم: the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أوتوا﴾; الإيمان: conjoined to العلم. لقد: the lām: in response to an omitted oath; قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); لبثتم: a verb and its fāʿil; في كتاب الله: a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿لبثتم﴾; إلى يوم البعث: a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to لبثتم; and the clause ﴿لقد لبثتم ...﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿فهذا يوم البعث ولكنكم كنتم لا تعلمون﴾: the fāʾ conjoins to the clause ﴿لقد لبثتم﴾, or it is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, the implied form being "if you deny the resurrection, then this is the Day of Resurrection." هذا: mubtadaʾ (subject); يوم: khabar (predicate); البعث: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ولكنكم: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لكن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters) and ﴿كم﴾ its noun; the clause ﴿كنتم ...﴾: the khabar of لكن; and the clause ﴿لا تعلمون﴾: the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:57-57.t: ﴿فيومئذ لا ينفع الذين ظلموا معذرتهم ولا هم يستعتبون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction or the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted clause); ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the negated verb ﴿ينفع﴾, and إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being "on the day when the Hour is established, there will not benefit." لا: negating; ينفع: an imperfect verb; الذين: its fronted object; the clause ﴿ظلموا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; معذرتهم: the fāʿil (agent) of ينفع; the wāw: a conjunction; لا: negating; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); يستعتبون: an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), the wāw of the plural being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the clause ﴿يستعتبون﴾: khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:58-58.t:
﴿ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the lām occurs in the response to an implied oath; قد: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ضربنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); للناس: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ضربنا; في هذا القرآن: a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ضربنا [Translator's note: so in the source; القرآن is grammatically a badal or naʿt of هذا, not a muḍāf ilayhi]; من كل مثل: a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun which is the object of ضربنا; and the clause ﴿ولقد ضربنا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿ولئن جئتهم بآية ليقولن الذين كفروا إن أنتم إلا مبطلون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām: preparing for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); إن: conditional; جئتهم: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause ﴿جئتهم﴾ is in the place of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); بآية: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) جئتهم; ليقولن: the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and يقولن: an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis [Translator's note: so in the source; here the verb is plural (لَيَقُولُنَّ), so the nūn of emphasis is not directly attached and the verb is usually parsed as nominative with the nūn of the five verbs dropped, as this book itself does at 29:61]; الذين: a relative noun in the position of nominative as fāʿil; the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position. إن: negating; أنتم: mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا: a particle of restriction; مبطلون: the khabar (predicate) of أنتم; and the clause ﴿إن أنتم ...﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of accusative.

muyesser-irab:59-59.t: ﴿كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الذين لا يعلمون﴾: ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf: a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), the implied form being "with a sealing like that sealing Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know"; ذلك: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address. يطبع الله: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); على قلوب: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يطبع; الذين: a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause ﴿لا يعلمون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:60-60.t:
﴿فاصبر إن وعد الله حق﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you know that, then be patient." اصبر: an imperative verb, the fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; إن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), وعد its noun, and the Name of Majesty muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and حق: the khabar (predicate) of إن.
﴿ولا يستخفنك الذين لا يوقنون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا: prohibitive; يستخفنك: an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of jussive by the prohibitive لا; the kāf: a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذين: the postponed fāʿil of ﴿يستخفنك﴾; and the clause ﴿لا يوقنون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-3.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: this [غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ ... سَيَغْلِبُونَ] is the reading of most people. It is reported from Abū ʿAmr and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that they read (الَم غَلبَتِ الرُّومُ) [i.e. with the active غَلَبَت] and read (سَتُغْلَبُونَ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended form is the passive سَيُغْلَبُونَ]. Abū Ḥātim reported that ʿIṣma narrated from Hārūn that this is the reading of the people of Syria; Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal says that this ʿIṣma is weak, while Abū Ḥātim narrates a great deal from him. The ḥadīth indicates that the reading is غُلِبَتِ with ḍamma on the ghayn. In this report there was a proof of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, because Persia had defeated the Romans, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, announced that the Romans would defeat Persia within a few years, and that the believers would rejoice at that because the Romans were People of the Book. This was part of the knowledge of the unseen that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, announced before it had happened. He commanded Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, to wager with them on that and to raise the wager; then wagering was forbidden and abrogated by the prohibition of gambling. (وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ): al-Farrāʾ claimed that the original was من بعد غلبتهم and the tāʾ was dropped, as it was dropped in His saying (وَأَقامَ الصَّلاةَ) [al-Nūr: 37]. This is an error that is not hidden from many grammarians, because «أقام الصلاة» [i.e. إقامة] is a maṣdar (verbal noun) from which something was dropped because its verb is weak, and the tāʾ was made a compensation for what was dropped; whereas «غلب» is not weak and nothing was dropped from it. Al-Aṣmaʿī reported: طرد طردا, حلب حلبا and غلب غلبا — so what dropping is there in this? And may one say about أكل أكلا and the like that something was dropped from it?

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (ثُمَّ كانَ عاقِبَةَ الَّذِينَ) [Translator's note: the comment treats this as the nominative reading عاقِبَةُ, although the source prints the accusative vowel]: the noun of كان; [the verb] is masculine because its femininity is not real. (السُّواى) is the khabar of كان. Whoever reads (عاقِبَةَ) in the accusative makes «السّوأى» the noun of كان. It is reported from al-Aʿmash that he read ثمّ كان عاقبة الذين أساؤا السّوءُ, with السوء in the nominative. (أَنْ كَذَّبُوا) is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is "because they denied".

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (يُبلَس) with fatḥa on the lām. What is known in the language is أبلس الرجل, when a man falls silent, his argument cut off, with no hope of having an argument; close to it is "he was bewildered", as the rajaz poet said:
336-
قال: نعم أعرفه وأبلسا
(He said: "Yes, I know it", and fell silent in despair.)
Some grammarians claimed that «إبليس» is derived from this, and that he "despaired (ablasa)", that is, his argument was cut off. Had it been as he said, it would have to be fully declinable, yet in the Qurʾān it is a diptote. Some of them argued that it is a noun that was felt heavy because no one else was named by it.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ مِنْ شُرَكائِهِمْ شُفَعاءُ): it is said: by "their partners" He means what they worshipped besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (وَكانُوا بِشُرَكائِهِمْ كافِرِينَ): they said: they are not gods.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
(فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): I heard Abū Isḥāq say: the meaning of «أمّا» is "leave what we were on and take up something else". Likewise Sībawayh said that its meaning is مهما يكن من شيء ("whatever may be the case"), that is: whatever may be the case, take up something other than what we were on. (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (فَهُمْ) is a second mubtadaʾ, what follows is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «الذين». Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (فِي رَوْضَةٍ): in a garden; and الرياض are gardens. Abū ʿUbayda said: الروضة is what is in low ground; if it is elevated it is a تُرعة. Someone else said: a meadow is at its finest when it is in an elevated, rugged place, as al-Aʿshā said: [basīṭ] 337-
ما روضة من رياض الحزن معشبة
(No grassy meadow of the rugged uplands [is more fragrant than she].)
Except that it is not called a روضة unless there is vegetation in it; if there is no vegetation in it and it is elevated, it is a تُرعة; and other things have been said about الترعة. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «يحبرون» means "they are honoured". Al-Kisāʾī reported حبرته, that is, I honoured him and favoured him. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: it is derived from their saying على أسنانه حبرة, that is, a trace [on his teeth]; so يحبرون means the trace of bliss shows on them; and الحبر is derived from this.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: The exegetes hold that this concerns the prayers. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: its true meaning in my view is "glorify Allah in the prayers", because glorification (tasbīḥ) takes place in the prayer. It is reported from ʿIkrima that he read فسبحان الله حينا تمسون وحينا تصبحون; it is accusative as an adverbial (mafʿūl fīhi), and the meaning is: "a time in which you enter the evening and a time in which you enter the morning", so that something from the qualifying clause refers back to حين; its like in the Qurʾān is (يَوْماً لا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئاً) [al-Baqara: 48]. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the prepositions are not dropped; rather only the hāʾ is implied in it.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: (وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ): the accusative is also possible, as a maṣdar.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t: (وَمِنْ آياتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ): (أَنْ) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; likewise (أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْواجاً لِتَسْكُنُوا إِلَيْها). (وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُمْ مَوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً): it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: المودّة ("affection") is a man's love for his wife, and الرحمة ("mercy") is his mercy towards her lest harm befall her.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear His signs that point to Him: the creation of the heavens and the earth, the variety of the tongue in the mouth, the variety of languages, and the variety of colours and forms despite the great number of people, so that you hardly see anyone without being able to distinguish him from another. This is among the strongest proofs of the Disposer and Creator, because one who made something other than this would not have this differentiation in it.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: (وَمِنْ آياتِهِ أَنْ تَقُومَ السَّماءُ وَالْأَرْضُ بِأَمْرِهِ): that is, they stand without pillars by His power; He called it a "command" figuratively, as one says: "this is a great matter (amr)". On the meaning of (يَسْمَعُونَ) [Translator's note: this word belongs to the preceding verse, al-Rūm: 23] there are two views: "they accept", like his saying سمع الله لمن حمده ("Allah hears (accepts) whoever praises Him"); and the other is that among them were some who, if the Qurʾān was recited while they were present, stopped their ears so as not to hear. When He, Mighty and Majestic, had made clear the proof of Himself, He said: (ثُمَّ إِذا دَعاكُمْ دَعْوَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ إِذا أَنْتُمْ تَخْرُجُونَ), that is, the One who did these things is able to raise you. The readers agree on fatḥa on the tāʾ here in «تخرجون» [i.e. تَخرُجون], but they differ over the one in «al-Aʿrāf»: the people of Medina read (وَمِنْها تُخْرَجُونَ) [al-Aʿrāf: 25], and the people of Iraq read it with fatḥa, and Abū ʿUbayd inclines to that. The two meanings are close, except that the people of Medina distinguished between them because of the sequence of the discourse: the sequence of the discourse in the one in «al-Aʿrāf» fits better with ḍamma, since death is not their own act, and so likewise the bringing out; while fatḥa in Sūrat al-Rūm fits better with the sequence of the discourse, that is: when He calls you, you come out, that is, you obey; so the act is more appropriately attributed to them.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: Abū al-Haytham reported from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: «Every qunūt in the Qurʾān is obedience.» Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: all who are in the heavens and the earth are obedient to Him with the obedience of their submission to whatever He wills of health and sickness, wealth and poverty; this is not the obedience for which they are rewarded.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: (وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ): we have discussed it. (وَلَهُ الْمَثَلُ الْأَعْلى): that is, whatever He, Mighty and Majestic, wills comes to be. Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: المثل is the attribute.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: (شُرَكاءَ) is in the position of the nominative, and (مِنْ) is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. (فَأَنْتُمْ فِيهِ سَواءٌ): mubtadaʾ and khabar; سواء here is not the one that is an adverb. (تَخافُونَهُمْ كَخِيفَتِكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): accusative through the verb [i.e. the maṣdar]; the kāf and mīm are in the position of the genitive, and they are also in the position of the nominative by interpretation, as you say عجبت من ضربكم عمرا ("I wondered at your striking ʿAmr"). من ضربكم عمرو is also possible, because the maṣdar is annexed to the agent and to the object. You say: عجبت من وقع أنيابه بعضها على بعض ("I wondered at the striking of his canines one upon another"), and if you wish you put [بعضها] in the nominative, because أنيابه is in the position of the nominative by interpretation; but the nominative with an overt noun is ugly according to the Kufans. If you said عجبت من وقعها بعضها على بعض, the nominative would be good according to all. (كَذلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, and the implied form is: "We set out the signs in detail, a detailing like that".

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: (بَلِ اتَّبَعَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ): plural of هوى, because its origin is faʿal.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: (فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ): that is, set your direction towards the religion. (حَنِيفاً): as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «حنيفا» means a Muslim who performs the pilgrimage. He said: and (فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ) is the religion of Allah. Abū Isḥāq said: «فطرة الله» is accusative in the sense of "follow the natural disposition (fiṭra) of Allah"; he said: because the meaning of (فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ) is "follow the religion and follow the fiṭra of Allah". Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] said: «فطرة» is a maṣdar from the meaning of فأقم وجهك, because its meaning is: Allah created people upon that with a creating (fiṭra). We have discussed "the fiṭra of Allah" at greater length than this in «al-Maʿānī», and the ḥadīth «Every child is born upon the fiṭra», and the views of the jurists on it. It is said: its meaning is that he is born with the constitution that you know. And it is said: the meaning of "the fiṭra of Allah upon which He created people" is: follow the religion of Allah for which He created people. The fiṭra was called a religion because people are created for it; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (وَما خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنْسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ) [al-Dhāriyāt: 56]. And someone argued from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَها) [al-Isrāʾ: 7] [i.e. that "for it" may mean "against it"].

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: (مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ) is accusative as a ḥāl. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: because the meaning of «فأقم وجهك» is "so set your faces". This is the view of Abū Isḥāq, and he argued from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ) [al-Ṭalāq: 1]. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "so set your face, you and those with you, turning [to Him]". Abū al-ʿAbbās rejected the view of whoever said the implied form is "they do not know, turning [to Him]", because the meaning of منيبين is "returning", so how could it be "they do not know, returning"? Moreover, after it comes (وَاتَّقُوهُ); its meaning is only: "so set your faces and fear Him (وَلا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ)".

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (مِنَ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ): ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, Abū Hurayra and Abū Umāma, may Allah have mercy on them both, interpreted it as referring to the people of the qibla [the Muslims]. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: those who divided their religion are the People of the Book. وفارقوا دينهم [the variant reading] means they abandoned their religion which they ought to follow, namely tawḥīd. (وَكانُوا شِيَعاً): that is, factions. (كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ): it is said: they rejoice because they have not discerned the truth, though they are obliged to discern it. It is said: this was before the proofs became manifest. A third view is that one who disobeys Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may rejoice in his disobedience, and likewise Satan, highway robbers and others; and Allah knows best. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the complete stop may be at «ولا تكونوا من المشركين», the meaning [continuing] «من الذين فارقوا دينهم» (وَكانُوا شِيَعاً) as a new sentence (resumptive), and that it may also be connected to what precedes it. Abū Jaʿfar said: if it is connected to what precedes it, then according to the Basrans it is a badal with the repetition of the preposition, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ) [al-Aʿrāf: 75]; and had it been without the preposition, it would be permissible.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: (دَعَوْا رَبَّهُمْ مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ): as a ḥāl. From Ibn ʿAbbās: that is, turning to Him with all their hearts.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: (لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهُمْ): the lām of purpose (lām kay). It is also said: it is the lām of command carrying the sense of threat, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (فَمَنْ شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِنْ وَمَنْ شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ) [al-Kahf: 29], and as you say: "speak to so-and-so, until we see what befalls you from me". Likewise (فَتَمَتَّعُوا); and what indicates that is (فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ).

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: (أَمْ أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطاناً): a question carrying the sense of making them stop and acknowledge (tawqīf). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «سلطانا», that is, a book. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the Arabs make السلطان feminine, saying قضت به عليك السلطان ("the authority [fem.] decreed it against you"). As for the Basrans, the masculine is more eloquent in their view, and the Qurʾān came with it; the feminine is permissible in their view because it means "proof (ḥujja)". Our saying سلطان means "one who has authority", that is, one who has the proof. However, Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said otherwise, in what ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān reported to us from him; he said: سلطان is the plural of سليط, as you say رغيف and رغفان; so its masculine is according to the sense of "all" and its feminine according to the sense of "group".

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: (وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ): the implied form according to Sībawayh is قنطوا ("they despaired"); that is why it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: (فَآتِ ذَا الْقُرْبى حَقَّهُ): Mujāhid and Qatāda interpreted it as a man's relative, and made maintaining kinship ties an obligation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so much so that Mujāhid said: charity is not accepted from anyone while his kin are in need. And it is said: ذو القربى is kinship with the Prophet ﷺ, and his due is made clear in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما غَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي الْقُرْبى) [al-Anfāl: 41]. «وابن السبيل» ("the wayfarer") is the guest, so He made hospitality an obligation. (فَأُولئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ, (هُمُ) a second mubtadaʾ, (الْمُضْعِفُونَ) the khabar of the second, and the clause is the khabar of the first. There are two views on the meaning of المضعفين: one is that good deeds are multiplied for them; the other is that good and bliss have been multiplied for them, that is, they are possessors of multiples, as one says فلان مقو, that is, he has strong companions [or mounts]; and one says فلان رديء مردئ, that is, he is bad in himself and his companions are bad.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
(فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ): the hāʾ was dropped from بضع to distinguish masculine from feminine. The nūn of سنين was given fatḥa because it is a sound plural. Some Arabs say في بضعِ سنينٍ [with the nūn inflected], as they say من غسلينٍ. If that is permissible, [it is because] سنة was given a plural with wāw and nūn and yāʾ and nūn because something was dropped from it, and this plural was made a compensation. The sīn was given kasra, whereas it had fatḥa in سنة, because the kasra was made an indication that it is a plural formed otherwise than it should be. This is the view of the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ would be obliged to give it ḍamma, except that he says: the ḍamma is an indication of the wāw; and a wāw was dropped from سنة according to one of the two views, yet no one we know gives it ḍamma. (لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ): one also says من قبلٍ ومن بعدٍ. Al-Kisāʾī reported from some of the Banū Asad: (لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلٍ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ) [Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowelling; the description that follows fixes the forms], the first genitive with tanwīn and the second with ḍamma without tanwīn. Al-Farrāʾ reported «من قبلِ ومن بعدِ», both genitive without tanwīn. Al-Farrāʾ has, in this section of his book on the Qurʾān, many things in which the error is plain. Among them: he claimed that «من قبلِ ومن بعدِ» is permissible, as the poet said: [majzūʾ al-kāmil] 332-
إلّا علالة أو بداهة ... سابح نهد الجزاره
(Except for the second run or the first burst of a swift steed, stout of limb.)
And as he said: [munsariḥ] 333-
يا من رأى عارضا أكفكفه ... بين ذراعي وجبهة الأسد
(O who has seen a cloud I keep watching, between the Forearms and the Forehead of the Lion [i.e. the lunar mansions].)
The error in this is plain, because the Qurʾān does not have لله الأمر من قبلِ ومن بعدِ ذلك, so that it would be like his saying «بين ذراعي وجبهة الأسد». Do you not see that you say أخذته بنصف وربع الدرهم ("I bought it for a half and a quarter of the dirham"), but it is not permissible to say أخذته بنصف وربع [with neither annexed]; and you say قطع الله يد ورجل زيد ("may Allah cut off the hand and foot of Zayd"), but it is not permissible to say يد ورجل [alone]. Moreover, this too is not common in the speech of the Arabs, and the Book of Allah is only interpreted according to what is common and eloquent; it is not permissible to make an analogy on it with what does not resemble it. If you said اشتريت دار وغلام عمرو ("I bought the house and the slave of ʿAmr"), it would not be permissible according to anyone we know. Among them [his errors]: he claimed that من قبلِ ومن بعدِ is permissible while you intend the annexation. This undoes the whole chapter, because the ḍamma was in it only because of the absence of the annexation while intending it; so if you put it in the genitive while intending it, the speech contradicts itself. «من قبلٍ ومن بعدٍ» is only permissible on the basis that they are both indefinite. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "from something earlier and from something later". Among them: he likened من قبل ومن بعد to their saying من علُ, and recited: [rajaz] 334-
إن تأت من تحت أجئها من عل
(If you come from below, I will come at her from above.)
But من قبل ومن بعد are not of the type of من عل. Sībawayh said: they did not make vowelless, among nouns, what resembles the fully declinable noun, nor what has been put in a position like that of the non-declinable. What resembles [the declinable] is «من علُ», which they gave a vowel because they say من علٍ; as for the declinable noun that has been treated like the non-declinable, it is their saying ابدأ بهذا أولُ ("begin with this first") and يا حكمُ ("O Ḥakam"). Do you not see that Sībawayh, by his precision [Translator's note: the source has «لحذفه», likely for لحذقه, "his skill"], distinguished between «من عل» and «أول»? Then al-Farrāʾ came and combined them, and recited what we have mentioned, and recited: [ṭawīl] 335-
فو الله ما أدري وإنّي لأوجل ... على أيّنا تعدو المنيّة أوّل
(By Allah, I do not know — and I am fearful — upon which of us death will first descend.)
So he mixed them all in the chapter and brought both of them under «قبل وبعد», though one of them differs from قبل وبعد.
As for the discussion of قبل and بعد according to the doctrine of Sībawayh and of the Basrans: their way is not to be inflected, because the annexed-to noun and the annexation had been dropped from them, so they became definite without a means of definiteness, and their full declinability departed. They could not be left without a vowel because they had been declinable, so ḍamma was chosen for them, because genitive and accusative can reach them by right of inflection, so they were given a vowel other than those two, and they were given ḍamma. However, Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: since they are both "limits" (ghāya), they were given what is the furthest (ghāya) of the vowels. (وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): there are two views on its meaning. One is that they rejoice at the Romans' victory over Persia, because the Romans are People of the Book and so nearer to the Muslims than the idolaters. The other view, which is more fitting, is that their joy is only at the fulfilment of the promise of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, since there was in it a proof of the prophethood, because He, Mighty and Majestic, announced what would happen within a few years, and it happened.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
(ظَهَرَ الْفَسادُ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ بِما كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ): there are two views on its meaning. One is: drought appeared on land, that is, in the deserts, and he read it: "and in the sea", that is, in the cities of the sea, like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82]; that is: scarcity of rain and high prices appeared because of the sins that people's hands have earned, so that He might make them taste the punishment of some of what they did; then [this] was omitted. The other view is that the meaning of (ظَهَرَ الْفَسادُ) is: sins appeared — highway robbery and oppression — and this is corruption in the true sense; the first is figurative. But on the second answer there is an ellipsis and abridgement in the discourse, indicated by what follows it; the meaning would be: sins appeared on land and sea, so Allah withheld the rain from them and made their prices high, in order to make them taste the punishment of some of what they did (لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ). Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind reported from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās: «لعلهم يرجعون» means "so that they may repent".
As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (وَما آتَيْتُمْ مِنْ رِباً لِيَرْبُوَا فِي أَمْوالِ) [al-Rūm: 39], we have mentioned the view of the scholars on it: that it is a man giving another man a gift, intending a return for it and not intending reward [from Allah]; that is permitted, except that he is not rewarded for it, because he did not intend by it the reward of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. However, al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the Prophet ﷺ in particular was forbidden that, by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (لا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ) [al-Muddaththir: 6]. And it is said: the meaning of "whatever you give of ribā" is the ribā that is not lawful; the holder of this view said: the meaning of "it does not increase with Allah" is that it is not adjudged to the one who takes it, because it is not his, but belongs to the one from whom it was taken. The dual of الربا is ربوان; so says Sībawayh, and nothing else is permissible according to his followers. I heard Abū Isḥāq say, mentioning the view of the Kufans: it is not enough for them, in saying ربيان, that they err in orthography by writing الربا with yāʾ; they even err in the dual — and he considered this serious. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: (لِيَرْبُوَا فِي أَمْوالِ النَّاسِ), and this makes it clearer that it is a wāw-final root, and that the view is as Abū Isḥāq said.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: (مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا مَرَدَّ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ): that is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not turn it away from them, and if He does not turn it away, no one is able to repel it. According to grammarians other than Sībawayh «لا مردٌّ له» [with nominative and tanwīn] is permissible, but according to Sībawayh that is far-fetched unless there is a conjunction in the discourse. (يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ): the original is يتصدّعون; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād because of their closeness. One says تصدّع القوم when people disperse; and from it الصّداع ("headache") is derived, because it splits apart the parts of the head.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: (كانَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنا): the khabar of كان. (نَصْرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): its noun. Had it been outside the Qurʾān, it would have been permissible to put حقّ in the nominative and نصر in the accusative, because حقّا, though indefinite, is followed by علينا; and it would have been permissible to put both in the nominative, by implying [a pronoun of the matter] in كان with the khabar being the clause. In the ḥadīth: «Whoever defends the honour of his companion, Allah will turn the fire of Hell away from him»; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited (وَكانَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنا نَصْرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ).

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: (وَيَجْعَلُهُ كِسَفاً): plural of كسفة, which is a piece. In the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj it is كِسْفا with sukūn on the sīn; it too is a plural of كسفة, as one says سدرة and سدر. On this reading the pronoun after it refers back to it, that is: "and you see the rain coming out from between the pieces", because every plural that differs from its singular only by the hāʾ may well be treated as masculine. Whoever reads كِسَفا, the pronoun refers in his view to the clouds [Translator's note: the source has «الحساب», read as السحاب]. In the reading of al-Ḍaḥḥāk: فترى الودق يخرج من خلله ("from its gap"); and خلال may be the plural of خلل.

nahhas-irab:49-50.t:
(وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ) (49) (فَانْظُرْ إِلى آثارِ رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها إِنَّ ذلِكَ لَمُحْيِ الْمَوْتى وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (50)
(وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ): we have discussed it. Abū Isḥāq held that it is for emphasis, and said that Quṭrub's view that the implied form is "before the sending down" is wrong, because the rain is inseparable from the sending down. He recited: [ṭawīl] 338-
مشين كما اهتزّت رماح تسفّهت ... أغاليها مرّ الرّياح النّواسم
(They walked, swaying as spears sway whose tops are tossed by the passing of gentle winds.)
He made المرّ ("passing") feminine [in تسفّهت] because the winds are inseparable from it, and because the meaning is "the winds tossed their tops"; so likewise the meaning of «من قبل أن ينزل عليهم المطر» is "before the rain". One says آثر and إثر. (كَيْفَ يُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ): assimilation is not permissible in it, lest two vowelless letters come together.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: (وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنا رِيحاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا): it is said: the implied form is "they saw the crops turning yellow"; it is said: "they saw the clouds"; and it is said: "they saw the wind", الريح being made masculine because what is meant is the one sent of it. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: there is nothing to prevent making masculine any noun of unreal femininity, such as أعجبني الدار ("the house pleased me") and the like. (لَظَلُّوا): al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: its meaning is ليظلّنّ ("they would surely remain"). Abū Isḥāq said: this is permissible because there is the sense of requital (mujāzāh) in the discourse.

nahhas-irab:52-53.t: (فَإِنَّكَ لا تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتى وَلا تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ الدُّعاءَ): they were put in the position of the dead and the deaf because they do not benefit from what they hear. (وَما أَنْتَ بِهادِي الْعُمْيِ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ): al-Farrāʾ said: من ضلالتهم is also possible, in the sense of "you cannot hold them back from their misguidance"; and عن in the sense of "you cannot turn them away from their misguidance".

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: (اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ ضَعْفٍ): ʿAṭiyya reported from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: I recited to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ «من ضَعف», and he said to me: (مِنْ ضَعْفٍ) [i.e. ضُعف]. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read (مِنْ ضَعْفٍ) [i.e. ضُعُف], and the Kufans read (مِنْ ضَعْفٍ), which is the maṣdar [Translator's note: the source prints all the forms with the same vowelling; the vowels given here follow the known readings: Ḥamza and Shuʿba ضَعف, the rest ضُعف]. The grammarians among them allowed من ضَعَف, and likewise every word in which a guttural letter is second or third. Abū Isḥāq said: its interpretation is: Allah is He who created you from the sperm-drop, your state with which is weakness; then after weakness He made youth.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: (وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يُقْسِمُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ ما لَبِثُوا غَيْرَ ساعَةٍ): there is no rejection of the punishment of the grave in this, since it has been authenticated from the Prophet ﷺ through more than one chain that he sought refuge from it and commanded that refuge be sought from it. Among that is what ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd narrated: he ﷺ heard Umm Ḥabība saying: "O Allah, let me enjoy my husband the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, my father Abū Sufyān and my brother Muʿāwiya." The Prophet ﷺ said to her: «You have asked Allah about appointed lifespans and allotted provisions; rather ask Him to protect you from the punishment of Hell or the punishment of the grave», among well-known ḥadīths. On the meaning of (ما لَبِثُوا غَيْرَ ساعَةٍ) there are two views. The first is that it means there must be a stillness before the Day of Resurrection, and the annihilation decreed upon creation overtakes both those shown mercy and those punished; on this basis they said "we remained only an hour", because they did not know [Translator's note: the source has «يعملوا», read as يعلموا] its extent. The other view is that they mean in this world, because of its passing away and coming to an end, even though they swore about the unseen and about what they did not know. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (كَذلِكَ كانُوا يُؤْفَكُونَ), that is, thus they used to lie in this world. A group of the theologians (ahl al-naẓar) claimed that there cannot be lying at the Resurrection because of the state they are in, but the Qurʾān indicates otherwise. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (كَذلِكَ كانُوا يُؤْفَكُونَ), and He, exalted be His praise, said: (يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعاً فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ أَلا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْكاذِبُونَ) [al-Mujādila: 18].

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: The believers answered them, saying: (لَقَدْ لَبِثْتُمْ فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ إِلى يَوْمِ الْبَعْثِ). Abū Isḥāq said: that is, in the Preserved Tablet. Yaʿqūb reported from one of the readers «إلى يوم البَعَث» [Translator's note: the variant vowelling is not shown in the source; by the following remark it is البَعَث with fatḥa on the ʿayn]; this is a word containing a guttural letter.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: (فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يَنْفَعُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مَعْذِرَتُهُمْ): when the believers answered them, they asked to return to this world and offered excuses, but they were not excused. (وَلا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ): nor is their state that of one who is asked to make amends and so returns.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
(وَلَقَدْ ضَرَبْنا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هذَا الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ وَلَئِنْ جِئْتَهُمْ بِآيَةٍ لَيَقُولَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلاَّ مُبْطِلُونَ) (58)
(وَلَقَدْ ضَرَبْنا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هذَا الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ): [parables] that guide them to what they need.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: An emphatic maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object). Abū Isḥāq said: (وَعْدُ اللَّهِ) in the nominative is also possible, in the sense of "that is the promise of Allah". (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): they are the disbelievers, and they are the majority.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: (وَلا يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ) is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition; it was emphasised with the heavy nūn and so made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, as two things are made indeclinable when one is joined to the other. (الَّذِينَ لا يُوقِنُونَ) is in the position of the nominative; some Arabs say الذّون in the nominative position.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: (يَعْلَمُونَ ظاهِراً مِنَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): then He made clear what they are ignorant of by His saying: (وَهُمْ عَنِ الْآخِرَةِ هُمْ غافِلُونَ). The first «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the second is a second mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the first; there is a sense of emphasis in the discourse. The second «هم» may also be a badal (substitute) for the first, as you say رأيته إياه ("I saw him, him"); there is also a sense of emphasis in the discourse.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ بِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكافِرُونَ): the lām is for emphasis, and the implied form is لكافرون بلقاء ربّهم, by fronting and postponing. On this basis you say: إنّ زيدا في الدار لجالس ("Zayd is in the house, sitting indeed"); and if you said إنّ زيدا لفي الدار لجالس, it would be permissible. But if you said إنّ زيدا جالس لفي الدار, it would not be permissible, because the lām is brought only to emphasise the noun and khabar of إنّ, so once you have brought them [without it], it is not permissible to bring it.
