Likewise if you said إنّ زيدا لجالس لفي الدار, it would not be permissible.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: (وَأَثارُوا الْأَرْضَ): because the people of Mecca were not people of tillage [Translator's note: the source has «حرب» ("war"), likely for حرث ("tillage"); translated according to the context].

nahhas-meani:1-3.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤـمۤ. غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ فِيۤ أَدْنَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ [verses 1–3].
Mujāhid said: It is al-Jazīra (Upper Mesopotamia), which was the land of the Romans closest to Persia.
Muḥammad ibn Salama al-Aswānī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Sanjar narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abū Isḥāq al-Fazārī narrated to us, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī ʿAmra, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿الۤـمۤ. غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ﴾: he said: The idolaters liked "Persia" to prevail over "the Romans", because they [the Persians] were idol-worshippers, and the Muslims liked "the Romans" to prevail over "Persia", because they were People of the Book. This was mentioned to Abū Bakr, and Abū Bakr mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Indeed, they will prevail. He said: Abū Bakr mentioned it to them, and they said: Set a term between us and you; if we prevail, we get such-and-such, and if you prevail, you get such-and-such. So he set a term of five years, and they did not prevail. That was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: [Why did you not make it up to less than — I think he said: less than ten?] Saʿīd said: al-biḍʿ is what is less than ten.
Then the Romans prevailed after that, and that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤـمۤ. غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ فِيۤ أَدْنَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ المُؤْمِنونَ بَنَصْرِ اللهِ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: Gambling was lawful at that time. He said: And the Prophet ﷺ said to Abū Bakr: How much is al-biḍʿ? He said: From three to nine.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar read ﴿غَلَبَتِ الرُّومُ﴾ with fatḥa on the ghayn and the lām, and said: they prevailed over the nearest countryside.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning according to the reading of those who read ﴿غُلِبَتِ ٱلرُّومُ وَهُم مِّن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ﴾ is: the Romans, after their defeat — that is, after they were defeated — will prevail.
And whoever reads ﴿سَيُغْلَبونَ﴾, the meaning for him is: and Persia, after their victory — that is, after they had prevailed — will be defeated.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ﴾.
Al-biḍʿ according to Qatāda is more than three and less than ten.
According to al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ: what is less than ten.
According to Abū ʿUbayda: between three and five.
Abū Zayd reported baḍʿ, and it is derived from their saying baḍḍaʿahu when he cut it into pieces; from it comes baḍʿa of meat (a piece of meat), and from it: "he possesses the buḍʿ of the woman", which is only a euphemism for her private part.
In the narration of Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فِي أَدْنَى الأَرْضِ﴾, he said, he says: at the edge of Syria (al-Shām).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied wording (taqdīr) is: in the nearest land to Persia.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِلَّهِ ٱلأَمْرُ مِن قَبْلُ وَمِن بَعْدُ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: When you say ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ and ﴿مِنْ بعدُ﴾, its meaning is: before what you know and after what you know, and before everything and after everything.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is: to Allah belongs the decree of victory, before the victory and after it.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ بِنَصْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is, they will rejoice at Allah's helping the Romans — because they are People of a Book — against Persia, who are Magians; and they will rejoice at the mighty sign which none but Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knows, because He informed them of what would come to pass.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ ظَاهِراً مِّنَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلآخِرَةِ هُمْ غَافِلُونَ﴾.
ʿIkrima and Ibrāhīm said: that is, they know the affairs of their livelihood and the interests of their worldly life.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُواْ فِيۤ أَنفُسِهِمْ مَّا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
That is, except to establish the truth.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَثَارُواْ ٱلأَرْضَ وَعَمَرُوهَآ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا عَمَرُوهَا﴾.
﴿وَأَثَارُواْ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾ means they ploughed it and sowed it, whereas in Mecca there is no ploughing and no sowing.
And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿تُثِيرُ الأَرْضَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ عَاقِبَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَاءُواْ ٱلسُّوۤءَىٰ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash read: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ عَاقِبَةَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوا السُّوءُ﴾, with السُّوءُ in the nominative.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-sūʾ is the worst of evil, and al-sūʾā is the fuʿlā form of it.
It has also been said: ﴿ٱلسُّوۤءَىٰ﴾ here is the Fire, just as al-ḥusnā is Paradise.
The meaning of ﴿أَسَاءُوا﴾ here is: they associated partners [with Allah]; this is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أَن كَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Al-Kisāʾī said: that is, because they denied the signs of Allah.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ يُبْلِسُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: they will be dejected.
Abū Yaḥyā related from Mujāhid, who said: al-iblās is disgrace.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said أَبْلَسَ الرجلُ when a man is bewildered and grieved, and his argument fails him so that he cannot find his way to it, and he despairs of good, as [the poet] said:
* "قَالَ نَعَمْ أَعرِفُه وَأَبْلَسَا" *
(He said: Yes, I know it — and fell dumbfounded.)

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ فَهُمْ فِي رَوْضَةٍ يُحْبَرُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿يُحْبَرونَ﴾ means they are made to enjoy bliss.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its literal sense is that the traces of blessing become visible on them.
From that comes al-ḥabr, and "on his teeth is a ḥabra (a stain)".
Al-Awzāʿī related from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr: ﴿فِي رَوْضَةٍ يُحْبَرُونَ﴾, he said: listening [to song] in Paradise.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ ٱللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The five prayers are in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; and he recited the verse: ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ ٱللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ﴾, he said: Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ; ﴿وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ﴾, he said: Fajr; ﴿وَعَشِيَّاً﴾: ʿAṣr; ﴿وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُون﴾: Ẓuhr.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُخْرِجُ ٱلْحَيَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَيِّتِ وَيُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَيِّتَ مِنَ ٱلْحَيِّ وَيُحْيِي ٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَكَذَلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ﴾.
There are several views on its meaning:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: that is, He brings the sperm-drop out of the man, and the man out of the sperm-drop.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: And likewise the egg.
Salmān said: He brings the believer out of the unbeliever and the unbeliever out of the believer; and al-Ḥasan said the same.
It has also been said: He causes the living to die and gives life to the dead.
﴿وَيُحْيِي ٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَكَذَلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ﴾,
that is, just as He gives life to the earth with plants.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن تُرَابٍ﴾.
The meaning is: that He created your origin, who is "Adam", peace be upon him, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ الْقَرَْيَةَ﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. with the muḍāf omitted].
It is also possible that the [seminal] fluid is created from dust.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً لِّتَسْكُنُوۤاْ إِلَيْهَا﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: that Eve was created from Adam.
The other: that the meaning is: He created for you mates of your own kind, because a human being is more at ease with his own kind and finds more repose in it. Similar to it is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسِ وَاحِدَةٍ وَجَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا لِيَسْكُنَ إلَيْهَا﴾.
Both views apply to its meaning.
That is, He made from its kind its mate; and this points to both sexes together. The pronoun in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿جَعَلاَ لَهُ شُرَكَاءَ فِيمَا آتَاهُمَا﴾ would then refer to the two sexes, and the pronoun in His saying ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ refers to the two sexes because they are a multitude.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: affection (al-mawadda) is intercourse, and mercy (al-raḥma) is the child.
It has also been said: affection and mercy are the inclining of their hearts towards one another.
And the meaning is: and among His signs that point to His oneness, and that He has no partner and no equal.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
﴿ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ means for the jinn and mankind.
And ﴿ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ has also been reported, and it is good.
[Translator's note: the second word is printed with the same vowelling as the first; the reported variant is evidently لِلْعالِمِين ("for those who know"), with kasra on the lām.]

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ ٱلْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً﴾.
The meaning is: and He shows you the lightning, [which is] among His signs; one clause is conjoined to another.
It is also possible that the meaning is: and among His signs is a sign by which He shows you the lightning, as the poet said:
وَمَا الدَّهْرُ إلاَّ تَارَتَانِ فمنهما * أَمُوتُ وأُخْرَى أَبْتَغِي العَيْشَ أَكْدَحُ
(Time is nothing but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek a living, toiling.)
[Translator's note: the verse is cited for an omitted noun after «فمنهما», i.e. "of them is [a time in which] I die".]
The fear is for the traveller, and the hope is for the one at home.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَن تَقُومَ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلأَرْضُ بِأَمْرِهِ﴾.
That is, that the two of them remain standing.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَهُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ كُلٌّ لَّهُ قَانِتُونَ﴾.
This too is among His signs, and [the words "among His signs"] were omitted because there is an indication of them in the context.
Al-qānit is the one who stands in obedience.
And the standing here is submission to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, whether the servants like it or dislike it.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَبْدَأُ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
There are three views on its meaning:
a- In the narration of Ṣāliḥ from Ibn Anas: ﴿وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيهِ﴾ means it is easier for the created being, because He began its creation from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, whereas the restoration is by His saying to it ﴿كَنْ فَيكُونُ﴾; and that is easier for the created being.
[Translator's note: «ابن انس» is as written in the source; this explanation is usually reported via Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās.]
b- Mujāhid said: The restoration is easier for Him than the beginning, and all of it is easy for Him.
The meaning on this view is: it is easier for Him in your estimation and in terms of what you know, by way of comparison; and after it comes ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ﴾.
c- Qatāda said: ﴿وَهُوَ أَهْوْنُ عَلَيْهِ﴾ means it is easy. This is a good view; from it is "Allāhu akbar", meaning great (kabīr), and from it is the poet's saying:
لَعَمْرُكَ مَا أَدْرِي وَإنَّي لأَوْجَلُ * عَلَى أَيِّنَا تَعْدُو المَنِيَّةُ أَوَّلُ
(By your life, I do not know — and I am indeed afraid — upon which of us death will fall first.)
And the saying of the other:
إنَّ الَّذِي سَمَك السَّماءَ بنى لَنَا * بَيْتَاً دَعَائِمُهُ أعزُّ وأَطْوَلُ
(He who raised up the sky built for us a house whose pillars are mighty and tall.)
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿وهو هيِّنٌ عليه﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He is saying ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ﴾.
It has also been said: it means "there is no god but Allah".
Its literal sense in the language is: and to Him belongs the highest description.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ضَرَبَ لَكُمْ مَّثَلاً مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: This is a parable that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, struck for the idolaters, saying: ﴿هَلْ لَّكُمْ مِّن مَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ مِّن شُرَكَآءَ فِي مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ فَأَنتُمْ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌ﴾, that is, would any of you be content for his slave to be like him in his wealth and his person? If you are not content with this, how then have you assigned a partner to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He?
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view; that is, would any of you be content to make his slave like himself — that is, like his free partner, without whom he settles no matter? As He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَلْمِزُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾, that is, let none of you find fault with another.
So too His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿كَخِيفَتِكُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ﴾; and as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَوْلاَ إذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ المُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتُ بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ خَيْرَاً﴾; and as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾.
It has also been said: as its spending is feared from your side.
That is, you do not make your slaves like yourselves, while all of you are slaves of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; how then do you assign to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, a partner, when there is nothing like Him?

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفاً فِطْرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا﴾.
Al-fiṭra is the beginning of creation; from it comes ﴿فَاطِرُ السَّمَواتِ﴾, and from it "the camel's canine tooth faṭara (broke through)", and from it "faṭartu the well", that is, I began digging it.
That is, He began their creation on the basis that they know they have a Creator and a Disposer.
In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Every child is born upon the fiṭra, until his parents are the ones who make him a Jew or make him a Christian."
Al-Awzāʿī and Ḥammād ibn Salama said: This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَإذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَتَهُمْ﴾.
The meaning on this view is: every child is born upon the covenant that was taken from him.
And in the ḥadīth: "He brought them out like tiny ants and took the covenant from them." So every child is born upon that covenant — even if he ascribes his worship to other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, or describes Him with other than His attribute — until his parents teach him Judaism and Christianity.
It has also been said: upon the natural constitution that you know, distinguishing nothing.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak said: This is for whoever will be a Muslim;
he holds that it is specific.
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This was before the obligations were revealed and jihad was commanded.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting of them is the first view; it is the view of the people of the Sunna, and it agrees with the language.
It cannot be abrogated, because it is a report, nor can it be specific. The meaning of the ḥadīth only became problematic because they interpreted "al-fiṭra" as Islam, whereas it is only the beginning of creation.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَلاَ تَكُونُواْ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾.
﴿مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ﴾ means returning to Him in obedience.
And the meaning is: so set your faces, turning [to Him] (munībīna).
[Translator's note: i.e. ﴿مُنِيبِينَ﴾ is ḥāl (circumstantial) to the plural subject understood in ﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ﴾ of verse 30.]
And the meaning of ﴿كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾
is: each says, "I am upon guidance."

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلنَّاسَ ضُرٌّ دَعَوْاْ رَبَّهُمْ مُّنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
That is, they sought refuge with none but Him, and abandoned what they used to worship besides Him.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَكْفُرُواْ بِمَآ آتَيْنَاهُمْ فَتَمَتَّعُواْ فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
So He moved from the report [in the third person] to direct address; and this is by way of threat and warning, as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُلِ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَمَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِنْ وَمَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَاناً فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِمَا كَانُواْ بِهِ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Every sulṭān in the Qurʾan is an excuse and a proof."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is: or have We sent down to them a book in which there is an excuse, or a proof, or evidence, that directs them to associating partners?

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَآ أَذَقْنَا ٱلنَّاسَ رَحْمَةً فَرِحُواْ بِهَا﴾.
That is, a blessing, they rejoice in it.
﴿وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ﴾, that is, and if a misfortune befalls them.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَآتِ ذَا ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ حَقَّهُ وَٱلْمِسْكِينَ وَٱبْنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
Qatāda said: If you do not give to your kinsman and walk to him on your own feet, you have cut him off.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ آتَيْتُمْ مِّن رِّباً لِّيَرْبُوَ فِي أَمْوَالِ ٱلنَّاسِ فَلاَ يَرْبُو عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid and Ibn ʿAbbās said: It is the man who gives a gift to another man and seeks something better than it in return; he has no reward for it, and no sin upon him.
ʿIkrima said: Ribā is of two kinds: a lawful ribā and an unlawful ribā. As for the lawful, it is that a man gives another something so that he will give him more than it; this does not increase with Allah. The unlawful is in deferment (al-nasīʾa).
Ibrāhīm said: This was in the Jāhiliyya: a man would give his kinsman wealth so that it would multiply with him; it does not increase with Allah.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ آتَيْتُمْ مِّن زَكَاةٍ تُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُضْعِفُونَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿مِّن زَكَاةٍ﴾ means of charity.
Then He said ﴿فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُضْعِفُونَ﴾, that is, those who find manifold of that, that is, possessors of multiplication, as you say: rajulun muqwin, that is, a man possessing strength.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ظَهَرَ ٱلْفَسَادُ فِي ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي ٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فِي ٱلْبَرِّ﴾: the son of Adam's killing of his brother; ﴿وَٱلْبَحْرِ﴾: the seizing of the ship by force.
ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: the land is the deserts, and the sea is the towns.
Qatāda said: And the corruption is shirk (associating partners).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied wording on this view is: and in the places of the sea, that is, those lying on the sea.
The best that has been said about this verse — and Allah knows best — is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās. Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ظَهَرَ ٱلْفَسَادُ فِي ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ﴾:
he says: the diminishing of blessing because of the deeds of the servants, so that they may repent.
The meaning on this view is: drought has appeared on land and sea because of people's sins.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينَ ٱلْقِيِّمِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لاَّ مَرَدَّ لَهُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ﴾.
That is, direct your aim to the upright religion before the Day of Resurrection comes, when no soul's faith will benefit it if it had not believed before.
The meaning of ﴿يَصَّدَّعُونَ﴾ is: they will be divided, a party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحاً فَلأَنفُسِهِمْ يَمْهَدُونَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿فَلأَنفُسِهِمْ يَمْهَدُونَ﴾: in the grave.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of ﴿يَمْهَدُونَ﴾ in the language is: they smooth [a place] for themselves by good works; from al-mihād, which is the bed.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُهُ كِسَفاً فَتَرَى ٱلْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلاَلِهِ﴾.
﴿وَيَجْعَلُهُ كِسَفاً﴾: [kisaf is] the plural of kisfa, which is a piece.
﴿فَتَرَى ٱلْوَدْقَ﴾: Mujāhid said: that is, the rain. ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلاَلِهِ﴾, that is, from between the clouds.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ﴾.
On the repetition of ﴿قَبْلِ﴾ here there are three views:
a- Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: This is by way of tawkīd (emphasis), and most of the grammarians hold this view.
b- Quṭrub said: that is, though they were, before the sending down, before the rain…
c- The third view is, in my opinion, the best of them: that the meaning is "before the clouds", that is, before seeing the clouds, they were despairing; and the clouds have been mentioned before.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰ آثَارِ رَحْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْيِيِ ٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَآ﴾.
﴿رَحْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: that is, the rain is of Allah's mercy. ﴿كَيْفَ يُحْيِيِ ٱلأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَآ﴾.
Muḥammad al-Yamānī read: ﴿كَيْفَ تُحْيى الأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا﴾.
The meaning according to his reading is: how the mercy gives life to the earth, or the traces [do so].
And ﴿يُحْيِي﴾ with yāʾ means: Allah gives life, or the rain, or the trace — for whoever reads it thus.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنَا رِيحاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرّاً لَّظَلُّواْ مِن بَعْدِهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾.
The grammarians said: ﴿فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرّاً﴾ means they saw the vegetation yellowed; its literal sense is: they saw the trace yellowed. ﴿لَّظَلُّواْ مِن بَعْدِهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ means layaẓallunna (they would surely remain); this is the view of al-Khalīl.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This occurs with the particles of condition (ḥurūf al-mujāzāt).

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنَّكَ لاَ تُسْمِعُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَلاَ تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوْاْ مُدْبِرِينَ﴾.
That is, they are in the position of the dead and the deaf, because they do not accept, owing to their obstinacy.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن تُسْمِعُ إِلاَّ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِآيَاتِنَا فَهُمْ مُّسْلِمُونَ﴾.
That is, you make none hear except one who is receptive, not obstinate.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن ضَعْفٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةٍ﴾.
﴿خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن ضَعْفٍ﴾ means from semen.
﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةٍ﴾ means youth.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ يُقْسِمُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ مَا لَبِثُواْ غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ﴾.
That is, they swear that they remained in the graves no more than a single hour.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ كَانُواْ يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾.
That is, thus they used to lie in this world.
It is said أُفِكَ الرَّجُل when a man is turned away from truth and good; and arḍun maʾfūka is land withheld from rain.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْعِلْمَ وَٱلإِيمَانَ لَقَدْ لَبِثْتُمْ فِي كِتَابِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْبَعْثِ﴾.
It has been said: the meaning is: according to the report of the Book of Allah, you remained in your graves until the Day of Resurrection.
It has also been said: there is a fronting and deferring (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the wording,
and the meaning is: and those who were given knowledge in the Book of Allah said: you have remained until the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلاَ يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُوقِنُونَ﴾.
﴿وَلاَ يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ﴾ means let them not provoke you; ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُوقِنُونَ﴾ means those who doubt.

safi-cedvel:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
((الفاء) resumptive (أمّا) a particle of condition and elaboration (الذين) a relative noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis of أمّا (في روضة) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ هم [Note: or attached to (يحبرون), the clause يحبرون being the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).], and the (الواو) in (يحبرون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «الذين آمنوا..» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين)).
The clause «عملوا..» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the ṣila clause).
The clause «هم في روضة..» is in the position of a nominative (khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين)).
The clause «يحبرون..» is in the position of a nominative (a second khabar).
(16) (الواو) a conjunction (أمّا الذين كفروا ... ) like أمّا الذين آمنوا (بآياتنا) attached to (كذّبوا), (الفاء) the connective of the apodosis (في العذاب) attached to (محضرون), the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause الذين آمنوا ...).
The clause «كفروا..» has no grammatical position (ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين)).
The clause «كذّبوا ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the ṣila clause).
The clause «أولئك.. محضرون» is in the position of a nominative (khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين)).

* Morphology:
(روضة): a name for a garden or for Paradise; its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- Singing in Paradise:
It is related on the authority of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a gathering of the ḥūr al-ʿīn (the wide-eyed maidens), who raise their voices in a way the creatures have never heard the like of. They say: We are the everlasting, so we do not perish; we are the blissful, so we never despair; we are the content, so we are never displeased; blessed is the one who is for us and for whom we are.."

safi-cedvel:17-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (سبحان) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, accusative (حين) an accusative adverbial attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) سبحان in the three places; the two verbs (تمسون, تصبحون) are complete verbs, that is, "you enter the evening and the morning", (الواو) parenthetical (له) attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) fronted for the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الحمد) (في السموات) attached to الحمد [Note: al-ʿUkbarī attached it to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الحمد, but the operator in it is weak.], (عشيّا) an accusative adverbial attached to سبحان, so it is conjoined to حين (من الميّت) attached to the first (يخرج) (من الحيّ) attached to the second (يخرج) (بعد) an accusative adverbial attached to (يحيي), (الواو) a conjunction (كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq whose operator is تخرجون [Note: that is, "you will be brought out of the graves, an extraction like the extraction mentioned before."], and the (الواو) in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause « (سبّحوا) سبحان..» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
The clause «تمسون..» is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
The clause «تصبحون..» is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
The clause «له الحمد..» has no grammatical position (parenthetical).
The clause «تظهرون..» is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
The clause «يخرج..» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
The clause «يخرج (الثانية..) ..» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause يخرج (the first)).
The clause «يحيي ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause يخرج (the second)).
The clause «تخرجون..» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause يحيي).

* Benefits:
1- The meanings of «أصبح, أمسى and أضحى» are three:
a- That the content of the sentence coincides with the times proper to them, namely morning, evening and forenoon.
b- That they give the meaning of entering these times; in this case they are complete verbs, satisfied with their nominative. Ḥumayd al-Arqaṭ said:
فأصبحوا والنوى عالى معرسّهم ... وليس كل النوى تلقي المساكين
(They entered the morning while the destination was far above their camping-place; and not every destination casts down the poor.)
c- That they carry the meaning of صار (became), as in our saying: أصبح عليّ فارسا (ʿAlī became a horseman), and أمسى خالد كريما (Khālid became generous).
2- The variety of colours and tongues:
Truly, when a person reflects on how each individual of mankind has been singled out with a colour and features that distinguish him from others, how these languages have sprung forth and these tongues have differed among the peoples of the earth, and how each group of people has agreed on a language of their own which they master to the exclusion of other languages, truly that fills the soul with wonder, the mind with awe, and the hearts with reverence for the Creator of the universe, the Disposer of its affairs, who spreads His signs throughout its regions. But where are the minds that perceive, the souls that are fair, and the hearts that understand...?

safi-cedvel:20-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction (من آياته) attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) fronted for the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun).. and likewise in the five places that follow (أن) a maṣdar particle (من تراب) attached to (خلقكم) (ثمّ) a conjunction (إذا) the particle of suddenness.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن خلقكم) is in the position of a nominative, a delayed mubtadaʾ.
The clause «من آياته أن خلقكم ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause يخرج الحيّ....).
The clause «خلقكم..» has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن)).
The clause «أنتم بشر ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle-relative).
The clause «تنتشرون ... » is in the position of a nominative (naʿt (adjective) of بشر) [Note: or it is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنتم.].
(21) (الواو) a conjunction (لكم) attached to (خلق), (من أنفسكم) attached to (خلق) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (أزواجا).], (اللام) of reason (تسكنوا) an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the lām, its sign of accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent) (إليها) attached to (تسكنوا)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تسكنوا ... ) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (خلق).
(بينكم) an accusative adverbial attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose operator is جعل [Note: or attached to (جعل), taking it in the sense of خلق or أوجد.], (في ذلك) attached to an omitted khabar of inna (اللام) of emphasis (آيات) the delayed ism of inna, accusative, its sign of accusative being the kasra.. and likewise the similar cases that follow (لقوم) attached to a naʿt of آيات.
The clause «من آياته أن خلق ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause من آياته أن خلقكم).
The clause «خلق....» has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle-relative (أن)).
The clause «تسكنوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن)).
The clause «جعل ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause خلق لكم).
The clause «إنّ في ذلك ... » has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumption or parenthetical).
The clause «يتفكّرون..» is in the position of a genitive (naʿt of قوم).
(22) (خلق) a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative (الواو) a conjunction in the three places (اختلاف) conjoined to the mubtadaʾ خلق, nominative.
The clause «من آياته خلق ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause من آياته أن خلقكم).
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ... » has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumption - or parenthetical) - (23) (منامكم) a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative (بالليل) attached to the maṣdar منامكم (من فضله) attached to the maṣdar (ابتغاؤكم).
The clause «من آياته منامكم ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause من آياته أن خلقكم).
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ... » has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumption - or parenthetical) - (24) (الواو) a conjunction (يريكم) an imperfect verb, nominative - the maṣdar particle being implied before it by analogy with the verbs mentioned before - [Note: it is permissible that (من آياته) be a ḥāl of (البرق), the clause then being verbal, conjoined to the nominal clause (من آياته أن خلقكم).].
(خوفا) a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (من السماء) attached to (ينزّل), (الفاء) a conjunction (به) attached to (يحيي), and the (الباء) is causal (بعد) an accusative adverbial attached to (يحيي).
The clause «من آياته (إراءتكم ... ) » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause من آياته أن خلقكم).
The clause «يريكم..» has no grammatical position (ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن)).
The clause «ينزّل ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause يريكم).
The clause «يحيي ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause ينزّل).
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ... » has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumption - or parenthetical) - and the clause «يعقلون..» is in the position of a genitive (naʿt of قوم).
(25) (الواو) a conjunction (بأمره) attached to a ḥāl of السماء and الأرض (ثمّ) a conjunction (إذا) an adverbial of future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to the content of the apodosis (دعوة) a mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative (من الأرض) attached to (دعاكم), (إذا) the particle of suddenness - and the clause «من آياته أن تقوم ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause من آياته أن خلقكم).
The clause «تقوم السماء ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle-relative (أن)).
The clause «دعاكم ... » is in the position of a genitive (muḍāf ilayhi).
The clause «أنتم تخرجون..» has no grammatical position (apodosis of a non-jussive condition).
The clause «تخرجون..» is in the position of a nominative (khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم)).
(26) (الواو) a conjunction (له) attached to an omitted khabar fronted for the mubtadaʾ (من), (في السموات) attached to an omitted ṣila of من (كل) a mubtadaʾ, nominative - and the tanwīn in it is a substitute for something omitted, that is, "every created being" - (له) attached to the khabar (قانتون).
The clause «له من في السموات..» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause من آياته أن تقوم).
The clause «كلّ له قانتون.» has no grammatical position (an explanatory resumption).
(27) (الواو) a conjunction (هو الذي ... يعيده) its i'rab has been given earlier [Note: in verse (11) of this sūra.], (الواو) circumstantial - or parenthetical - and the pronoun (هو) refers to the creation, or the repetition, or the return, understood from the context (عليه) attached to (أهون), (الواو) a conjunction (له المثل) like له من.... (في السموات) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in الأعلى (الواو) a conjunction (الحكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «هو الذي....» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause له من في السموات).
The clause «يبدأ ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative noun (الذي)).
The clause «يعيده ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the ṣila clause).
The clause «هو أهون ... » has no grammatical position (parenthetical) - or is in the position of an accusative ḥāl - and the clause «له المثل ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause هو الذي....).
The clause «هو العزيز ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause هو الذي....).

* Morphology:
(أهون): a noun of comparison (ism tafḍīl) by which description, not comparison, is intended; its pattern is أفعل, from the triliteral verb (هان).

* Rhetoric:
The device of al-laff: in the words of the Exalted «وَمِنْ آياتِهِ مَنامُكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ وَابْتِغاؤُكُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ» this belongs to the category of al-laff (folding), and its order is: "and among His signs are your sleeping and your seeking of His bounty, by night and by day"; except that the last two members were separated, because they are two times, and time and what occurs in it are like one thing, with the folding helping towards unity. It is also possible that what is meant is "your sleeping in both times, and your seeking in both"; but the apparent sense is the first, because it recurs in the Qur'an, and the soundest meanings are those the Qur'an indicates, which they hear with attentive ears.

* Benefits:
1- The particle أن may be omitted and the verb put in the position of the maṣdar. Among that is the well-known proverb:
تسمع بالمعيدي خير من أن تراه.
(That you hear of al-Muʿaydī is better than that you see him.)
The first to utter it was al-Mundhir ibn Māʾ al-Samāʾ.
He had admired the reports about al-Muʿaydī, and when he stood before him and saw his ugliness he said the aforementioned proverb.
The implied form is: أن تسمع بالمعيدي etc.
2- It is a condition that the agent of the verb and of what follows it as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi be the same. For this reason Ibn Mālik answered in Sharḥ al-Tasḥīl that the meaning of يريكم is "He makes you see", and thereby the agent of the verb «يريكم» and the agent of the fear and the hope become one. So reflect...!

safi-cedvel:35-36.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) is the munqaṭiʿa (disjunctive) particle meaning بل ("rather"), and the hamza is that of denial (إنكار). (عليهم) is attached to (أنزلنا). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (بما) is attached to (يتكلّم). (به) is attached to (يشركون).
The clause «أنزلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «هو يتكلّم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أنزلنا.
The clause «يتكلّم ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
The clause «كانوا به يشركون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يشركون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
(36) (الواو) is a conjunction. (بها) is attached to (فرحوا). (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is a maṣdar particle, (إذا) is the particle of suddenness (fujāʾiyya) ...
The clause «أذقنا ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «فرحوا بها» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
The clause «تصبهم سيّئة ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the condition, its protasis and its apodosis, which is itself conjoined to the clause أنزلنا ...
The clause «هم يقنطون ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined to (إذا) of suddenness.
The clause «هم يقنطون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Rhetoric:
Iltifāt (shift of person): in His saying, the Exalted, «أَمْ أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطاناً».
A shift from address to the third person, to signal turning away from them and to enumerate their offences to others.
Majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted, «فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ».
It indicates that "speaking" is figurative for "indicating", as you say: "a book that speaks of such-and-such", and "this is something the Qur'an has spoken of", meaning indication and testimony, as if He had said: it testifies to their shirk and to its soundness.

* Benefits:
- We spoke briefly before about the human types scattered through the verses of the Noble Qur'an. We offer further examples through these verses:
a- In the first verse Allah, glory be to Him, presents to us the picture of the human being who turns to his Lord in the hour of hardship and turns away from remembering Him in the hour of relief.
This reminds me of the popular proverb: «ما زلت صلي حتى حصّلي فإذا حصّلي بطّلت صلي» ("I kept praying until I got what I wanted; once I got it, I stopped praying").
b- And this is another type, almost the opposite of the first. It portrays for us the human being when he rejoices in what Allah gives him of His bounty, and how he despairs and his heart is constricted when any harm befalls him, so that he becomes despairing and ungrateful.
This reminds us of the patience of the prophets, which differs from the distress and constriction of heart that people show. Allah favoured Ayyūb for a period of time, then tried him in lives, fruits and health for another period. His wife would ask him to ask Allah for well-being and deliverance from the affliction, and he would say to her: I am ashamed before Allah to ask Him for well-being from the affliction, for the length of the affliction does not equal the days of happiness and ease that Allah granted us; so let us be patient and give thanks. Hence the proverb of the patience of Ayyūb.

safi-cedvel:37-38.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for reproachful questioning (istifhām tawbīkhī). (الواو) is a conjunction. (لمن) is attached to (يبسط..).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يبسط..) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يروا.
(في ذلك) is attached to the khabar of إنّ. (اللام) is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) for emphasis. (لقوم) is attached to an adjective of آيات.
The clause: «يروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive, namely:
"Were they heedless and did they not see ..."
The clause «يبسط....» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «يقدر....» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يؤمنون ... » is in the position of genitive as an adjective of قوم.
(38) (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis of an implied condition. (حقّه) is a second direct object, accusative. (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (للذين) is attached to (خبر). (هم) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is المفلحون, the nominal clause being the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.].
The clause «آت ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, namely: "if provision is in Allah's hand, then give ..."
The clause «ذلك خير ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī) or causal.
The clause «يريدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أولئك ... المفلحون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ذلك خير [Note: It is permissible for the clause to be a ḥāl from the agent of يريدون.].

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (ما) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of accusative as a fronted direct object. (آتيتم) is a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis. (من ربا) is attached to a ḥāl from ما [Note: or it is a tamyīz for it.]. (اللام) is for causation. (يربو) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (في أموال) is attached to (يربو). (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis. (لا) is negative. (عند) is an adverb, accusative, attached to (يربو).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يربو ... ) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (آتيتم).
(الواو) is a conjunction. (ما.... من زكاة) is like ما.. من ربا. (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis. (هم المضعفون) is like هم المفلحون [Note: in the preceding verse (38).].
The clause: «آتيتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يربو ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle أن (maṣdar).
The clause «لا يربو ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو" ... and the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined to the fāʾ.
The clause «آتيتم (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آتيتم (the first).
The clause «تريدون ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of آتيتم [Note: or in the position of genitive as an adjective of زكاة, the connecting pronoun being omitted, i.e. "you seek Allah's countenance by it".].
The clause «أولئك ... المضعفون» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined to the fāʾ, and there is an iltifāt in the speech.

* Morphology:
(المضعفون) is the plural of المضعف, an active participle of the quadriliteral verb أضعف, its wazn being مُفْعِل with ḍamma on the first letter and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Iltifāt (shift of person): in His saying, the Exalted, «فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُضْعِفُونَ».
A shift away from address, since it said "فأولئك" rather than "فأنتم", for glorification, as if He, glory be to Him, were addressing the angels, peace be upon them, and the elect of creation, to make their state known. It is also possible that the expression is for generalisation, so that by أولئك is meant these and others.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الذي) is a relative noun, a khabar in the position of nominative [Note: It may be an adjective of the name of Majesty (الجلالة), the khabar being the clause هل من شركائكم من يفعل ..., and the connector being (من ذلكم), the reference being to His, the Exalted, deeds.]. (ثمّ) is a conjunction of delay in the three places. (هل) is an interrogative particle of denial. (من شركائكم) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من). (من ذلكم) is attached to a ḥāl from شيء. (شيء) is genitive in form, accusative in position, a direct object governed by يفعل. (سبحانه) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, accusative. (عمّا) is attached to (تعالى), the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "they associate with Him".
The clause: «الله الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «خلقكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «رزقكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يميتكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رزقكم.
The clause «يحييكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يميتكم.
The clause «هل من شركائكم من يفعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يفعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause « (نسبّح) سبحانه ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, introduced for supplication.
The clause «تعالى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the preceding resumptive clause.
The clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(في البرّ) is attached to (ظهر). (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "what the hands of the people have earned"]. (اللام) is for causation. (يذيقهم) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the agent is a latent pronoun referring to Allah, understood from the context.
The clause: «ظهر الفساد ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كسبت أيدي الناس» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما), and the interpreted maṣdar (ما كسبت ... ) is in the position of genitive through the bāʾ, attached to (ظهر).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يذيقهم ... ) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (ظهر).
The clause «يذيقهم» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «لعلّهم يرجعون ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يرجعون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of لعلّهم.

safi-cedvel:42-43.t:
* I'rab:
(في الأرض) is attached to (سيروا). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the khabar of كان. (قبل) is an adverbial noun, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of the relative noun الذين ...
The clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «سيروا ... » is in the position of accusative as the reported speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «انظروا ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause سيروا.
The clause «كان عاقبة ... » is in the position of accusative as a direct object of the verb of looking (naẓar), suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «كان أكثرهم مشركين» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī).
(43) (فأقم ... للدين): its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (30) of this sūra.]. (من قبل) is attached to (أقم). (أن) is a maṣdar particle..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتي..) is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
(لا) is the lā of generic negation. (له) is attached to the khabar of لا. (من الله) is attached to an omitted element indicated by مردّ; it cannot be attached to مردّ, since in that case it would have to be given tanwīn [Note: al-Jamal allowed attaching it to the preceding verb يأتي, i.e. "a day comes from Allah on which there is no turning back"]. (يومئذ) is an adverb, accusative [Note: or indeclinable on fatḥa because it is annexed to an indeclinable adverb, namely (إذ), the tanwīn in it being the compensatory tanwīn], attached to (يصّدّعون).
The clause: «أقم وجهك ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, namely: "if some people associate partners, then set your face toward the religion."
The clause «يأتي يوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «لا مردّ له» is in the position of nominative as an adjective of يوم.
The clause «يصّدّعون» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(يصّدّعون): the tāʾ of the form-V pattern (tafaʿʿul) is replaced by ṣād because it comes before ṣād; its origin is يتصدّعون, its wazn is يتفعلون.

safi-cedvel:44-45.t:
* I'rab:
«من» is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ. «كفر» is in the position of jussive, the protasis. (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis. (عليه) is a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كفره). (الواو) is a conjunction. (من) is like the first. (لأنفسهم) is attached to (يمهدون).
The clause: «من كفر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كفر ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «عليه كفره» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined to the fāʾ.
The clause «من عمل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «عمل صالحا ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «يمهدون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم" ... and the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis.
(45) (اللام) is for causation. (يجزي) is accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the agent is a pronoun referring to Allah, understood from the context.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجزي ... ) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (يمهدون) [Note: or to (يصّدّعون) in verse (43), the meaning being: they separate so that He may reward the believers out of His bounty, and the disbelievers with justice.].
(من فضله) is attached to (يجزي). (لا) is negative..
The clause «يجزي ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آمنوا..
The clause «إنّه لا يحبّ الكافرين» has no grammatical position; it is a justification for an implied statement, i.e. "He rewards the disbelievers; indeed He does not love them."
The clause «لا يحبّ الكافرين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Benefits:
- Responsibility and recompense:
The European philosopher "Bergson" said: whoever reflects on people's deeds sees people who do good and receive nothing but evil, and others who do evil and receive nothing but good.
This contradicts the laws of this universe, which is founded on order and justice.
It follows that this universe must have a just God, who rewards good with good and evil with evil. And since many people do not receive justice in this world, man must have a life other than this one, in which justice is established and in which every human being receives in full the reward for what he did in this life. This agrees with the laws of this perfect universe, which must have a just, able and willing Creator, and He is Allah.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (من آياته أن يرسل..) is like من آياته أن خلقكم [Note: in verse (20) of this sūra. (2, 3, 4) in the preceding verse (45).]. (مبشّرات) is an accusative ḥāl from الرياح, the sign of the accusative being the kasra. (الواو) is a conjunction. (اللام) is for causation in the three places. (يذيقكم) is like يجزي «2». (من رحمته) is attached to (يذيقكم). (تجري) is like يجزي «3». (بأمره) is attached to (تجري). (تبتغوا) is like يجزي «4». (من فضله) is attached to (تبتغوا). (الواو) is a conjunction ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يرسل ... ) is in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يذيقكم ... ) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to an implied verb, i.e. "He sends them" [Note: or attached to what the element conjoined to it is attached to, which is implied, i.e. "He sends the winds as heralds of rain so that you may drink of it and so that He may let you taste ..."].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تجري..) is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to an implied verb, i.e. "He sends them".
The clause «(أن) (تبتغوا)» is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to an implied verb, i.e. "He sends them".
The clause: «من آياته (إرسال) الرياح» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يرسل» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «يذيقكم» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «تجري الفلك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second implied maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «تبتغوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the third maṣdar particle (أن).
The clause «لعلّكم تشكرون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied justification, i.e. "He did that so that you may prosper and so that you may give thanks."
The clause «تشكرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(مبشّرات) is the plural of مبشّرة, the feminine of مبشّر, an active participle of the quadriliteral verb بشّر, its wazn being مُفَعِّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Istiʿāra (metaphor) and majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَلِيُذِيقَكُمْ مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ».
The metaphor is in His saying, the Exalted, «لِيُذِيقَكُمْ», which has often been discussed before; it is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya).
Majāz mursal (loose figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted, «مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ». It is a majāz mursal whose relation is ḥāliyya (the contained for the container), because mercy dwells in fertility and rain, so the thing that dwells was mentioned and the place was meant. Some interpreted "mercy" as: "of His bounty, of sweet waters, fresh trees, bodily health and all that follows from these matters which none can count but Allah."

safi-cedvel:47-47.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (اللام) is an implied lām of oath. (قد) is a particle of affirmation. (من قبلك) is attached to a ḥāl from رسلا, or attached to (أرسلنا). (إلى قومهم) is attached to (أرسلنا). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (بالبيّنات) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of جاءوهم. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (من الذين) is attached to (انتقمنا). (الواو) is a conjunction. (حقا) is the accusative khabar of كان. (علينا) is attached to the khabar (حقا).
The clause: «أرسلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath, and the implied oath clause, its answer and what is conjoined to it form a parenthetical resumptive.
The clause «جاءوهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أرسلنا.
The clause «انتقمنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause جاءوهم.
The clause «كان حقا ... نصر» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied oath clause.

safi-cedvel:48-49.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction in the four places. (في السماء) is attached to (يبسطه). (كيف) is a non-jussive conditional noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl governed by يشاء [Note: its apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "however He wills He spreads it in the sky".]. (كسفا) is a second direct object, accusative. (من خلاله) is attached to (يخرج). (به) is attached to (أصاب), the bāʾ being causal. (من عباده) is attached to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun [Note: or it is a tamyīz of the relative noun (من).], i.e. "whomever He wills to strike with it among His servants". (إذا) is the particle of suddenness.
The clause: «الله الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يرسل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «تثير ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يرسل.
The clause «يبسطه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تثير.
The clause «يشاء» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of يبسط.
The clause «يجعله ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يبسطه.
The clause «ترى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يجعله.
The clause «يخرج ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from الودق.
The clause of the condition, its protasis and its apodosis ... has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to ترى.
The clause «أصاب ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «هم يستبشرون» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
The clause «يستبشرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(49) (الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (إن) is the lightened form of the heavy (inna), without effect (muhmala). (من قبل) is attached to the khabar مبلسين. (أن) is a maṣdar particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ينزّل) is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The deputy agent of the verb (ينزّل) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to الودق. (عليهم) is attached to (ينزّل). (من قبله) is an emphasis of what precedes it. (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa).
The clause: «كانوا ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «ينزّل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (أن).

* Benefits:
1- The conditional kayfa:
It is stated in al-Mughnī: kayfa is used in two ways, one of which is as a conditional, and among that is His saying, the Exalted: «ينفق كيف يشاء، يصوركم في الأرحام كيف يشاء، فيبسطه في السماء كيف يشاء». In these three examples kayfa is conditional, and its condition is omitted, as what precedes it indicates it.
2- كيف يشاء: We cite this text mentioned by the author of al-Mughnī, because of the benefit we see in it. He said:
kayfa is used in two ways. One is that it be a condition, in which case it requires two verbs, identical in form and meaning, not jussive, as in «كيف تصنع أصنع» ("however you do, I do"). It is not permitted, by agreement, to say «كيف تجلس أذهب», nor «كيف تجلس أجلس» with the jussive according to the Basrans, except Quṭrub, because it differs from the particles of condition in that its apodosis must agree with its protasis, as was mentioned. It was also said that this is permitted absolutely, and Quṭrub and the Kufans held this; and it was said that it is permitted on condition that it be joined with «ما». They said: among its occurrences as a conditional are «يُنْفِقُ كَيْفَ يَشاءُ» and «يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحامِ كَيْفَ يَشاءُ» and «فَيَبْسُطُهُ فِي السَّماءِ كَيْفَ يَشاءُ», and its apodosis in all of that is omitted, as what precedes it indicates. This poses a difficulty for their absolute statement that its apodosis must match its protasis, and there are comments and rebuttals on this which we have passed over, for brevity.

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis of an implied condition. (إلى آثار) is attached to (انظر). (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl governed by يحيي. (بعد) is an adverb, accusative, attached to (يحيي), and the reference in (ذلك) is to the one who gives life to the earth, namely Allah. (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). (الواو) is a conjunction. (على كلّ) is attached to the khabar قدير.
The clause: «انظر ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if Allah sends the winds, then look at the effects of ..."
The clause «يحيي الأرض ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the name of Majesty (لفظ الجلالة) [Note: the original sense is: look at the effects of Allah's mercy, in how the earth is given life; so the interrogative noun kayfa, as it appears, is accusative by removal of the preposition, but the i'rab above is sound by way of implication.].
The clause «إنّ ذلك لمحيي ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «هو ... قدير» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّ ذلك لمحيي....

* Morphology:
(محيي) is an active participle of the quadriliteral verb أحيا, its wazn being مُفْعِل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:51-53.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (إن) is a jussive conditional particle. (أرسلنا) is in the position of jussive, the protasis. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (رأوه) is also in the position of jussive, conjoined to (أرسلنا). (اللام) the second is the lām of oath, indicated by the first, the preparatory lām (lām muwaṭṭiʾa). (من بعده) is attached to (يكفرون).
The clause: «أرسلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «رأوه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «ظلوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the oath ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
The clause «يكفرون ... » is in the position of accusative as the khabar of ظلوا.
(52) (الفاء) is causal. (لا) is negative in both places, and the second object of the first (تسمع) is a pronoun referring to the second object of the second (تسمع), by way of conflict of governors (tanāzuʿ). (ولّوا) is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters ... and the wāw is the agent. (مدبرين) is a ḥāl that emphasises its governor (ḥāl muʾakkida), accusative..
The clause: «إنّك لا تسمع ... » has no grammatical position; it is a justification for an implied statement, i.e. "do not grieve over them, for they are deaf like the dead."
The clause «لا تسمع الموتى ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «لا تسمع الصمّ ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.
The clause «ولّوا ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it [Note: it is permissible to strip it of the meaning of condition, and then it is attached to the preceding (تسمع).].
(53) (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is a negative particle acting like ليس. (أنت) is a detached pronoun, the subject (ism) of ما. (هادي) is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ما, the sign of the genitive being an implied kasra on the letter before the yāʾ, which is dropped in writing in accordance with the reading in continuous recitation (qirāʾat al-waṣl). (عن ضلالتهم) is attached to هادي, which is made to include the meaning of "one who turns away" [Note: see verse (81) of Sūrat al-Naml.]. (إن) is negative. (إلّا) is for restriction. (من) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a direct object. (بآياتنا) is attached to (يؤمن). (الفاء) is a conjunction..
The clause: «ما أنت بهادي ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّك لا تسمع ...
The clause «إن تسمع ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive (istiʾnāf bayānī) or causal.
The clause «يؤمن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «هم مسلمون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يؤمن.

* Morphology:
(51) مصفرّا: an active participle of the quinquiliteral verb اصفرّ; it may also be a passive participle, the wazn being the same because of the doubling of the rāʾ. When the assimilation is undone, the difference between the active and the passive participle appears in the pronunciation. Its wazn is مُفْعَلّ with ḍamma on the fāʾ and shadda on the lām ...

safi-cedvel:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
(من ضعف) is attached to (خلقكم). (من بعد) is attached to an omitted second direct object governed by جعل in both places. (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a direct object, the returning pronoun being omitted. (الواو) is a conjunction, or circumstantial. (القدير) is a second khabar, nominative.
The clause: «الله الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «خلقكم..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «جعل (the first)» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause خلقكم.
The clause «جعل (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause جعل (the first).
The clause «يخلق ... » is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله) [Note: it may be resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «هو العليم ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يخلق.

* Morphology:
(شيبة) is a samāʿī (heard, non-analogical) maṣdar of the triliteral verb شاب, its wazn being فَعْلة, on the pattern of the maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar al-marra). There are other maṣdars of the verb: شيب, with fatḥa and sukūn, and مشيب, with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:55-57.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (يوم) is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يقسم). (ما) is negative. (غير) is an adverb, accusative, attached to (لبثوا). (كذلك) is attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq governed by (يؤفكون), whose wāw is the deputy agent.
The clause: «تقوم الساعة ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يقسم المجرمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «ما لبثوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يؤفكون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
(56) (الواو) is a conjunction, and the wāw in (أوتوا) is the deputy agent. (اللام) is the lām of oath, for an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of affirmation. (في كتاب) is attached to (لبثتم), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "in the decree of the Book of Allah". (إلى يوم) is attached to (لبثتم). (الفاء) is a conjunction [Note: al-Bayḍāwī made it a connector of the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you were deniers of the resurrection, then this is the Day of Resurrection", that is, "the falsity of your denial has become clear".]. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is negative ...
The clause: «قال الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يقسم المجرمون.
The clause «أوتوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «قد لبثتم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath ...
The implied oath clause is in the position of accusative as the reported speech.
The clause «هذا يوم ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the reported-speech clause.
The clause «لكنّكم كنتم ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the reported-speech clause.
The clause «كنتم لا تعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of لكنّكم.
The clause «لا تعلمون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم.
(57) (الفاء) is a conjunction. (يومئذ) is an adverb, accusative [Note: or indeclinable because it is annexed to the indeclinable (إذ)], attached to the negated (ينفع). (لا) is negative. (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a fronted direct object. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is like the first, and the wāw in (يستعتبون) is the deputy agent.
The clause: «لا ينفع ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يقسم المجرمون.
The clause «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا هم يستعتبون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لا ينفع ...
The clause «يستعتبون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(معذرة) is a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb عذر (of the pattern ضرب), meaning "he lifted blame or sin from him"; its wazn is مَفْعِلة with kasra on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
- «وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يُقْسِمُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ ما لَبِثُوا غَيْرَ ساعَةٍ».
This rhetorical figure is a kind of jinās (paronomasia): bringing one word with two or several meanings. This rhetorical art occurs in pre-Islamic poetry and in the Noble Qur'an in a moderate, pleasing and quite acceptable form, but poets of later ages soon bit into it with their molars, competing to use it excessively, with affectation and strain, until it became a kind of artificiality after having been a kind of craftsmanship, and until it became odious and detested among the poets of the age of decline.
Among the curious things is that the folk poets heard it from the educated poets, were dazzled by its form, and thought it a peak of rhetoric, so they built on it some arts of popular literature, such as the «عتابا» (ʿatābā), which is a kind of paired verse. In its first three hemistichs they committed to perfect jinās (al-jinās al-tāmm) and called it «المرصود» (al-marṣūd), and they did not tolerate transgressing this rule.
Thus many verbal and semantic embellishments turned into independent arts among the folk poets, and were it not for length we would record many of these arts and give examples clarifying this tendency.

safi-cedvel:58-60.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (لقد ضربنا) is like لقد لبثتم [Note: in verse (56) of this sūra]. (الناس) is attached to (ضربنا). (في هذا) is attached to (ضربنا). (من كلّ) is attached to (ضربنا) [Note: the two prepositions differ in form and meaning, so attachment to the verb itself is sound.]. (الواو) is a conjunction. (اللام) is the preparatory lām of the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa). (إن) is a jussive conditional particle. (جئتهم) is in the position of jussive, the protasis. (بآية) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of جئت. (اللام) is the lām of oath. (يقولنّ) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of nominative ...
and (النون) is for emphasis. (إن) is a particle of negation. (إلّا) is for restriction.
The clause: «قد ضربنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to an implied oath.. and the oath clause is resumptive.
The clause «جئتهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied oath clause.
The clause «يقولنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the second implied oath.
The clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إن أنتم إلّا مبطلون» is in the position of accusative as the reported speech.
(59) (كذلك) is attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq governed by يطبع. (على قلوب) is attached to (يطبع). (لا) is negative.
The clause «يطبع الله» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical or resumptive.
The clause «لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
(60) (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis of an implied condition. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive particle. (يستخفّنّك) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of jussive ... and (النون) is for emphasis, and (الكاف) is a direct object. (لا) is negative.
The clause: «اصبر ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the disbelievers say that, then be patient ..."
The clause «إنّ وعد الله حقّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
The clause «لا يستخفّنك الذين ... » is conjoined to the clause اصبر.
The clause «لا يوقنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
... ...

safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(في أدنى) is attached to (غلبت). (الواو) is a conjunction. (من بعد) is attached to (سيغلبون).
The clause «غلبت الروم..» has no grammatical position; it is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya).
And the clause «هم ... سيغلبون..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the inceptive clause.
(4-5) (في بضع) is attached to (سيغلبون), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "within the span of a few years". (لله) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الأمر). (قبل) is an adverb of time built on ḍamma, in the position of genitive by (من), attached to the khabar. (من بعد) is like (من قبل), being conjoined to it. (الواو) is a conjunction. (يومئذ) is an accusative adverb of time, a muḍāf, attached to (يفرح), and the tanwīn at its end is a substitute for an omitted clause. (بنصر) is attached to (يفرح), and the fāʿil (agent) of (ينصر) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he), referring to the Name of Majesty. (الواو) is a conjunction.
And the clause «لله الأمر..» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
And the clause «يفرح المؤمنون..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the inceptive clause.
And the clause «ينصر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, or causal.
And the clause «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «هو العزيز ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «ينصر».

* Morphology:
(الروم) is a generic noun, the name of a people who were named after the name of their father Rūm ibn ʿĪṣū ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, as it has been said.
(غلبهم) is the maṣdar of the triliteral غلب, of the pattern of ضرب, its wazn being فعل with two fatḥas. There are other maṣdars: غلب with fatḥa and sukūn, غلبة with two fatḥas, مغلب with fatḥa on the mīm and the lām, غلبّ with two ḍammas and a doubled fatḥa-vowelled bāʾ, and with two kasras, غلبّة with two ḍammas and a doubled fatḥa-vowelled bāʾ, and غلابية with fatḥa on the ghayn, kasra on the bāʾ and fatḥa on the yāʾ.

* Benefits:
- The Persians and the Romans (al-Furs wa-l-Rūm):
The Arabs applied the word al-Rūm to the state of Byzantium, whose capital was Constantinople; today the Rūm are the Eastern Christians, "Catholics and Orthodox".
The Persians and the Romans fought a battle between Buṣrā and Adhriʿāt, and the Persians won. This reached Quraysh, who rejoiced at the victory of polytheism over the People of the Book, and regarded it as a victory for themselves. Umayya ibn Khalaf and Abū Bakr quarrelled and wagered on a hundred young she-camels, up to nine years, which Abū Bakr would pay to Umayya if the Romans were not victorious within that period, and Umayya would pay to Abū Bakr if they were victorious. When Umayya feared that Abū Bakr might leave Mecca, he asked him for a guarantor, and his son ʿAbd Allāh stood surety for him. When Umayya went out to Uḥud and died after the battle, as a result of a stab from the spear of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Romans had been victorious over Persia on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya. Abū Bakr demanded the hundred she-camels, and they were paid to him; Abū Bakr brought them to the Messenger of Allah, who said to him: Give them in charity. Thus the reasons for the revelation of the verse become clear to us. And al-biḍʿ is what lies between three and nine. The Romans were victorious over the Persians seven years after the battle south of Ḥawrān in which the Persians were victorious over the Romans.
Allah the Almighty has spoken the truth ... «غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ، فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ»

safi-cedvel:6-7.t:
* I'rab:
(وعد) is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of an omitted verb, confirming the content of the preceding clause, accusative. (لا) is negative in both places. (الواو) is a conjunction.
The clause « (وعدهم) الله وعدا» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يخلف الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption [Note: they have permitted it to be in the position of accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the maṣdar (وعد), the meaning being "a promise of Allah that is not broken" ...].
And the clause «لكنّ أكثر الناس ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «لا يخلف الله».
And the clause «لا يعلمون..» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (لكنّ).
(7) (من الحياة) is attached to (ظاهرا). (الواو) is circumstantial. (عن الآخرة) is attached to the khabar (غافلون), and the second (هم) is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the first.
And the clause «يعلمون ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption, or causal; and the clause «هم ... غافلون..» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «يَعْلَمُونَ ظاهِراً مِنَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا»:
The benefit of making (ظاهر) indefinite is to diminish what they know, and diminishing it brings it close to negation so that it matches that for which it is a substitute. It is related from al-Ḥasan that he said when reciting this verse: such is the skill of one of them in the outward side of worldly life that he taps the dinar with his finger and knows whether it is good or bad. Its benefit also is: that they know only one outward aspect out of the sum of outward aspects.
Repetition (al-taʿaṭṭuf): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَهُمْ عَنِ الْآخِرَةِ هُمْ غافِلُونَ».
The art of taʿaṭṭuf is the repetition of the very same word within a sentence in speech or in a line of poetry. He repeated «هم» for emphasis in affirming their heedlessness of the Hereafter.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogation of rebuke (istifhām inkārī). (الواو) is a conjunction. (في أنفسهم) is attached to (يتفكّروا). (ما) is negative, and the second is a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to (السموات) by the (الواو). (بينهما) is an accusative adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of (ما).
