(إلّا) is for restriction. (بالحقّ) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of (خلق) or its object. The sign of the genitive in (مسمّى) is the implied kasra. (الواو) is resumptive. (من الناس) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (كثيرا). (بلقاء) is attached to (كافرون), the khabar (predicate) of (إنّ), and the (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).
The clause «لم يتفكّروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: "Were they ignorant and did they not reflect".
And the clause «ما خلق الله ... » is in the position of accusative, a direct object of the verb of reflecting, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the negation [Note: al-ʿUkbarī permitted it to be resumptive, the preceding speech being complete.].
And the clause «إنّ كثيرا.. لكافرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(أولم يسيروا) is like (أولم يتفكّروا) [Note: in the preceding verse (8).]. (في الأرض) is attached to (يسيروا). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, the khabar (predicate) of (كان). (من قبلهم) is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). (منهم) is attached to (أشدّ). (قوّة) is a tamyīz (specification), accusative, and the pronoun that is the fāʿil (agent) in (أثاروا، عمروها) refers to the ancients. (أكثر) is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) standing in for the maṣdar, so it is its adjective, and the pronoun in the second (عمروها) refers to the people of Mecca. (بالبيّنات) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الرسل). (الفاء) is resumptive. (ما) is negative. (اللام) is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd). (يظلمهم) is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām of denial.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يظلمهم ... ) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted khabar of (كان).
(الواو) is a conjunction. (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). (أنفسهم) is a fronted direct object, accusative.
The clause «لم يسيروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "Did they sit still and not travel".
And the clause «ينظروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the negated clause «يسيروا».
And the clause «كان عاقبة ... » is in the position of accusative, a direct object of the verb of looking in the sense of reflecting, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative (كيف).
And the clause «كانوا أشدّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «أثاروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «كانوا» [Note: the wāw before it may be circumstantial, the clause then being in the position of accusative, a ḥāl, with an implied (قد).].
And the clause «عمروها ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «أثاروا» ...
And the clause «عمروها (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type (ما) [Note: and the interpreted maṣdar (ما عمروها) is in the position of genitive by (من), attached to (أكثر).].
And the clause «جاءتهم رسلهم..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «عمروها» (the first) [Note: the wāw before it may be circumstantial, the clause being in the position of accusative, a ḥāl, with an implied (قد).].
And the clause «ما كان الله ليظلمهم..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يظلمهم..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type (أن).
And the clause «كانوا ... يظلمون..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «ما كان..».
And the clause «يظلمون..» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كانوا).
(10) (ثمّ) is a conjunction. (عاقبة) is the khabar of (كان), accusative, fronted. (السوءى) is the ism of (كان), postponed, nominative, its sign of nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif [Note: it may be an absolute object whose operative is (أساؤوا).. or a direct object whose operative is (أساؤوا) with an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "they did the worst deed".]. (أن) is a maṣdar particle. (بآيات) is attached to (كذّبوا). (بها) is attached to (يستهزئون).
And the interpreted maṣdar: (أن كذّبوا) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, the lām or the bāʾ, attached to (عاقبة) [Note: it may be a badal (substitute) for (السوءى) if the latter is a noun for the deficient (al-nāqiṣ), in which case the maṣdar is in the position of nominative..].
And the clause «كان عاقبة..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «ما كان الله ليظلمهم».
And the clause «أساؤوا..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «كذّبوا..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type (أن).
And the clause «كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «كذّبوا».
And the clause «يستهزئون..» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كانوا).

* Morphology:
(السوءى) is the feminine of الأسوأ, an elative (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral ساء; its wazn is فعلى with ḍamma and sukūn.

* Benefits:
كيف is an interrogative noun by which one asks about the state of a thing; it is built on fatḥa. When كيف occurs before a noun or a deficient verb, it is a fronted khabar, such as: كيف أخوك.
When it occurs before the bāʾ that is a preposition, this bāʾ is redundant, such as: كيف بزيد. When a complete verb follows it, it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. كيف may also be conditional, requiring two verbs agreeing in form and meaning, not jussive, such as: كيف تصنع أصنع. And according to some it makes them jussive.

safi-cedvel:11-14.t:
* I'rab:
(ثمّ) is a conjunction in both places. (إليه) is attached to (ترجعون), and the (الواو) in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «الله يبدأ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يبدأ ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الله).
And the clause «يعيده..» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause «يبدأ».
And the clause «ترجعون..» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause «يبدأ».
(12) (الواو) is a conjunction. (يوم) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (يبلس).
And the clause «تقوم الساعة..» is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «يبلس المجرمون..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(13) (الواو) is a conjunction. (لهم) is attached to the khabar of (يكن). (من شركائهم) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (شفعاء), which is the ism of (يكن). (بشركائهم) is attached to the khabar (كافرين).
And the clause «لم يكن لهم شفعاء» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «يبلس».
And the clause «كانوا ... كافرين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «يبلس». [Translator's note: the source prints «شعفاء» in the I'rab of verse 13, evidently a slip for (شفعاء).]
(14) (الواو) is a conjunction. (يوم) is like the first, attached to (يتفرّقون). (يومئذ) is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the preceding adverb, and the tanwīn is a substitute for an omitted clause.
And the clause «تقوم الساعة..» is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «يتفرّقون..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «يبلس المجرمون».

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
(لكم) is attached to (ضرب) [Note: or to an omitted second direct object, by implying in (ضرب) the sense of "made" (جعل).]. (من أنفسكم) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (مثلا). (هل) is an interrogative particle of rebuke. (لكم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) (شركاء). (ممّا) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (شركاء). (شركاء) is genitive in form and nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ. (في ما) is attached to (شركاء). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (فيه) is attached to the khabar (سواء). (كخيفتكم) is attached to an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq). (أنفسكم) is a direct object of the maṣdar (خيفتكم). (كذلك) is attached to an omitted absolute object whose operative is (نفصّل). (لقوم) is attached to (نفصّل).
The clause «ضرب ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «هل لكم ممّا ملكت..» is in the position of accusative, a badal (substitute) for (مثلا).
And the clause «ملكت أيمانكم..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (ما).
And the clause «رزقناكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما) [Note: (ما) may be an indefinite with a qualifier, in which case the clause is in the position of genitive, its adjective.].
And the clause «أنتم فيه سواء..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «هل لكم ممّا ...».
And the clause «تخافونهم ... » is in the position of nominative, a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).
And the clause «نفصّل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يعقلون ... » is in the position of genitive, an adjective (naʿt) of (قوم).

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) is for transitional rejection (iḍrāb intiqālī). (بغير) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun (الذين), and (أهواءهم) is the direct object of (اتّبع), accusative. (الفاء) is a conjunction. (من) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject). The second (من) is a relative noun in the position of accusative, a direct object whose operative is (يهدي), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "He led him astray" or "He led them astray". (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is negative. (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (ناصرين), which is genitive in form and nominative in position, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «اتّبع الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «من يهدي..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause «يهدي..» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause «أضلّ الله....» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «ما لهم من ناصرين..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause [Note: the clause may be a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun, i.e. "whom Allah has led astray, he being unaided".].

safi-cedvel:30-32.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) connects the apodosis of an implied condition, and the fāʿil (agent) in (أقم) refers to the Messenger, peace be upon him. (للدين) is attached to (أقم). (حنيفا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the fāʿil or the object or (الدين). (فطرة) is a direct object of an omitted verb in the manner of incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "Hold fast to the fiṭra of Allah". (التي) is a relative noun in the position of accusative, an adjective (naʿt) of (فطرة). (عليها) is attached to (فطر). (لا) is the lā of generic negation. (لخلق) is attached to the khabar of (لا). (الدين) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك), nominative [Note: or it is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative noun and (القيّم) is the khabar; and it was said: (القيم) is an adjective of (الدين), and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "the oneness of Allah".]. (الواو) is a conjunction. (لا) is negative.
The clause «أقم ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if some people go astray, then set your face to the religion..".
The clause « (الزموا..) فطرة الله..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «فطر ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
And the clause «لا تبديل لخلق الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
And the clause «ذلك الدين القيّم ... » has no grammatical position; it is a second causal clause.
And the clause «لكنّ أكثر الناس....» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «ذلك الدين ...».
And the clause «لا يعلمون..» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (لكنّ).
(منيبين) is a ḥāl, accusative, from the fāʿil of (الزموا), its sign of accusative being the yāʾ. (إليه) is attached to (منيبين). (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places. (لا) is the prohibitive lā, which jusses. (من المشركين) is attached to the khabar of (تكونوا)..
The clause «اتّقوه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «الزموا فطرة ...».
And the clause «أقيموا.....» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «الزموا فطرة ...».
And the clause «لا تكونوا من المشركين..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause «الزموا فطرة....».
(32) (من الذين) is a badal (substitute) for (المشركين) with repetition of the preposition. (بما) is attached to the khabar (فرحون). (لديهم) is an adverb built on sukūn, in the position of accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of (ما).
And the clause «فرّقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «كانوا شيعا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause «كلّ حزب ... فرحون» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(30) فطرة: the tāʾ is written open (long form) in this place in the codex, and there is none in the Qur'an other than this place. It is a word that came on the pattern of the maṣdar of manner (maṣdar al-hayʾa) from the triliteral فطر, and it is a noun meaning receptivity to the true religion, or the religion of Islam. The dictionary says: al-fiṭra is the attribute with which everything existing is described at the first time of its creation: the natural attribute of man, the religion, the sunna, ... etc.

* Benefits:
- فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ:
The theistic philosophers, whether Muslim or non-Muslim, divided into two groups:
One group took composite scientific proofs as evidence for the existence of Allah, and the most frequent of these proofs on their tongues are "circularity and infinite regress" (al-dawr wa-l-tasalsul) and their impossibility, the proof from necessity, and the proof from existence.
The explanation of these proofs is found in the books of logic and the works of philosophers and theologians, for whoever wants to read further.
The other group resorted to the innate ideas in man, which impose themselves on many thinkers, which are easier and, by their own account, stronger in indicating the existence of Allah. Many Western philosophers have resorted to them, and many of the Muslim mystics and scholars have done so even more. This innate disposition (fiṭra), which stirs in us the sense of the existence of the great Creator, at the same time drives us to contemplate the order of this wondrous universe, beginning with ourselves and the order of our bodies, and ending with the order of plants and life, whose secrets only the scholars grasp. And above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.
I do not hide from you, dear reader, that the flower which bursts from the soil and takes its bewitching shapes and colours, and the fruit which comes out of the factories lodged in the bowels of the earth, varying in size and taste, point more to the Creator of the universe and Maker of man than the Sphinx and the Pyramids, than the great dams or the skyscrapers ... !

safi-cedvel:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (ضرّ) is the postponed fāʿil (agent) of (مسّ), nominative. (إليه) is attached to (منيبين). (منه) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (رحمة). (إذا) is the particle of suddenness (fujāʾiyya). (منهم) is attached to an adjective (naʿt) of (فريق). (بربّهم) is attached to (يشركون).
The clause «مسّ ... ضرّ» is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «دعوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «أذاقهم ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «فريق منهم ... يشركون» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «يشركون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (فريق).
(34) (اللام) is the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba) [Note: or it is the lām of command, conveying threat, so the imperfect is jussive ... and similar, in the sense of threat: "تمتّعوا.."]. (يكفروا) is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām. (بما) is attached to (يكفروا), and the second object is omitted, its implied form being "إيّاه", and it is the returning pronoun ...
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يكفروا ... ) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (يشركون).
The first (الفاء) is resumptive, and the second causal. (سوف) is a particle of futurity, and the object of (تعلمون) is omitted, i.e. "the outcome of your enjoyment".
And the clause «يكفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type (أن).
And the clause «آتيناهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «تمتّعوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «سوف تعلمون» has no grammatical position; it is causal.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
His saying: {في أَدْنَى الأرض}: some claimed that the al is a substitute for the pronoun and that the original is «في أَدْنى أَرْضِهم» ("in the nearest part of their land"); this is a Kufan view. This is on the view that the flight [al-harab] was in the direction of their [the Byzantines'] lands; as for those who say it was in the direction of the lands of the Arabs, that is not possible. [Translator's note: «الهَرَب» ("the flight") is as written in the source; the context concerns where the defeat took place.] The generality read «غُلِبَتْ» in the passive. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Ibn ʿUmar and the people of Syria [read it] in the active.
His saying: «غَلَبِهم»: on the well-known reading the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object. This object, then, is either nominative in position, on the view that the maṣdar annexed to it is taken from a passive verb — there being disagreement over that — or accusative in position, on the view that the maṣdar is from an active verb whose agent is omitted, its implied form being "after their enemy, the Persians, defeated them". On the second reading it is annexed to its agent.
His saying: «سَيَغْلِبون» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and {مِّن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ} is attached to it. The generality — indeed some reported consensus — [read] «سَيَغْلِبون» in the active. On the well-known reading it is clear, i.e. after Persia defeated them, they will defeat Persia. On the second reading, He informed that they will win a second time after having won first. It is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that he read it in the passive; this contradicts what has come regarding the occasion of the verse and in the ḥadīths. This fits to some degree with those who read «غَلَبَتْ» in the active, and it has preceded that Ibn ʿUmar is among those who read so. Al-Naḥḥās explained the reading of ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar with a good explanation, namely that the meaning is: "and Persia, after their defeating the Byzantines, will be defeated". However, there is in it the implication of something not mentioned, nor has any occasion for mentioning it occurred.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {فِي بِضْعِ}: attached to what precedes it. The explanation of البِضْع and its derivation has preceded in Yūsuf. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The original of «غَلَبِهم» is غَلَبَتِهم, with the feminine tāʾ, which was deleted because of the annexation, as in «وإقامَ الصلاةِ»." Al-Naḥḥās judged him mistaken, on the grounds that that may be said of إقام الصلاة because of its weakness [as a weak-radical form], but here there is no necessity calling for it.
Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Abū Ḥaywa read «غَلْبِهم» with sukūn on the lām; it may be an irregular lightening, or a dialectal form of the one with fatḥa, like الظَّعْن and الظَّعَن.
His saying: {مِن قَبْلُ وَمِن بَعْدُ}: the generality read them indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because they are cut off from annexation; it means: before the defeat and after it, or before every matter and after it. Al-Farrāʾ reported kasra on both without tanwīn, and al-Naḥḥās judged him mistaken, saying: "Only مِنْ قبلٍ ومِنْ بعدٍ is permissible", meaning with kasra and tanwīn. I say: it has been read so. Its rationale is that he did not intend their annexation, so he made them declinable, as in his saying:
3642 - فساغَ لي الشَّرابُ وكنتُ قَبْلاً ... أَكاد أَغَصُّ بالماءِ القَراحِ
(Then drink became pleasant to me, whereas before I would almost choke on pure water.)
[and his saying:]
3643 - ونحنُ قَتَلْنا الأُسْدَ أُسْدَ خَفِيَّةٍ ... فما شَرِبُوا بَعْداً على لَذَّةٍ خَمْرا
(We killed the lions, the lions of Khafiyya, and afterwards they never drank wine with pleasure.)
And «مِنْ قبلٍ» with tanwīn and the genitive, and «ومِنْ بعدُ» indeclinable on ḍamma, has [also] been reported.
Some explained what al-Farrāʾ reported on the basis that he assumed the muḍāf ilayhi to be present, so the first was left as it was. He recited:
3644 - . . . . . . . . . . ... بين ذراعَيْ وَجبْهةِ الأَسَدِ
(…between the two forearms and the forehead of the Lion [constellation].)
The difference is evident, for in the wording [of the verse] there is the like of what was omitted — with disagreement over the estimation of the verse as well.
His saying: «ويومَئذٍ», i.e. when the Byzantines defeat Persia. The governor of «يومَ» is «يفرحُ».

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {بِنَصْرِ الله يَنصُرُ}: of paronomasia (tajnīs); it has preceded at the end of al-Kahf.
His saying: «بِنَصْرِ الله»: the apparent view is that it is attached to «يَفْرَح». Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be attached to «يَنْصُرُ»; this breaks up the arrangement [of the text].

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {وَعْدَ الله}: an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) whose governor is implied, i.e. "Allah promised them that, a promise". His saying {لاَ يُخْلِفُ الله وَعْدَهُ} confirms the meaning of this maṣdar. It may [also] be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the maṣdar, so it is like a qualified maṣdar and thus clarifies the kind, as though it were said: "Allah promised a promise not broken".

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {في أَنفُسِهِمْ}: an adverbial of the reflecting, not the object of the reflecting, since its object is [that] He created the heavens and the earth.
His saying: «ما خَلَقَ»: «ما» is negating. In this clause there are two views. The first: that it is resumptive, with no connection to what precedes it. The second: that it suspends (muʿalliqa) the reflecting, so it is in the position of an accusative by dropping the preposition. It is weak that it be interrogative with the meaning of negation; the two mentioned views apply to it.
And «بالحقِّ» is either causal or circumstantial.
His saying: «بلقاءِ» is attached to «لَكافرون»; the lām does not prevent that, since it is within the scope of «إنَّ».

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا}: an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a cultivation greater than their cultivation". It was also read «وآثاروا», with an alif after the hamza, which is an extension (ishbāʿ) of the fatḥa of the hamza.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {عَاقِبَةَ الذين}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it in the nominative, the rest in the accusative. The nominative is on the view that it is the noun of كان, the verb being masculine because the femininity is metaphorical. In the khabar (predicate) there are then two views. The first: «السُّوْءَى», i.e. the evil deed or the evil trait. The second: «أَنْ كَذَّبوا», i.e. the end of their affair was the denial. On the first, there are two views on «أَنْ كَذَّبوا». The first: that it is by dropping the preposition — either the lām of cause, i.e. "because they denied", or the bāʾ of causation, i.e. "for their denying"; when the particle was dropped, the two well-known views between al-Khalīl and Sībawayh about the position of «أَنْ» apply. The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from «السُّوْءَى», i.e. "then their end was the denial". On the second, «السُّوْءَى» is a maṣdar of «أساءُوا», or an adjective of an omitted object, i.e. "they committed the evil deed"; السُّوْءَى is the feminine of الأَسْوَأ ("the worst").
Some permitted the khabar of كان to be omitted for the sake of vagueness (ibhām), with السُّوْءَى either a maṣdar or an object, as preceded, i.e. "they committed the evil sin", i.e. "their end was destruction".
As for the accusative, it is as the khabar of كان. In the noun there are two views. The first: السُّوْءى, i.e. "the evil deed was the end of the evildoers", with «أنْ كَذَّبُوا» as preceded. The second: that the noun is «أنْ كَذَّبُوا», with السُّوْءَى also as preceded.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {يُبْلِسُ}: the generality read it in the active, which is the well-known [usage]; one says أَبْلَسَ الرجلُ, i.e. his argument broke off and he fell silent; so it is intransitive. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
3645 - يا صاحِ هل تَعْرِفُ رَسْماً مُكَرَّسَاً ... قال نعم أعرِفُه وأَبْلَسا
(O companion, do you recognize a trace caked [with dung]? He said: "Yes, I recognize it" — and fell silent in despair.)
Al-Sulamī read «يُبْلَسُ» in the passive, and there is remoteness in it, because أَبْلَسَ is not transitive. This reading has been explained on the basis that what stands in place of the agent is the maṣdar of the verb; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, since the original is "the despairing of the criminals will be despaired". And «يُبْلِس» is the governor of «يومَ تقومُ».

semin-durr:14-14.t: And {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: annexed to a clause, its implied form being "on the day when it rises". This is as if it were a verbal emphasis, since the implied form becomes: "the criminals will despair on the day the Hour rises, on the day the Hour rises".

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {يُحْبَرُونَ}, i.e. they will be made glad. الحَبْر and الحُبُور: gladness. It has been said: it is from التحبير, which is beautifying. One says: هو حَسَنُ الحِبْر والسِّبر ("he is of fine appearance and complexion"), with kasra on the ḥāʾ and the sīn and with fatḥa on them. In the ḥadīth: «يَخْرج من النارِ رجلٌ ذَهَبَ حِبْرُه وسِبْرُه» ("A man will come out of the Fire whose beauty and complexion have gone"). The form with fatḥa is a maṣdar and the one with kasra is a noun.
الرَّوضة is a garden. It has been said: it is not a رَوْضة unless there are plants in it; and it has been said: unless there is water in it; and it has been said: it is what is low-lying, while the elevated one is called a تُرْعَة; and it has been said: it is not called a رَوْضة unless it is in a rough, elevated place. Al-Aʿshā said:
3646 - ما رَوْضَةٌ مِنْ رياض الحَزْنِ مُعْشِبَةٌ ... خضراءُ جادَ عليها مُسْبِلٌ هَطِلُ
(No meadow of the meadows of the rugged upland, grassy and green, on which a pouring, streaming cloud has rained generously…)
The original of رِياض is رِواض; the wāw was changed to a yāʾ, in the manner of حَوْض and حِياض.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {حِينَ تُمْسُونَ}: تُمْسُون and تُصْبحون are complete (tāmm), i.e. "you enter upon the evening and the morning", as in their saying: «إذا سَمِعْتَ بسُرى القَيْنِ فاعلَمْ بأنَّه مُصْبِحٌ» ("If you hear of the smith's night-travelling, know that he is staying till morning"), i.e. staying in the morning. The generality [read it] with the adverbial annexed to the verb after it. ʿIkrima read «حيناً» with tanwīn, the clause after it being an adjective of it; the referent pronoun is then omitted, i.e. "you enter the evening in it", as in His saying {واخشوا يَوْماً لاَّ يَجْزِي وَالِدٌ عَن وَلَدِهِ} [Luqmān: 33]. The governor of this adverbial is «سُبْحانَ», because it stands in for its governor.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {وَعَشِيّاً}: conjoined to «حينَ», and what is between them is parenthetical. And «في السماوات» may be attached to «الحمد» itself, i.e. praise is in these two places.

semin-durr:19-19.t: The disagreement of the readers over the light and doubled «الميت» has preceded, and likewise His saying «تُخْرَجون» in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf. And «كذلك» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "and like that wondrous bringing forth will you be brought forth".

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَكُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. "and among the signs of His oneness and that He will resurrect you is His creating and originating you"; «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent.
His saying: {ثُمَّ إِذَآ أَنتُمْ}: the sequence and the delay are evident here, since they only become human beings after many stages. «وتَنْتشرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). «إذا» is the one of surprise (fujāʾiyya); however, the [إذا of] surprise most often occurs after the fāʾ, because it requires immediate succession. The rationale of its occurring with «ثُمَّ» is relative to what befits the particular state, i.e. after those stages which He related to us elsewhere — our being a drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump, then bare bone, then bone clothed with flesh — humanity and spreading came suddenly.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {واختلاف أَلْسِنَتِكُمْ}, i.e. your languages, Arab and non-Arab, along with the diversification of each of the two groups into various kinds, especially the non-Arabs, for their languages differ. What is meant by the tongues is not the bodily organs.
His saying: «للعالمين»: Ḥafṣ read it with kasra on the lām, making it the plural of عالِم ("one who knows"), the opposite of ignorant; similar to it is {وَمَا يَعْقِلُهَآ إِلاَّ العالمون} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 43]. The rest [read it] with fatḥa, because they are signs for all people, even if some of them are heedless of them. The discussion of «العالمين» — whether it is a plural or a collective noun — has preceded at the beginning of al-Fātiḥa, so consult it there.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {مَنَامُكُم بالليل والنهار}: it has been said: in the verse there is fronting and postponement, so that each one is with what suits it; the implied form is: "and among His signs is your sleeping by night and your seeking of His bounty by day"; the preposition was omitted because of its being joined to «الليل» and conjoined to it, since the conjunction may stand in place of the preposition. It is better to leave it as it is: sleeping by day is something the Arabs counted as a blessing from Allah, especially at the times of the midday rest (qaylūla) in hot lands.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {يُرِيكُمُ البرق}: there are several views in it. The first — which is the apparent one and agrees with its sisters — that it is a clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), except that the infinitival particle was omitted, and when it was omitted its governance was cancelled. The original is: "and among His signs is that He shows you", as in his saying:
3647 - ألا أيُّهذا الزاجرِيْ أَحْضُرُ الوغَى ... . . . . . . . . . .
(O you who reproach me [for] attending the battle…)
The second: that «مِنْ آياتِه» is attached to «يُرِيكم», or to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «البرق»; the implied form is "and He shows you the lightning as one of His signs", so He has conjoined a verbal clause to a nominal clause. The third: that «يُرِيْكُم» is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "and among His signs is a sign by which — or in which — He shows you the lightning", the qualified noun and its referent pronoun being omitted. Like it:
3648 - وما الدَّهْرُ إلاَّ تارَتان فمِنْهما ... موتُ. . . . . . . . . .
(Time is but two turns: of them [is one in which] I die…)
i.e. "of them is a turn in which I die". [Translator's note: the source prints «موتُ»; the explanation reads it as «أموتُ».] The fourth: that the implied form is "and among His signs is a cloud", or "a thing that shows you"; so «يُريكم» is an adjective of that implied [noun], and the agent of «يُريكم» is a pronoun referring to it — unlike the preceding view, in which the agent is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {مِّنَ الأرض}: there are several views in it. The first: that it is attached to «دَعاكم», and this is the most apparent.
The second: that it is attached to something omitted as an adjective of «دَعْوة». The third: that it is attached to something omitted indicated by «تَخْرُجون», i.e. "you came out of the earth"; it may not be attached to «تَخْرُجون», because what follows «إذا» does not govern what precedes it. Al-Zamakhsharī has a fine expression here.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ}: in «أَهْوَن» there are two views. The first: that it is for preference (tafḍīl), in its proper sense. On this it is asked: how can preference be conceived, when repeating and beginning are, in relation to Allah the Exalted, exactly equal? There are several answers to that. The first: that it is relative to human belief based on observation — that repeating a thing is easier than inventing it, since beginning usually needs the exercise of thought — even though this is negated of the Creator, Glorified and Exalted; so they were addressed according to what they were accustomed to.
The second: that the pronoun in «عليه» does not refer to Allah the Exalted but to the creation, i.e. "the return is easier for the creation", i.e. quicker, because the beginning involves gradation from stage to stage until it becomes a human, while the repetition does not need these gradations; so it is as though it were said: "it is shorter for it, easier, and with less transition".
The third: that the pronoun in «عليه» refers to the created being, meaning: "repetition is easier for the created being", i.e. his repeating something after he has made it; this is in the custom of created beings, so how do they deny it on the side of Allah the Exalted? [The second of the two views:] that «أهونُ» is not for preference but is an adjective meaning هَيِّن ("easy"), as in their saying اللَّهُ أكبرُ, [i.e.] "the Great". The apparent view is that the pronoun in «عليه» refers to the Creator, the Exalted, so as to agree with the pronoun in His saying {وَلَهُ المثل الأعلى}. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was the adjunct (ṣila) postponed in His saying {وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ} and fronted in His saying {هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ}? I say: there, restriction was intended, and that is its proper place, so it was said: 'it is easy for Me', even though you find it hard that [a child] be born between a decrepit old man and a barren woman. Here, however, restriction has no meaning; how could it, when the matter is built on what they understand, that repeating is easier than beginning? Had the adjunct been fronted, the meaning would have changed." The Shaykh said: "His words are built on fronting conveying restriction; we have discussed it with him and not conceded it." I say: the correct view is that it does convey it, and all of that has preceded.
His saying: {وَلَهُ المثل الأعلى}: it may be linked to what precedes it, namely His saying {وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ}, i.e. He has struck it for you as a likeness in what is easy and what is difficult — al-Zajjāj inclined to this — or to what follows it, namely His saying {ضَرَبَ لَكُمْ مَّثَلاً مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ} [al-Rūm: 28]. It has been said: المَثَل is the description. And «وفي السماوات» may be attached to «الأَعْلى», i.e. He is exalted in these two realms; or it may be attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأعلى», or from «المَثَل», or from the pronoun in «الأَعْلى», since it refers to «المَثَل».
His saying: «مِنْ أَنْفُسكم»: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, in the position of an adjective of «مَثَلاً», i.e. He took a likeness and drew it from the nearest thing to you, which is yourselves. [Translator's note: this last paragraph pertains to verse 28 but appears under this entry in the source.]

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {هَلْ لَّكُمْ مِّن مَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ مِّن شُرَكَآءَ}: «مِنْ شركاء» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in it because the two conditions for redundancy are present. In its khabar (predicate) there are two views. The first: the first preposition-phrase, which is «لكم». And {مِّن مَّا مَلَكَتْ} may be attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شركاءَ», because it is originally an adjective of an indefinite noun that was fronted before it; its governor is the governor of this preposition-phrase that serves as khabar. The khabar is implied after the mubtadaʾ, and {فِي مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ} is attached to «شركاء». [And the «ما» in «ممَّا» means "kind".] The implied form of all of this is: "Are there partners in what We have provided you, being of the kind that your right hands possess, established for you?" So "being" is the adjective to which «ممَّا مَلَكَتْ» is attached, and when it was fronted it became a ḥāl; and "established" is the khabar to which «لكم» is attached.
The second: that the khabar is «مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ», and «لكم» is attached to what the khabar is attached to, or to something omitted as a ḥāl from «شركاء», or to «شركاء» itself, as in your saying «لك في الدنيا مُحِبٌّ» ("you have in the world a lover"), where «لك» is attached to مُحِبّ and «في الدنيا» is the khabar.
His saying: {فَأَنتُمْ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌ}: this clause is the answer to the interrogative that has the meaning of negation, and «فيه» is attached to «سَواء».
His saying: «تَخافونهم»: there are two views in it. The first: that it is a second khabar of «أنتم», its implied form being: "so you are equal with them in what We have provided you, fearing them as you, the masters, fear one another". What is meant is the negation of the three things — I mean the partnership, the equality with the slaves, and their fearing them. What is meant is not the affirmation of the partnership and the negation of the equality and the fear, as in one of the two views on your saying «ما تأتينا فتحدِّثَنا», meaning "you do not come to us talking", i.e. you do come to us but do not talk to us; rather what is meant is the negation of all, as preceded.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "{فَأَنتُمْ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌ}: the clause is in the position of an accusative as the answer to the interrogative, i.e. 'do you have … so that you would be equal?'" End quote. There is room for consideration in this: how can he make a nominal clause stand in place of a verbal clause and judge the position of the nominal clause to be accusative by an implied governor? This is not permissible. Had he explained the meaning and said that if the verb were placed after the fāʾ it would be accusative by an implied «أن», it would have been correct. It must also be made clear that the accusative is according to the meaning I have presented, of negating the three things.
The second view: that «تخافونهم» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in «سَواء», i.e. "so you would be equal, each of you fearing the other's partnership with him in property"; i.e. if you are not content that your slaves be partners with you in property, how do you associate with Allah one who is made by Him? Abū al-Baqāʾ said this.
Al-Rāzī mentioned a fine meaning, namely: "Between the likeness and what it is likened to there is resemblance and difference. The resemblance is known; the difference is in several respects. His saying «مِنْ أنفسكم», i.e. from your own kind, despite the lowliness, deficiency and incapacity of the souls — and He compared Himself to you despite His majesty, greatness and power. His saying {مِّن مَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ}, i.e. your slaves: ownership is incidental, subject to transfer by sale and to removal by manumission, whereas what the Exalted owns never leaves His ownership. So if it is not permissible that your slave be your partner — he being your like when freed in every respect, and your like in humanity while in slavery — how can there be associated with Allah the Exalted what He owns in every respect, totally distinct from Him? And His saying «فيما رَزَقْنَاكم» means that it is not really yours; it belongs only to Allah the Exalted and to whom He truly provides. So if it is not permissible [for a slave] to share with you in what is yours in name, how can He the Exalted have a partner in what is His in reality?" End quote. I have only mentioned this meaning at length because it clarifies the views of i'rab I have mentioned.
His saying: «كَخِيْفَتِكم», i.e. "a fear like your fear". The generality [read] «أنفسَكم» in the accusative, because the maṣdar is annexed to its agent. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it in the nominative, by annexing the maṣdar to its object. Some considered this ugly when the agent is present; others said: it is not ugly; rather it may be annexed to either of them when both are present. He recited:
3649 - أَفْنَى تِلادي وما جَمَّعْتُ مِنْ نَشَبٍ ... قَرْعُ القواريزِ أفواهَ الأباريقِ
(What wiped out my inherited wealth and the property I gathered was the knocking of glasses against the mouths of the ewers.)
with «الأفواه» in the accusative and the nominative.
His saying: «كذلك نُفَصِّل», i.e. "like that clear detailing do We detail". Abū ʿAmr read, in one transmission, «يُفَصِّلُ» with the yāʾ of the third person, referring back to His saying «ضَرَبَ لكم»; the rest in the first person, referring back to His saying «رَزَقْناكم».

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {حَنِيفاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «أَقِمْ», or from its object, or from «الدِّين».
His saying: «فِطْرَةَ الله»: there are two views on it. The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) giving emphasis to the content of the sentence, like His saying {صِبْغَةَ الله} [al-Baqara: 138] and {صُنْعَ الله} [al-Naml: 88]. The second: it is accusative by an implied verb. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "That is, 'hold fast to the fiṭra of Allah'. I implied it in the address to the plural because of His saying «مُنِيبيْن إليه», which is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «الزَموا». And His saying «واتَّقوه، وأقيموا، ولا تكونوا» is conjoined to this implied verb." Then he said: "or [it is implied as] 'upon you the fiṭra'." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected it: "because the word of incitement (kalimat al-ighrāʾ) is not omitted, for it is a substitute for the verb; were you to delete it, the deletion of both the substitute and what it substitutes for would follow, and that is a severe abridgement." I say: this is the opinion of the Basrans. As for al-Kisāʾī and his followers, they permit it.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {مُنِيبِينَ}: a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «الزموا», the implied verb, as has preceded; or from the fāʿil of «أَقِمْ» according to the sense, because what is meant by it is not one particular person; rather, everyone is meant. It was also said: a ḥāl from «الناس» when the believers are meant by them. Al-Zajjāj said: after His saying «وَجْهَكَ» there is an omitted maʿṭūf (conjoined element), its implied form being: "so set your face and [that of] your community", so the ḥāl is from all of them. The omission of the conjoined element is permissible because «مُنيبين» points to it, just as its omission is permissible in His saying {ياأيها النبي} [al-Ṭalāq: 1], that is, "and the people", because {إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ} points to it. So al-Zajjāj claimed regarding {ياأيها النبي}. It was also said: it is conjoined to the khabar (predicate) of kāna, that is, "be turning [to Him]", because His saying «ولا تكونوا» points to it.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {فَرِحُونَ}: the apparent view is that it is the khabar of «كلُّ حِزْب». Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be nominative as an adjective of «كل», saying: "It is also possible that «من الذين» is disconnected from what precedes it. Its meaning: 'of those who departed from their religion, every party is rejoicing in what it has'. But he made «فرحين» nominative as an adjective of «كل», like his saying:
3650 - وكلُّ خليلٍ غيرُ هاضمِ نَفْسِه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Every close friend is not one who wrongs himself ...)".
The Shaykh said: "He first supposed «فرحين» to be genitive, an adjective of «حِزْب»; then he said: 'but it is nominative as an adjective of «كل»', because when you say «مِنْ قومِك كلُّ رجلٍ صالح», the genitive is permissible for «صالح» as an adjective of «رجل», and it is the more frequent, as in his saying:
3651 - جادَتْ عليه كلُّ عينٍ ثَرَّةٍ ... فَتَرَكْنَ كلَّ حديقةٍ كالدِّرْهمِ
(Every copious-flowing spring poured upon it, and left every garden like a silver coin.)
and the nominative is also permissible as an adjective of «كل», as in his saying:
3652 - وَلِهَتْ عليه كلُّ مُعْصِفَةٍ ... هَوْجاءُ ليس لِلُبِّها زَبْرُ
(Every raging gale was frantic over it, a wild one with no restraint in its core.)
with «هوجاء» nominative as an adjective of «كل»." End of quotation. It is a fine exposition.

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {إِذَا فَرِيقٌ}: this «إذا» is the one of sudden occurrence (al-fujāʾiyya), which occurs as the apodosis of the condition because it is like the fāʾ in indicating immediate succession; it does not occur at the beginning of a discourse, and the fāʾ may accompany it as a redundant element.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {لِيَكْفُرُواْ}: it may be the lām of purpose (lām kay), or the lām of command, its meaning being a threat, like {اعملوا مَا شِئْتُمْ} [Fuṣṣilat: 40].
His saying: «فَتَمَتَّعُوْا»: the majority read it, and «تَعْلمون», in the second person. Abū al-ʿĀliya read both with yāʾ [third person], the former being passive. And from him: «فَيَتَمَتَّعوا» with a yāʾ before the tāʾ. And from ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd]: «فَلْيَتَمَتعوا» with the lām of command.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {سُلْطَاناً}: that is, proof and argument. If we take it as literal, then «يتكلم» is figurative; and if we take it as literal, then «يتكلم» is figurative; and if we take it as an omitted muḍāf, that is, "possessing authority", then «يتكلَّم» is literal. [Translator's note: the source repeats the clause "if we take it as literal, then «يتكلم» is figurative" twice; it is translated as written.] Abū al-Baqāʾ said here: "It was also said: it is the plural of «سَلِيْط», like «رَغِيف» and «رُغْفان»." End of quotation. This is not permissible, because it would have been proper to say «فهم يتكلمون». And «فهو يتكلمُّ» is the answer to the question contained in the disconnected «أم».

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {لِّيَرْبُوَ}: the majority read it with a fatḥa-vowelled yāʾ (from below), attributing the verb to the pronoun of «الرِّبا», that is, "so that it may increase". Nāfiʿ read it with a ḍamma-vowelled tāʾ (from above) as an address to the group. So the wāw in the first reading is the lām (root letter) of the word, and in the second it is the pronoun for a plural masculine addressee. The two readings of «آتيتم», with the long and the short vowel, have already been discussed in al-Baqara.
His saying: «المُضْعِفُون»: that is, "those who possess multiples". Al-Farrāʾ said: "like «مُسْمِن» and «مُعْطِش», that is, one who has fat camels and thirsty camels." Ubayy read it with a fatḥa on the ʿayn, taking it as a passive participle.
And His saying «فأولئك هم»: al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a fine iltifāt (shift of address), as if He [said] to His angels: 'Those who desire the face of Allah by their charity, they are the ones who receive multiples. The meaning: they are the ones who receive multiples by it, because there must be a pronoun returning to «ما»'." End of quotation. He means that when the conditional noun is not an adverbial, a pronoun must return to it from the apodosis. That was discussed in al-Baqara at His saying {قُلْ مَن كَانَ عَدُوّاً لِّجِبْرِيلَ} [al-Baqara: 97], the verse. Then he said: "There is another view: its implied form is «فَمُؤْتُوْه فأولئك هم المُضْعَفُون» ('those who give it, those are the ones whose reward is multiplied'). The omission is because the discourse contains evidence for it. This is easier to derive, while the first is richer in benefit."

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {الله الذي خَلَقَكُمْ}: two views are possible regarding the khabar of the majestic Name. The more apparent: it is the relative noun after it. The second: it is the sentence {هَلْ مِن شُرَكَآئِكُمْ مَّن يَفْعَلُ}, with the relative noun being an adjective of the majestic Name. Al-Zamakhsharī supposed the link (rābiṭ) between the mubtadaʾ and the sentence serving as khabar, saying: "His saying «مِنْ ذلكم» is what links the sentence to the mubtadaʾ, because its meaning is 'of His deeds'." The Shaykh said: "What the grammarians have mentioned is that a demonstrative serves as a link when it points to the mubtadaʾ; as for «ذلك» here, it is not a pointer to the mubtadaʾ, but it resembles what al-Farrāʾ allowed of linking by meaning, which people opposed, namely in His saying {والذين يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْوَاجاً يَتَرَبَّصْنَ} [al-Baqara: 234]. He said: 'The implied form is: «يتربَّصُ أزواجُهم» ("their wives wait")'. So he supposed the link through a muḍāf attached to the pronoun of «الذين», and the link is achieved by it. Likewise al-Zamakhsharī supposed «من ذلكم» to be «من أفعاله» ("of His deeds"), with a muḍāf attached to the pronoun that returns to the mubtadaʾ."
His saying: «مِنْ شركائِكم»: a fronted khabar, and «مِنْ» is partitive. «مَنْ يَفْعَلُ» is the mubtadaʾ. And «مِنْ ذلكم» is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl from «شيء» after it, for in origin it is an adjective of it. The third «مِنْ» is redundant (mazīda) on the direct object, because it falls within the scope of the negation derived from the question. The implied form is: "Which of your partners does anything of that?"
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The first and second «مِنْ» are each independent in giving emphasis, in order to render their partners incapable and to declare their worshippers ignorant." The Shaykh said: "I do not know what he meant by this statement."
And al-Aʿmash read «تُشْرِكون» in the second person.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {بِمَا كَسَبَتْ}: that is, "because of their earning". The bāʾ is attached to «ظَهَر», or to «الفساد» itself, which is remote.
His saying: «لِيُذِيقَهم»: the lām expresses cause and is attached to «ظهر». It was also said: to an omitted element, that is, "He punished them with that in order to make them taste". It was also said: the lām expresses consequence (ṣayrūra). Qunbul read «لنُذِيْقَهم» with the nūn of majesty ("that We may make them taste"); the others read it with the yāʾ of the third person.

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {لاَّ مَرَدَّ لَهُ}: «المَرَدُّ» is the maṣdar of «رَدَّ». And «مِن الله» may be attached to «يأتي», or to an omitted element that the maṣdar indicates, that is, "no one can repel it from Allah". It is not permissible for «مَرَدّ» to govern it, because it would then have had to take tanwīn, since it would belong to the category of the "lengthened" (muṭawwal) constructions.

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {فَعَلَيْهِ كُفْرُهُ} and «فلأَنْفُسِهم يَمْهَدون»: the fronting of the two prepositional phrases indicates restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ), meaning that the harm of this one's disbelief and the benefit of that one's deed do not pass beyond him.

semin-durr:45-45.t: His saying: {لِيَجْزِيَ}: there are several views about what it is attached to. The first: «يَمْهدون». The second: «يَصَّدَّعون». The third: an omitted element. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its implied form is «ذلك ليجزيَ» ('that is so that He may recompense'), with the pointer referring to what was established in His saying «مَنْ كفر» and «مَنْ عمل»." The Shaykh made the counterpart of His saying {الذين آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ} omitted, because His saying {إِنَّهُ لاَ يُحِبُّ الكافرين} indicates it. This is when we attach the lām to «يَصَّدَّعون» or to that omitted element. He said: "Its implied form: «ليجزيَ الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحاتِ مِنْ فَضْلِه والكافرين بعَدْلِه» ('so that He may recompense those who believed and did righteous deeds out of His bounty, and the disbelievers by His justice')".

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {الرياح}: the majority read «الرياحَ» in the plural, because of «مبشِّراتٍ». Al-Aʿmash read it in the singular, intending the genus, because of «مبشِّرات».
His saying: «ولِيُذيْقَكم»: either it is conjoined to the meaning of «مُبَشِّرات», because the ḥāl and the adjective suggest the reason, so the implied form is as if "so that He may give glad tidings and so that He may make you taste"; or it is attached to an omitted element, or "He sent them so that He may make you taste"; or the wāw is redundant according to one opinion, so the lām is attached to «أَنْ يُرْسِلَ».

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {وَكَانَ حَقّاً}: some of the reciters of pauses (waqafa) pause at «حقاً» and begin with what follows, making the ism of kāna a latent pronoun in it and «حقاً» its khabar, that is, "and the vengeance was a right". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is weak, because he did not recognize the worth of what he presented in the structure of the verse", meaning pausing at «حَقَّاً». Some made «حَقَّاً» accusative as a maṣdar, with the ism of kāna being the pronoun of the affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), «علينا» a fronted khabar and «نَصْرُ» a postponed mubtadaʾ. Some also made «حقاً» accusative as a maṣdar, with «علينا» a fronted khabar and «نَصْرُ» a postponed ism. [Translator's note: the source states these two views almost identically, differing only in calling «نصر» a "mubtadaʾ" in the first and an "ism" in the second; translated as written.] The sound view is that «نَصْر» is its ism, «حَقَّاً» its khabar, and «علينا» is attached to «حَقاً» or to an omitted element serving as an adjective of it.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {مِّن قَبْلِهِ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is a repetition of the first «مِنْ قَبلِ» by way of emphasis. The second: it is not a repetition. That is by making the pronoun in «قَبْله» refer to the cloud (al-saḥāb), which is permissible because it is a generic noun that may be treated as masculine or feminine; or to the wind, in which case the second «مِنْ» is attached to «يُنَزَّل». It was also said: the pronoun may return to «كِسَفا»; so Abū al-Baqāʾ stated unrestrictedly, while the Shaykh restricted it to the reading of the one who vowelled the sīn with sukūn. The readings of «كِسَفاً» have already been discussed in [Sūrat] Subḥān. People have said much about this place; I saw fit to mention it to clarify its meaning.
Each of the two masters, al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya, has shown the benefit of the mentioned emphasis. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It conveys the swift turning of human hearts from despair (iblās) to rejoicing; for His saying {مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ} admits a span of time, that is, 'before it is sent down upon them' by much, such as days and the like; so «مِنْ قبله» came, meaning that this is directly connected to the rain, so it is a useful emphasis."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The sense of emphasis in it is to indicate that their last experience of rain was long ago, so their despair became firm and their dejection persisted, and their rejoicing was proportionate to their distress at that." It is a fine statement.
Except that the Shaykh did not approve of it from the two, saying: "What they mentioned about the benefit of emphasis is not apparent; it is merely for emphasis, and it serves only to remove figurative interpretation." End of quotation. I do not know why it is not apparent. Qutrub said: "Even if they were, before the sending down, before the rain." It was also said: the implied form is "before the sending down of the rain, before they sowed", and the rain pointed to the crops, because they come out by means of the rain. His saying «فَرَأَوْه مُصْفَرَّاً» points to that, meaning the crops. The Shaykh said: "This does not hold, because {مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُنَزَّلَ} is attached to «مُبْلِسِيْن», and it is not possible for «من قبل الزرع» to be attached to «مبلسين», because two prepositions are not attached to a single governing element except by means of a conjunction or a substitution, and there is no conjunction here; substitution is not permissible, since the sending down of the rain is not the crops, nor are the crops part of it. A badal al-ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) may be imagined here, with strain: either because the sending down includes the crops, in the sense that the crops arise from the sending down, so the sending down as if includes them. This is according to the school of those who say that the first includes the second."
Al-Mubarrad said: "The second is the cloud, because when they saw the cloud they were hoping for rain." End of quotation. He means "before seeing the cloud". This too requires a conjunction so that the attachment of the two prepositions to «مبلسين» is valid. Al-Rummānī said: "before the sending [of the winds]." And al-Kirmānī: "before the rejoicing, because He joined it with despair, and because He bestowed rejoicing upon them." Their statement requires a conjunction for what has preceded, and claiming an omitted conjunction is not easy, for there is disagreement about it: some allow it by analogy and some do not. All this applies to single words. As for sentences, there is no disagreement about analogical use of it.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {إلى آثَارِ}: Ibn ʿĀmir, the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read it in the plural; the others in the singular. And Sallām read it with a kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the thāʾ, which is a dialectal variant of it.
The majority read «كيف يُحْيي» with the yāʾ of the third person, that is, "the trace of the mercy" for the one who read the singular; and for the one who read the plural, the verb is attributed to Allah the Exalted, and this is also possible with the singular. Al-Jaḥdarī, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn al-Samayfiʿ read «تُحْيي» with the feminine tāʾ. There are two analyses of it. The more apparent: the agent returns to the mercy. The second, said by Abū al-Faḍl: it returns to «أثر», and «أثر» was made feminine because it acquired feminine gender by annexation, like similar cases that have preceded. It was refuted: the condition for that is that the muḍāf be in the sense of the muḍāf ilayhi, or be part of it, not extraneous, and this is extraneous. And «كيف يُحْيي» suspends [the effect of] «انظرْ», so it is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition. Abū al-Fatḥ said: "The sentence «كيف يُحْيي» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, by carrying it on the meaning." End of quotation. But how can a sentence of interrogation occur as a ḥāl?

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: {فَرَأَوْهُ}: that is, "they saw the vegetation", because the context points to it; or [the pronoun returns] to the «أثر», because the mercy is the rain and its trace is the vegetation. This is apparent with the reading in the singular; with the reading in the plural it returns by meaning. It was also said: the pronoun is for the cloud. It was also said: for the wind. Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read «مُصْفارَّاً» with an alif. And «لَظَلُّوا» is the answer to the oath prepared for by «لَئِنْ», and it is past in form but future in meaning, like His saying {مَّا تَبِعُواْ قِبْلَتَكَ} [al-Baqara: 145].
The discussion of the like of {فَإِنَّكَ لاَ تُسْمِعُ} to the end has preceded in al-Anbiyāʾ and in al-Naml, and likewise the two readings of «ضعف» and what the difference between them is in al-Anfāl.
The pronoun in «مِنْ بعدِه» returns to the yellowing (iṣfirār), which is indicated by the adjective, as in his saying:
3653 - إذا نُهِي السَّفيهُ جَرَى إليه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When the fool is forbidden, he runs toward it ...)
that is, toward foolishness (safah), because «السَّفيه» points to it.

semin-durr:55-55.t: His saying: {مَا لَبِثُواْ}: the answer to His saying «يُقْسِم», and it is according to the meaning, since had their statement been reported exactly it would have been «ما لَبِثْنا». And «كذلك» means "in the manner of that deception they were deceived".

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {فِي كِتَابِ الله}: the apparent view is that it is attached to «لَبِثْتم», in the sense of "in what He promised in His Book of the gathering and the resurrection". Qatāda said: [it is] by fronting and postponing, the implied form being: "and those who were given knowledge said: 'You have remained, in the Book of Allah ...'", and «في» is in the sense of «الباء», that is, "knowledge of the Book of Allah". That coming from Qatāda is unlikely.
The majority read «البعث» with sukūn on the ʿayn. Al-Ḥasan read it with fatḥa, and it was read with kasra. The kasra form is a noun, and the fatḥa form is a maṣdar.
His saying: «فهذا يومُ»: regarding the fāʾ there are two views. The more apparent: it conjoins this sentence to «لَقَدْ لَبِثْتُمْ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the answer to an implied condition, as in his saying:
3654 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . فقد جِئْنا خُراسانا
(... then we have come to Khurasan.)
as if it were said: if what you said is true, that Khurasan is the farthest that is intended for us, and it is time for us to be released, so too, if you were deniers of the resurrection, then this is the Day of Resurrection." He alludes to the well-known verse, which is:
قالوا: خراسانُ أَقْصى ما يُراد بنا ... ثم القُفولُ فقد جِئْنا خُراسانا
(They said: Khurasan is the farthest that is intended for us, then the return; and we have come to Khurasan.)
His saying: «لا تَعْلَمُوْن»: that is, the resurrection, that is, what was intended for you; or no object is supposed for it, that is, they were not among those possessing knowledge. This is more eloquent.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying: {فَيَوْمَئِذٍ}: that is, "when that occurs, and those who were given knowledge say that statement".
His saying: «لا يَنْفَعُ»: it is what governs «يومئذٍ» before it in the accusative. The Kufans read it here and in [Sūrat] Ghāfir with the yāʾ (masculine). Nāfiʿ agreed with them on what is in Ghāfir, because the feminine is figurative and because there is also a separation. The others read both with the feminine, observing the form.
His saying: {وَلاَ هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "From your saying «اسْتَعْتَبني فلانٌ فَأَعْتَبْتُه», that is, 'he sought my satisfaction and I satisfied him', and likewise when you were the one who wronged him. The true sense of «أَعْتَبْتَه» is 'you removed his reproach'. Do you not see his saying:
3655 - غَضِبَتْ تميمٌ أَنْ يُقتَّل عامرٌ ... يومَ النسارِ فَأُعْتِبُوا بالصَّيْلَمِ
(Tamīm became angry that ʿĀmir was killed on the day of al-Nisār, so they were appeased with calamity.)
how he made them angry? Then he said «فَأُعْتِبوا», that is, their anger was removed. And anger is in the sense of reproach. The meaning: it will not be said to them, 'Satisfy your Lord with repentance and obedience.' Similar is His saying the Exalted {فاليوم لاَ يُخْرَجُونَ مِنْهَا وَلاَ هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ} [al-Jāthiya: 35]. If you say: how were they made not seekers of satisfaction in some verses and not satisfied in others, namely His saying {وَإِن يَسْتَعْتِبُواْ فَمَا هُم مِّنَ المعتبين} [Fuṣṣilat: 24]? I say: as for their not being seekers of satisfaction, this is its meaning; and as for their not being satisfied, its meaning is that they are not content with what they are in, so their state was likened to that of people who were wronged and so are reproaching the wrongdoer, not content with him because of what they are in. So if they seek the satisfaction of Allah, that is, ask Him to remove what they are in, they are not among those who are answered." End of quotation.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«ويَسْتَعْتِبون» is in the sense of «يَعْتِبون», as you say «يَمْلك» and «يَستملك». The usual sense of the form istafʿala is seeking a thing, and this is not of that, because the meaning would be corrupted, since what would be understood from it is: 'and no reproach is sought from them'." I say: it is not corrupt, because of what has preceded from the statement of Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī].

semin-durr:58-58.t: His saying: {وَلَئِن جِئْتَهُمْ}: it is singular here and plural afterwards in His saying «أنتم» for a subtle reason, namely that He the Exalted informed in another place, saying: "and if you bring them every sign", that is, as the messengers brought. So the disbelievers said: "You, O you who claim messengership, are all nothing but such-and-such."

semin-durr:59-59.t: His saying: {كَذَلِكَ يَطْبَعُ}: that is, "He seals in the manner of that sealing".

semin-durr:60-60.t: His saying: {وَلاَ يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ}: the majority read it from «الاستخفاف» (making light of), with a dotted khāʾ and fāʾ. Yaʿqūb and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with an undotted ḥāʾ and a qāf, from «الاستحقاق» (claiming a right over). Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Yaʿqūb [read it] with the nūn of emphasis lightened. And the prohibition belongs to the pattern of their saying «لا أُرَيَنَّكَ ههنا» ("let me not see you here").

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يُبْلِسُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ (١٢))
(يُبْلِسُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ): the majority read it with the agent named (active voice).
A reading leaving the agent unnamed (passive) has been reported as anomalous (shādhdh); this is far-fetched, because أَبْلَسَ has not been used as a transitive verb. Its justification is that the maṣdar (verbal noun) was put in place of the fāʿil (agent) and then omitted, and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place; i.e. يُبْلِسُ إِبْلَاسَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ ("the despairing of the criminals is despaired"). [Translator's note: so vocalised in the printed text; on the author's explanation the passive يُبْلَسُ with nominative إِبْلَاسُ is evidently intended.]

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ (١٧))
His saying (حِينَ تُمْسُونَ): the majority read it as a genitive construct (iḍāfa), and what governs it is «سُبْحَانَ».
It has also been read with tanwīn (nunation), on the basis that «تُمْسُونَ» is made a naʿt (adjective) of it, with the referential pronoun omitted, i.e. "in which you enter the evening" (تُمْسُونَ فِيهِ); like His saying, the Exalted: (وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لَا تَجْزِي).

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَعَشِيًّا وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ (١٨))
His saying (وَعَشِيًّا): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «حِينَ», and «وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ» is parenthetical (muʿtariḍ). And «فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْحَمْدُ.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَيُحْيِي بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (٢٤))
His saying (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ): there are three views on it. First: that (مِنْ آيَاتِهِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْبَرْقَ, i.e. "He shows you the lightning, it being among His signs"; except that the wāw ought properly to come here before the verb; but since the ḥāl was placed first and was part of what is conjoined, the wāw was put directly before it. What makes this acceptable is that the preposition and its genitive noun have the status of an adverb (ẓarf); so it is like His saying: (آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً. .).
The second view: that «أَنْ» is omitted, i.e. "and among His signs is that He shows you" (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ يُرِيَكُمْ); and when «أَنْ» is omitted in a case like this, it is permissible to put the verb in the indicative. The third: that the thing described (al-mawṣūf) is omitted, i.e. "and among His signs is a sign in which He shows you the lightning" (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ آيَةٌ يُرِيكُمْ فِيهَا الْبَرْقَ); so the thing described and the referential pronoun were omitted. It is also permissible for the implied form to be "and among His signs is something" (شَيْءٌ), or "clouds" (سَحَابٌ); and the fāʿil (agent) of يُرِيكُمْ would then be a pronoun referring to the omitted شَيْءٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ تَقُومَ السَّمَاءُ وَالْأَرْضُ بِأَمْرِهِ ثُمَّ إِذَا دَعَاكُمْ دَعْوَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ إِذَا أَنْتُمْ تَخْرُجُونَ (٢٥))
His saying (مِنَ الْأَرْضِ): there are two views on it.
First: it is a naʿt (adjective) of دَعْوَةً. Second: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "you came out from the earth" (خَرَجْتُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ), and what indicates the omitted element is «إِذَا أَنْتُمْ تَخْرُجُونَ». It is not permissible for «مِنْ» to be attached to this تَخْرُجُونَ, because what comes after إِذَا does not govern what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ وَلَهُ الْمَثَلُ الْأَعْلَى فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (٢٧))
His saying (وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ): i.e. the resurrection is easier for Him in your estimation.
It is also said: أَهْوَنُ means "easy" (هَيِّنٌ), just as they said اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ, i.e. "great" (كَبِيرٌ).
It is also said: it is easier for the created being; because at the beginning it was moved from a sperm-drop to a clinging clot and to other stages, whereas at the resurrection it is completed all at once.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ضَرَبَ لَكُمْ مَثَلًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ هَلْ لَكُمْ مِنْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ مِنْ شُرَكَاءَ فِي مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ فَأَنْتُمْ فِيهِ سَوَاءٌ تَخَافُونَهُمْ كَخِيفَتِكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ كَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (٢٨))
His saying (فَأَنْتُمْ فِيهِ سَوَاءٌ): the clause is in the position of the accusative as the answer to the interrogative, i.e. "do you have …, so that you would be equal?" (هَلْ لَكُمْ فَتَسْتَوُوا).
As for (تَخَافُونَهُمْ): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent pronoun in «سَوَاءٌ», i.e. "so that you would be equal, each of you fearing the other's partnership with him in wealth"; i.e. if your slaves do not share with you in wealth, how can you associate in the worship of Allah one who is made by Allah?
(كَخِيفَتِكُمْ): i.e. a fear like your fear (خِيفَةً كَخِيفَتِكُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:30-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا فِطْرَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ ذَلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٣٠) مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ (٣١))
His saying (فِطْرَةَ اللَّهِ): i.e. "adhere to" or "follow" the religion of Allah (الْزَمُوا / اتَّبِعُوا).
And (مُنِيبِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the omitted verb.
It is also said: it is a ḥāl of the agent pronoun in «أَقِمْ», because in meaning it is addressed to all.
It is also said: «فِطْرَةَ اللَّهِ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He created you with a creating" (فَطَرَكُمْ فِطْرَةً).

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مِنَ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُوا شِيَعًا كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ (٣٢))
His saying (مِنَ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا): it is a badal (substitute) of الْمُشْرِكِينَ, with the preposition repeated.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (٣٤))
His saying (لِيَكْفُرُوا): the lām has the meaning of كَيْ ("so that").
It is also said: it is an imperative with the meaning of threat, as He said after it: «فَتَمَتَّعُوا».

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَانًا فَهُوَ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِمَا كَانُوا بِهِ يُشْرِكُونَ (٣٥))
السُّلْطَانُ is treated as masculine because it has the meaning of "proof" (الدَّلِيل), and as feminine because it has the meaning of "argument" (الْحُجَّة).
It is also said: it is the plural of سَلِيطٌ, like رَغِيفٌ and رُغْفَانٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا أَذَقْنَا النَّاسَ رَحْمَةً فَرِحُوا بِهَا وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذَا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ (٣٦))
His saying (إِذَا هُمْ): إِذَا is the locative إِذَا of surprise (al-mufājaʾa); it has taken the place of the fāʾ in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because surprise implies immediate sequence; and it does not come at the beginning of speech, just as the fāʾ does not. In some places the fāʾ has entered upon it as redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا آتَيْتُمْ مِنْ رِبًا لِيَرْبُوَ فِي أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ فَلَا يَرْبُو عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَمَا آتَيْتُمْ مِنْ زَكَاةٍ تُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ اللَّهِ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُضْعِفُونَ (٣٩))
His saying (وَمَا آتَيْتُمْ): «مَا» is in the position of the accusative, governed by آتَيْتُمْ. With the long vowel (آتَيْتُمْ) it means "you gave", and with the short vowel (أَتَيْتُمْ) it means "you came with" and "you intended".
His saying (لِيَرْبُوَ): i.e. the usury (الرِّبَا).
(فَأُولَئِكَ): this is a turn from the second person (address) to the third person (absence).

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ظَهَرَ الْفَسَادُ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي عَمِلُوا لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ (٤١))
His saying (لِيُذِيقَهُمْ): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to ظَهَرَ, i.e. so that their state ends up in that. It is also said: the implied form is "He punished them so as to make them taste" (عَاقَبَهُمْ لِيُذِيقَهُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ رُسُلًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِمْ فَجَاءُوهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَانْتَقَمْنَا مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا وَكَانَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنَا نَصْرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (٤٧))
His saying (وَكَانَ حَقًّا): «حَقًّا» is the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ placed first, and «نَصْرُ» is its noun (ism).
It is also permissible for «حَقًّا» to be a maṣdar (verbal noun), and «عَلَيْنَا» the khabar.
It is also permissible for there to be a pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) in «كَانَ», with «حَقًّا» a maṣdar, and «عَلَيْنَا نَصْرُ» a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the khabar of كَانَ.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ الَّذِي يُرْسِلُ الرِّيَاحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابًا فَيَبْسُطُهُ فِي السَّمَاءِ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ وَيَجْعَلُهُ كِسَفًا فَتَرَى الْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلَالِهِ فَإِذَا أَصَابَ بِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ إِذَا هُمْ يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ (٤٨))
His saying (كِسَفًا): with fatḥa on the sīn, on the basis that it is the plural of كِسْفَةٌ ("piece"); and with sukūn on it, with this same meaning, it is a lightening. It is also permissible for it to be a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "possessing pieces" (ذَا كِسَفٍ).
The hāʾ in «خِلَالِهِ» refers to the clouds; it is also said: to the pieces (الْكِسَف).

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ كَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ (٤٩))
His saying (مِنْ قَبْلِهِ): it is said: it is a repetition of the first قَبْل; but it is better for the hāʾ in it to refer to the clouds, or to the wind, or to the pieces (الْكِسَف). The meaning is: "even though they were, before the rain came down, [i.e.] before the clouds or the wind …"; so «مِنْ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُنَزِّلَ [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse has the passive يُنَزَّلَ].

ukberi-tibyan:50-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَانْظُرْ إِلَى آثَارِ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْيِي الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٥٠) وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنَا رِيحًا فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا لَظَلُّوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ يَكْفُرُونَ (٥١))
His saying (إِلَى آثَارِ): it is read in the singular (أَثَرِ) and in the plural.
And (يُحْيِي) with yāʾ, on the basis that the fāʿil (agent) is Allah, or the trace (الْأَثَر), or the notion of mercy.
And with tāʾ (تُحْيِي), on the basis that the fāʿil is آثَارُ, or الرَّحْمَةُ.
The hāʾ in «رَأَوْهُ» refers to the crops (الزَّرْع); what indicates them is «يُحْيِي الْأَرْضَ». It is also said: to the wind. It is also said: to the clouds.
(لَظَلُّوا): i.e. "they will surely remain" (لَيَظَلُّنَّ), because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and likewise أَرْسَلْنَا has the meaning of "We send" (نُرْسِلُ).

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ ضَعْفٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةً ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ ضَعْفًا وَشَيْبَةً يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْقَدِيرُ (٥٤))
And الضَّعْفُ: with fatḥa and with ḍamma on the ḍād, two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يَنْفَعُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مَعْذِرَتُهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ (٥٧))
His saying (لَا يَنْفَعُ): with tāʾ (لَا تَنْفَعُ) according to the wording [of مَعْذِرَة, which is feminine], and with yāʾ according to the meaning of "excuse" (الْعُذْر); or because something separates the two, or because it is not a real feminine. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:2-5.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ (٢) فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ (٣) فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ (٤) بِنَصْرِ اللَّهِ يَنْصُرُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ): the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object.
(فِي بِضْعِ): attached to (mutaʿalliq) يَغْلِبُونَ.
(مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ): both are indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the well-known [reading], because they are cut off from the genitive construct. It has been read, as an irregular reading (shādhdh), with kasra on both, on the basis that the muḍāf ilayhi is intended, as al-Farazdaq said:
يَا مَنْ رَأَى عَارِضًا يُسَرُّ بِهِ ... بَيْنَ ذِرَاعَيْ وَجَبْهَةِ الْأَسَدِ
(O you who have seen a rain-cloud one rejoices at, between the Forearms and the Forehead of the Lion [i.e. the lunar mansions].) Except that it is more plausible in the verse, because mentioning the muḍāf ilayhi with one of the two indicates the other.
It is also read in the genitive with tanwīn [مِنْ قَبْلٍ وَمِنْ بَعْدٍ], their inflection being like their inflection when in genitive construct; the implied form is "before everything and after everything." (وَيَوْمَئِذٍ): accusative by «يَفْرَحُ».
(بِنَصْرِ اللَّهِ): attached to it as well; and it may be attached to «يَنْصُرُ».

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَعْدَ اللَّهِ لَا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَعْدَ اللَّهِ): it is an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "Allah has promised a promise"; what precedes indicates the omitted verb, because it is a promise.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكَافِرُونَ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ): «مَا» is negative, and concerning the construal there are two views.
The first: it is a new sentence (mustaʾnaf) with no [grammatical] position, the speech being complete before it; and «أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا» is like (أَوَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا فِي مَلَكُوتِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ). The second: its position is accusative by يَتَفَكَّرُوا, and the negation does not prevent that, just as it did not prevent it in His saying, Exalted is He: (وَظَنُّوا مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ). (بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّهِمْ): attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كَافِرُونَ», and the lām does not prevent that. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَانُوا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً وَأَثَارُوا الْأَرْضَ وَعَمَرُوهَا أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا عَمَرُوهَا وَجَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلَكِنْ كَانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ (٩)).
